papers.title: Deintercalation Equilibria Control the Composition, Structure, and Electronic Quality in the Synthesis of 2$M$-WS$_2$
papers.summary: Alkali-metal intercalation-deintercalation (AMID) enables access to metastable layered materials such as 2$M$-WS$_2$. Mechanistic studies of AMID have focused on intercalation; how deintercalation proceeds and influences crystal properties is comparatively poorly understood. Here, we assess 34 deintercalation treatments of 2$M$-K$_x$WS$_2$ and find that K$^+$ removal proceeds through coupled redox and ion-exchange equilibria, whose positions set the composition, structure, and electronic quality of the products. Across a series of neat solvents, K$^+$ deintercalation amount increased with solvent polarity and was driven to near-completion upon addition of nonoxidizing crown ether chelators, regardless of solvent polarity. Spontaneous reintercalation occurred when 2$M$-WS$_2$ was placed in dilute aqueous solutions of the strong base KOH but not the neutral salt KCl. These results suggest that the extent of deintercalation is governed by the stability of K$^+$ in solution, rather than oxidant strength alone, consistent with a reaction under thermodynamic control. Treatments that bias the deintercalation equilibrium most strongly toward the products while avoiding deleterious side reactions produce the highest quality 2$M$-WS$_2$. A six-hour treatment with acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ gave the highest average residual resistivity ratio ($\overline{RRR}$). Residual K$^+$, quantified by ICP-MS, was found in all treated samples and appeared to impose an upper bound on $\overline{RRR}$. Treatments yielding crystals with $\overline{RRR}$ below this bound did not always afford 2$M$-WS$_2$; we observed two new structures in bleach-treated samples and signatures of alternative phases under other conditions. This work demonstrates that deintercalation is not merely a processing step in AMID but a mechanistically rich reaction that might be rationally tuned to improve and control metastable materials.

papers.title: Coordination Geometry Reconstruction Mitigates α‑Dihedral Angle Restriction of Polyanionic‐Type Cathodes for Ultrafast Sodium Storage
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries have attracted extensive attention for large‑scale energy storage owing to the abundance and low cost of sodium resources. However, the near‑coplanar structure geometry of polyanionic‐type cathodes causes in‑plane stress and electrostatic barriers, which lead to blocked Na + transport kinetics and hinder their practical application. Herein, an α‑plane, defined by the transition metal and its coordinating dangling anions, is identified as the critical structural bottleneck for Na + diffusion. By screening and tuning the dangling anions, a coordination geometry reconstruction is achieved that twists the α‑plane into α1‐ and α2‐planes. This twisting behavior breaks α‑plane restriction and relieves the in‑plane stress, thereby lowering the Na + migration barrier. Concurrently, the geometry reconstruction enlarges the Na2‑centered polyhedral volume and increases the Na2 site occupancy from 0.56 to 0.62. Thus, the modified cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 130 mAh g −1 and outstanding rate capability, with 80% retention at 30 C and 83 mAh g −1 at 50 C. It also exhibits excellent wide‐temperature operability (−40°C to 55°C) and stable full‑cell performance. The universality of this strategy is validated on several polyanionic cathodes. This work reveals the α‑plane as a tunable structural parameter, offering a geometry‑electronic synergy paradigm for high‑power polyanionic‐type cathodes.

papers.title: Anchoring LiZn Nanocrystals With Oligomer Binders for Enhanced Interfacial Stability in Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer‐anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray‐coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 coin cell with the composite interphase exhibits a lifespan of 700 cycles at 1 C with a high cathode loading of 3.06 mAh cm −2 . The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.

papers.title: Advances in Graphite-Based Dual-Ion Batteries toward Sustainable Energy Applications
papers.summary: The review examines graphite-based dual-ion batteries extensively, covering the basic working principles of this battery technology, the chemistry of anion and cation intercalation into graphite, charge carriers and electrolytes, and the current limitations and improvement strategies for their progress. We begin by reviewing the fundamental intercalation chemistry that has guided decades of research and clarify the different working mechanisms of dual-ion batteries compared with conventional LIBs. The main focus is on the chemistry of graphite intercalation and a detailed analysis of the mechanisms of anionic and cationic charge storage in graphite electrodes. The electrolyte compositions are particularly emphasised, as regards their critical role in the performance of the battery. Then the review systematically summarises the current limitations and corresponding optimisation strategies, including the design of electrode materials, the interphase stabilisation strategies and advanced electrolyte engineering. Finally, we discuss key challenges and suggest potential future research directions to improve high-performance DIB systems for practical energy storage applications. This work will be of interest and practical use to researchers engaged in the development of next generation batteries.

papers.title: Anion Engineering Enables Concurrent Optimization of Phonon and Carrier Transport in AMg$_2$X$_2$ Zintl Thermoelectrics
papers.summary: The simultaneous suppression of lattice heat transport and enhancement of carrier transport is central to the development of high-performance thermoelectric materials. Here, we investigate the microscopic mechanisms governing phonon and carrier transport in CaAl$_2$Si$_2$-type AMg$_2$X$_2$ (A = Ca, Sr, Ba; X = P, As, Sb, Bi) Zintl compounds using first-principles calculations, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and Boltzmann transport theory. As X changes from P to Bi, the widening phonon band gap restricts three-phonon scattering channels and increases the relative importance of four-phonon processes. In CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ and BaMg$_2$Bi$_2$, four-phonon scattering dominates the relaxation of low-frequency heat-carrying modes at 900 K. The Bi-based series also exhibits an anomalous increase in lattice thermal conductivity from Ca to Ba despite the increasing cation mass. Mode-resolved analysis links the lower thermal conductivity of CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ to reduced low-frequency group velocities and stronger anharmonic scattering, with Ca-related mid-frequency vibrations providing additional four-phonon scattering channels. Including both particle-like and coherent contributions, its lattice thermal conductivity reaches 0.23 W$\cdot$m$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$ at 900 K. Meanwhile, the increasing covalent character of the vertical Mg-X bonds is accompanied by enhanced band-edge dispersion and reduced carrier effective masses. These electronic changes, together with conduction-band convergence, favor n-type transport and yield a predicted peak $ZT$ of 3.68 at 900 K in CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$. These results elucidate the interplay of phonon spectral structure and higher-order anharmonicity in thermal transport, alongside the distinct electronic response to anion substitution.

papers.title: Intercalation of O2, H2, and CO beneath epitaxial graphene on Ir(111): A review of atomic-scale decoupling mechanisms and pathways to catalysis, sensing, and energy applications
papers.summary: Intercalation of gases and metal species beneath graphene supported on transition-metal substrates has emerged as a powerful strategy for tuning graphene–substrate interactions and tailoring its electronic, chemical, and mechanical properties. Numerous studies have investigated these phenomena using surface-sensitive techniques, including X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED). This review examines the intercalation of oxygen, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen, with particular emphasis on graphene grown on Ir(111). Oxygen intercalation proceeds under ultrahigh-vacuum conditions through atomic oxygen formation on bare Ir terraces and requires elevated temperatures (~355 K), whereas hydrogen intercalation occurs at much lower temperatures (~140 K). CO intercalation takes place near room temperature but requires millibar-range pressures. In all cases, substrate step edges and graphene flake boundaries serve as critical pathways for intercalant penetration. These structural features have been consistently identified as key entry points for intercalant diffusion. Intercalation provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling the properties of 2D materials, enabling modulation of electrical conductivity, thermoelectric response, and catalytic activity. The process significantly modifies the electronic, chemical, and mechanical characteristics of the graphene layer, while also partially decoupling it from the underlying substrate. Given these effects, gas intercalation beneath graphene represents a promising strategy for applications in catalysis, sensing, and energy storage. Intercalation can also be used to partially separate the graphene overlayer from the underlying metal, leading to considerable enhancement of electronic, chemical and mechanical properties. This review highlights the fundamental mechanisms and technological potential of gas (O 2 , H 2 , and CO) intercalation beneath graphene for applications in catalysis, sensing, energy storage, and next-generation graphene-based devices.

papers.title: Controlling Structure and Stability in Ultrathin Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene Multilayers for Hydrogen Gas Barrier Applications
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene is a promising 2D nanofiller for gas barrier composites. However, controlling the composite's nanoscale structure and ensuring its stability in harsh thermal environments remain significant challenges. This study compares the multilayer properties, morphology, and hydrogen (H 2 ) gas barrier performance of two different MXene‐based layer‐by‐layer (LbL) assemblies, demonstrating the influence of polymer content and complementary positively charged assembling species. LbL assembly effectively promotes brick‐and‐mortar‐like multilayer ordering of MXene in nanoscale thin films, but the method requires positively charged species to electrostatically assemble with negatively charged MXene. Using either reduced graphene oxide (rGO) precomplexed with a polycation (rGO‐PDDA) or positively charged MXene (f‐MXene) functionalized with [3‐(2‐aminoethylamino)‐propyl] trimethoxysilane (AEAPTMS) as the complementary species, the two MXene‐based multilayers show strikingly different behaviors at elevated temperatures. Structural and chemical characterization shows that only the rGO‐PDDA/MXene multilayer maintains electrostatic bonding, leading to improved stability and performance in harsh conditions. In films as thin as 43 nm, the LbL multilayers retain their performance. The rGO‐PDDA/MXene multilayer exhibits low H 2 gas permeability (7.13 ± 0.09 × 10 −11 m 3 ·m·m −2 ·atm −1 ·day −1 ) even at 400°C. This study offers insightful guidelines for the rational design of MXene‐ or polymer‐based composite films for gas barrier applications in extreme temperatures.

papers.title: Out-of-plane interference effects in the angle-resolved photoemission of epitaxial graphene
papers.summary: The epitaxial growth of monolayer graphene by Si sublimation of 6H-SiC(0001) is one of the most effective ways of producing large-scale monocrystalline graphene samples of high quality. However, graphene is left interacting with a reconstructed carbon buffer layer known as zerolayer graphene (ZLG) and the SiC substrate underneath. Beyond the mere creation of Dirac cone replicas, the effect of this interaction on photoemission measurements is poorly understood. We utilized synchrotron radiation for photon-energy-dependent angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to investigate the complex final-state interactions of photoelectrons within the heterostructure of monolayer graphene, ZLG, and SiC. We identify multiple resonances in the photoemission intensity of the Dirac cone as a function of photon energy that originate from interlayer interference, confirmed with a multiple scattering model. We also demonstrate for the first time that the relative intensity of the replica bands induced by the $(6\sqrt{3} \times 6\sqrt{3})\text{R}30^\circ$ reconstruction scales with the electron kinetic energy. Finally, we resolved four nondispersing electronic states, which originate from the ZLG. Our findings show that the three-dimensional (3D) structure of SiC and ZLG manifests itself in the photoemission from two-dimensional (2D) epitaxial graphene. By revealing how 3D substrate architecture dictates the photoemission of a 2D layer, this work establishes a crucial framework for investigating the electronic structure of complex heterostructures via ARPES.

papers.title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
papers.summary: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal that pre-existing S vacancies lower the Cr Frenkel-pair migration barrier by up to 1.1 eV, providing an atomistic mechanism for beam-induced Cr redistribution and structural transformations. Displacement threshold calculations further show that Br is the most susceptible species to electron-beam-induced displacement, identifying the relative ease of removing different atomic species. Together, these results establish a validated computational framework for investigating atomic-scale disorder and structural transformations in CrSBr, providing a basis for defect engineering in materials for future magneto-optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Mimicry of $\textit{d}$-wave Andreev Signatures by Interlayer Pairing
papers.summary: The recent discovery of high-$T_{\rm c}$ superconductivity in bilayer nickelates has attracted enormous attention. Despite dominant theoretical studies pointing to interlayer pairing, the pairing symmetry is strongly debated due to conflicting evidence on nodeless bulk gaps and $d$-wave-like transport signatures. Here, we demonstrate that a nodeless interlayer pairing can naturally mimic $d$-wave Andreev signatures when the point contact is not evenly coupled to the two layers. The phenomenon can be understood by recognizing how a contact potential, which is odd under the layer-exchanging mirror symmetry, acts like an effective Zeeman field on the layer pseudospin. This pseudo field then binds in-gap Andreev states that sweep through the gap with the width and strength of the barrier. We further demonstrate in a realistic model for La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ that the simulated subgap conductance for a top-layer barrier can reproduce the orientation dependent ZBCP usually interpreted as a fingerprint of $\textit{d}$-wave pairing. By revealing this mirror-selective Andreev response from an interlayer pairing state, our work offers a natural scenario to reconcile the conflicting experimental evidence in bilayer nickelates and advances our understanding of unconventional superconductivity.

papers.title: Quotient Index for Symmetry-Protected Zeros and the Tenfold Way in Mackey's Construction of Super Corepresentations
papers.summary: Symmetries that anticommute with a Hamiltonian can protect zero modes by obstructing their removal through symmetry-compatible perturbations. We formulate this obstruction as a quotient of the additive group of symmetry representations by the image of the map that forgets a compatible representation grading. To compute the quotient, we use Mackey's method to construct all irreducible super corepresentations of finite graded symmetry groups, allowing antiunitary operations and projective factor systems. Starting from the unitary Hamiltonian-preserving normal subgroup, this construction yields two complex and ten real structural types, characterized by residual Altland--Zirnbauer symmetry algebras. The residual and induced graded modules have isomorphic graded commutants, and their represented symmetry algebras share a graded Morita class that is super opposite to that of the commutant. We derive character criteria that identify these types. Exhaustive enumeration of the restriction relations gives independent sector contributions $0$, $Z$, or $Z_2$, with only integer factors in the purely unitary case. In the finite semisimple setting, the complete index vanishes if and only if all zero modes can be lifted by a symmetry-compatible perturbation. Applications to one-dimensional end states and interpolation cylinders of disordered boundary Dirac theories recover protected multiplet counts and connect the quotient to bulk topology and sigma-model topological terms using bulk--boundary correspondence, texture-index theorems, and fermion-phase calculations.

papers.title: Impact of multi-dot configurations on electron temperature and double quantum dot latching in gate-controlled qubit devices
papers.summary: Many currently envisaged scalable architectures for Si/SiGe spin qubit devices utilize gate-controlled multi-dot configurations characterized by their peculiar Coulomb blockade physics. One example is the concurrent use of a single electron transistor (SET) as a charge sensor and as a reservoir for adjacent qubit quantum dots (QD). We find that the SET energy spectrum impacts pulsed gate spectroscopy of the QD when the SET simultaneously acts as the reservoir and the sensor. Then, using the qubit QD as a probe, we quantify how strongly the electron temperature of the SET depends on the applied bias. It surpasses a reference experiment by 100 $mK$ even at 50 $μV$ bias. Our results provide a strong incentive for choosing spin qubit initialization schemes which do not rely on coupling to the reservoir in such devices. Switching to a double quantum dot connected to a single reservoir, a frequent configuration for qubit readout, we finally demonstrate the tunability of the characteristic latching behavior by systematically mapping it in the few-electron stability diagram.

papers.title: Industrial RPCVD growth of high-purity 28Si epilayers with 29Si content below 30 ppm for high-fidelity electron spin qubits
papers.summary: Silicon quantum-dot spin qubits are among the most promising routes to large-scale quantum computation, but the residual 29Si nuclear spins in natural silicon impose a hyperfine dephasing limit that must be overcome by isotopic purification. Here, we report the epitaxial growth of high-purity 28Si on float-zone silicon using an industrial reduced-pressure chemical vapor deposition (RPCVD) system. Secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) confirms an 28Si isotopic purity of 99.997%, with the 29Si concentration below 30 ppm. Through a systematic vacuum annealing matrix (850-1150 C), combined with atomic force microscopy and SIMS, we investigate the defect-mediated decomposition of the native oxide and the injection of non-equilibrium vacancies. We identify a thermal-budget window below 950 C within which the thin-layer structure of 28Si remains intact. At 1.5 K, magnetotransport measurements reveal a peak Hall mobility of 12,858 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and a quantum scattering lifetime of 0.659 ps, corresponding to a single-particle level broadening of 499 micro-eV. A double quantum dot fabricated on this platform exhibits a T2* of 0.62 us, a Hahn-echo coherence time of 28.8 us, and single-qubit gate fidelities of up to 99.9% measured by randomized benchmarking. Our results establish industrial RPCVD as a promising route toward high-coherence, high-fidelity silicon spin qubits.

papers.title: Probing Exotic Electron-Electron Interactions via Adiabatic Spin Inversion in MRFM
papers.summary: Light bosons beyond the Standard Model can mediate exotic spin-dependent interactions between electrons, motivating sensitive searches at short distances. We propose a magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM) scheme that exploits oscillating-cantilever-driven adiabatic reversals (OSCAR) of electron spins to convert these interactions into measurable mechanical signals. The ferromagnetic tip serves as both a dense polarized-spin source and a source of magnetic-field gradients, enabling force detection without magnetic shielding between the source and sensor. Within a linearized treatment of the coupled spin-mechanical dynamics, we derive resonance-frequency shifts associated with the $V_2$ and $V_3$ interactions and a second-harmonic force signal arising from the velocity-dependent $V_8$ interaction. We further investigate interrupted-OSCAR differential detection and distance-dependent measurements to discriminate exotic signals from conventional magnetic backgrounds. Using representative parameters from ensemble and single-spin MRFM experiments, we estimate the projected sensitivity under specified noise and statistical assumptions. The results suggest that the proposed scheme could provide complementary sensitivity to short-range spin-dependent interactions, with the potential to improve existing constraints on $V_2$ over selected submicrometer interaction ranges. Our study establishes adiabatic spin-inversion MRFM as a promising approach to probing exotic electron-electron forces.

papers.title: Lifting mechanical zero modes without dispersion
papers.summary: Floppy frameworks carry flat bands of zero-frequency mechanisms with no finite-frequency resonance, and couplings that lift them usually spread them. We show that an on-site tensor lifts a mechanism band without first-order dispersion exactly when, projected onto the mechanisms, it acts as wavevector-independent scalars on orthogonal pieces. Three structures achieve this: local normal modes, invariant symmetry sectors, and a balance law. A mechanism moves both ends of every bond between two vertex classes equally along it, and where the inter-class bond tensors are class scalars this balance law fixes its norm shares and hence the flat value from geometry alone. For the fluorite net the band lies outside the tensor spectrum, at 14/9 of the contact stiffness to first order, and stays flat to all orders in a fixed cage. A placement inside a tiling dual that keeps the common symmetry supplies such tensors, because each contact star inherits its site symmetry. Ten catalogued dual pairs lift flat; half are eigenvalue cases a resolved count matches, and the balance law explains flat bands in random cages too. Duality makes the rigid cage common. In a printable beam-frame lattice, contacts that lock joint rotation remove first-order bending dispersion whenever bonded mechanisms are orthogonal local normals.

papers.title: Hidden Coherence and Controlled Quasihole Motion in a Fermionic Laughlin State on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
papers.summary: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states support fractionalized excitations and geometric phases, yet experimentally resolving the many-body coherence encoded in their wave functions remains challenging. Here, we prepare a three-electron $ν=1/3$ Laughlin state on the Haldane sphere using seven superconducting qubits and reconstruct its many-body density matrix. Through Read's composite-boson construction, we reveal vortex-dressed coherence that remains appreciable over a larger separation range than electron coherence. The extended profile is suppressed in a Fock-diagonal reference constructed from the measured populations, demonstrating its dependence on off-diagonal many-body coherence. We further prepare a one-flux-added quasihole and characterize its fractional charge response against finite-size benchmarks. Controlled quasihole motion yields an effective geometric-phase signature from the reconstructed dominant-eigenstate trajectory. These complementary measurements provide microscopic access to the coherent structure and quasihole response of a finite fermionic Laughlin state, demonstrating an experimental route to probing strongly correlated FQH wave functions on programmable quantum processors.

papers.title: Interplay of Ni Order and Local Moments in Intercalated NixNbS2
papers.summary: Magnetic ions intercalated into the van der Waals gaps of layered transition metal dichalcogenides provide a system where local moments interact strongly with a metallic host. How the order of the intercalant sublattice affects their magnetism is important but rarely addressed, although disorder is hard to avoid, in particular in thin films and heterostructures. Here this question is examined in single crystals of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ with $0.10 \leq x \leq 0.57$, whose composition and Ni order were determined by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy and synchrotron x-ray diffraction. Anisotropic magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal three regimes. Long-range antiferromagnetic order appears only for $0.25 \leq x \leq 0.33$, where the Ni ions form the $2 \times 2$ and $\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}$ R$30^\circ$ superstructures, and $T_\mathrm{N}$ reaches 96 K at $x = 1/3$. In this range the effective moment, $\approx 2.5 μ_\mathrm{B}$ per Ni, agrees with DFT+$U$ calculations, in which the Ni spin is partly delocalized onto the surrounding S ligands. For $x \leq 0.18$ the dilute, randomly distributed Ni ions remain paramagnetic down to 2 K with a reduced moment. For $x \geq 0.37$, where Ni-Ni contacts are unavoidable, long-range order gives way to a short-range ordered state below 10-15 K with a further reduced moment. As calculations for ordered Ni arrangements find the Ni state nearly independent of $x$, even at $x = 1/2$, the reduction of the moment is attributed to a disorder-enabled reduction of the charge transfer from Ni to the NbS$_2$ layers. The magnetism of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ is thus governed by the (dis)order of the Ni sublattice rather than by the Ni concentration alone.

papers.title: Scaling-up electrochromic windows from the lab to buildings and grid integration
papers.summary: Electrochromic (EC) windows can regulate solar heat and daylight, yet laboratory performance alone does not determine their value in buildings. This Review traces electrochromic technology from materials and device architectures through scale-up and commercialization to building operation and grid interaction. It examines how useful function is filtered by large-area uniformity, durability, sealing reliability, manufacturing yield, cost, and control. These constraints explain why mature products still favor conservative inorganic solid-state platforms despite rapid advances in dual-band and multiband devices. The analysis further shows that optical states should be defined by application needs before materials and devices are optimized to deliver them, linking spectral design to comfort, energy, and flexibility objectives. Because most reported grid-responsive benefits remain simulation-based, future studies must separate projected potential from field-verified performance. Progress therefore requires application-driven design, scalable qualification, and real-world validation that preserve useful function from material discovery to reliable building operation and verifiable grid services. This Review discusses electrochromic technology from materials and device architectures, scale-up and commercialization, to building operation and grid interaction. It also examines how useful function is enabled by large-area uniformity, durability, sealing reliability, manufacturing yield, cost, and control.

papers.title: Lithium in North American Produced Waters: Geological Controls, Direct Extraction Mechanisms, and the Gap Between Synthetic and Real-Brine Evidence
papers.summary: Global lithium demand has increased rapidly, driven largely by expanding battery production, with consumption estimated at 263, 263,000 t in 2025. Supply remains concentrated among a limited number of hard- rock and salar producers. Oilfield- produced water in North America has emerged as a potential additional lithium source, particularly because oil and gas production already generates large volumes of this waste stream.
papers.primary_category: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

papers.title: Tuning solvent–salt interactions in ionic liquid–organic blends for enhanced supercapacitor performance
papers.summary: Advanced supercapacitors require electrolytes that extend the electrochemical stability window while preserving fast ion transport. Here, we investigate hybrid electrolytes based on mixtures of an ammonium-based ionic liquid (IL), N-butyl- N -trimethylammonium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([N 1114 ][NTf 2 ]), and 1.0 M TEABF 4 in propylene carbonate, with IL contents ranging from 10 to 90 vol%. A comprehensive electrochemical and operando spectroscopic approach was employed to elucidate the interplay between ion–solvent interactions, nanostructuring, and charge storage mechanisms. Our results demonstrate that IL incorporation induces the formation of nanosegregated domains and voltage-dependent interfacial structures that regulate ion mobility and the organization of the electric double layer. At low IL content, the system achieved an extended voltage of 3.4 V, enhanced capacitance, and reduced internal resistance, attributed to improved dielectric environment and efficient pore accessibility. In contrast, higher IL fractions promote strong ion–ion correlations, limiting ion transport, despite improved electrochemical stability and safety. Operando spectroscopy reveals the formation of a dynamic, protective interfacial layer derived from preferential IL decomposition, which stabilizes the electrode–electrolyte interface and suppresses solvent degradation at high voltages. Overall, this work provides a rational design strategy for hybrid electrolytes, highlighting their potential to enable safer and high-performance supercapacitors for advanced energy storage applications. By validating performance in both coin and pouch cells, we demonstrate that the improved interfacial behavior and expanded voltage window are maintained in a practical device format, bridging fundamental electrochemical insights with scalable implementation for compact, high-voltage applications that require fast charge/discharge and long cycle life.

papers.title: Ionic Liquid Regulated Wetting and Chemo‐Mechanical Stabilization of NCM811 Cathodes
papers.summary: (NCM811) cathodes due to non-selective interfacial adhesion, causing severe structural pulverization, interfacial debonding, and unstable cathode electrolyte interfacial (CEI) growth during cycling. Herein, we reveal the cation-dependent interfacial affinity of ionic liquids. An imidazolium-based ionic liquid (EMIM[TFSI]) preferentially wets and encapsulates NCM811 particles, forming a robust interfacial layer with superior elastic modulus (3.4 GPa vs. PVDF 0.49 GPa) and lower dissipation (0.15 vs. PVDF 0.27 keV), whereas pyrrolidinium- and piperidinium-based ILs predominantly plasticized the PVDF-rich phase. The conformal EMIM[TFSI] wetting buffers lattice strain efficiently, suppresses transition-metal dissolution, and induces the formation of thin, uniform, and robust CEI. Benefiting from the integrated chemo-mechanical stabilization, the EMIM[TFSI] modified NCM811 cathode delivers 83% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1 C, and 0.1 Ah pouch cells achieve 84% retention at 0.5 C. This study establishes that ionic liquid binders offer a rational chemo-mechanical engineering strategy for high-performance NCM811 cathodes.

papers.title: Non-trivial topological spin-polarized surface states induced nonreciprocal transport in the hourglass semimetal
papers.summary: Quantum materials such as topological semimetals have gained consummate interest due to their exotic band crossings and protected surface states. In particular, Ta$_3$GeTe$_6$ has emerged as a prototypical hourglass Dirac semimetal, as confirmed by both experimental and theoretical analysis. The ARPES confirms the topological hourglass-type band dispersions and Rashba-type band, while Hall measurements reveal a high hole carrier concentration and nonreciprocal transport behavior. These findings are further supported by a phenomenological toy model, which predicts a nonreciprocal resistance, consistent with the observed direction-dependent magnetoresistance. Furthermore, the Raman spectroscopy uncovers two-fold and four-fold phonon symmetries drag of highly anisotropic phonons, which establishes symmetry-dependent resistance. DFT calculations reveal Dirac-like and hourglass Dirac band crossings near the Fermi level for the bulk, with Rashba-type spin splitting induced by the surface inversion-symmetry breaking, leading to spin-polarized surface states. The combined experimental and theoretical results demonstrate that Ta$_3$GeTe$_6$ hosts a non-trivial electronic topology, with the inversion-symmetry breaking at the surface as the driver of this nonreciprocal transport behavior.

papers.title: Experimental realization of twofold topological phase transition induced by long-range hoppings in one-dimensional chains
papers.summary: Long-range hoppings offer a powerful mechanism to engineer exotic topological phases beyond conventional tight-binding models. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a twofold topological phase transition driven by third-nearest-neighbor couplings in a one-dimensional phononic chain that emulates cis-polyacetylene. Tunable hopping parameters in highly structured aluminum plates allow us to observe the emergence of Dirac points, a valley pseudospin structure, and topological edge states. The experimental results are supported by non-equilibrium Green's function transport calculations. Our findings confirm the predicted long-range phase diagram and establish phononic metamaterials as a versatile platform for exploring topological phenomena beyond the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger paradigm.

papers.title: Heat Transport Mechanisms in MOF-5
papers.summary: We find that MOF-5 supports both long-lived phonons and linker vibrations whose split spectra signal a breakdown of the phonon quasiparticle approximation. Combining mode-projected molecular dynamics spectra with spectral Wigner heat transport, we resolve two contrasting transport channels: low-frequency particle-like phonon propagation decreases strongly from 200 to 500 K, whereas wave-like phonon coherence remains nearly constant and supplies about half the intrinsic conductivity at 500 K. A phenomenological extrinsic scattering model provides a plausible explanation for the discrepancy between calculated and measured conductivities in terms of both its magnitude and temperature dependence. We also identify signatures of phonon quasiparticle breakdown in the linker vibrations of ZIF-8 and HKUST-1, indicating that this feature extends to other metal-organic frameworks.

papers.title: Universal machine learning potentials for two-dimensional materials mechanics and phonons
papers.summary: Accurate modeling of phononic and mechanical properties in two-dimensional (2D) materials remains challenging because lattice vibrations are highly sensitive to computational details while mechanical deformation can involve complex nonlinear responses. Recent advances in universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) offer a promising route toward efficient atomistic simulations, but their reliability and application prospects across diverse 2D materials have not been systematically established. Herein, we perform extensive density functional theory (DFT) calculations and develop system-specific local machine learning interatomic potentials to establish a comprehensive benchmarking framework for evaluating the predictive performance of uMLIPs. Our results demonstrate that state-of-the-art uMLIPs, particularly the eSEN-30M-OAM model, can achieve remarkable accuracy and, in some cases, outperform customized passively-fitted local MLIPs trained for classes of materials. Although this level of accuracy is not universally guaranteed, these models reliably describe previously unseen 2D lattices, capturing key features of phonon dispersion relations and predicting complex mechanical responses across a diverse range of materials. Notably, for nanoporous and defective systems, where conventional DFT calculations become computationally expensive, uMLIPs retain high fidelity in describing both lattice dynamics and mechanical deformation. While challenges remain for large-scale finite-temperature molecular dynamics simulations and higher-order property predictions, our systematic benchmarking identifies robust strategies that balance accuracy and computational efficiency. Overall, this work highlights the strong potential of uMLIPs for predictive modeling and high-throughput screening of functional 2D materials, with promising extensions toward multilayer heterostructures, nanocomposites, and biologically integrated systems beyond the reach of conventional approaches.

papers.title: Coupling Plasma‐Synthesized N‐Doped Graphene With Ice Templated Porous Electrode for Enhanced Aluminum Battery Performance
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aluminum batteries are promising for next‐generation energy storage owing to the low cost and abundance of aluminum. Graphene is an attractive cathode due to its high surface area and electrical conductivity, but its performance is limited by difficult production and sheet aggregation, which restrict electrolyte accessibility and ion transport. This study employs a plasma‐enabled synthesis approach to produce both pristine graphene and nitrogen‐doped graphene (N‐graphene), followed by an ice templating strategy to directly construct a three‐dimensional porous N‐graphene electrode. The effects of nitrogen doping and porous electrode architecture are systematically investigated by comparing dense and porous electrodes. Nitrogen‐doping increases the specific capacity by ∼50%, from 36.24 to 54.4 mAh/g at a current density of 0.1 A/g. Furthermore, introducing porous structure provides an additional ∼20% improvement, achieving a capacity of 65.5 mAh/g under the same conditions. This enhanced performance of porous electrode is attributed to its interconnected pores and partially aligned graphene sheets, which improve electrolyte accessibility and facilitate the adsorption and transport of AlCl 4 − anions. The robust porous structure of N‐graphene ensures excellent cycling stability, with no noticeable capacity decay over 5000 cycles. Coupling nitrogen doping with porous electrode architecture provides an effective strategy to enhance graphene‐based aluminum batteries.

papers.title: Inversion symmetry breaking by interlayer hybridization in a tetralayer van der Waals heterostructure
papers.summary: Inversion symmetry breaking unlocks a broad range of physical phenomena fundamental for modern technologies, motivating efforts to engineer noncentrosymmetric materials. In this context, monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, which naturally lack inversion symmetry, have emerged as a versatile platform for valley physics, strong excitonic effects, and nonlinear optics. However, in their hexagonal stacking phase, inversion symmetry is restored in even-layer stacks and bulk form, suppressing these effects and limiting applications. In this work, inversion symmetry breaking is demonstrated in a vertically stacked tetralayer heterostructure assembled from two intrinsically centrosymmetric bilayer flakes, as evidenced by second harmonic generation measurements with an intensity comparable to that of their constituent monolayer. Spectroscopic measurements and theoretical estimations indicate that effective symmetry breaking in the tetralayer heterostructure is driven by interlayer hybridization, giving rise to pronounced electronic and phononic signatures. This symmetry breaking further induces polar anisotropy, with an intensity ratio reaching 2.36. We propose that asymmetric contributions from excitons to the second harmonic optical dipole may influence this behavior. These findings establish interlayer coupling as a critical mechanism for introducing inversion symmetry breaking and tuning the optical response of van der Waals heterostructures, providing a powerful strategy for photonics and optoelectronics in two-dimensional materials.

papers.title: Scanning Probe Control, Quantum Dynamics, and Dispersive Readout of Suspended Carbon Nanotube Resonators
papers.summary: Suspended carbon nanotubes (CNTs) offer promising opportunities for quantum nanomechanics owing to their small effective mass, strong electrostatic tunability, and mechanical nonlinearity. We develop a unified theoretical framework for coherent control and readout of a suspended CNT driven by an atomic force microscope (AFM) tip and capacitively coupled to a Cooper-pair box (CPB). We first derive the linear and nonlinear Duffing response of the CNT and quantify the effects of AFM force gradients, tip-position fluctuations, and voltage noise on mechanical stability, dephasing, and heating. These results establish operating conditions for coherent actuation with limited backaction. We then quantize the Duffing oscillator, derive its Kerr anharmonicity, and identify the requirements for selective control of individual vibrational transitions. Estimates of thermal occupation and active cooling illustrate the constraints for CNT modes spanning frequencies from 54 MHz to 5.37 GHz. Finally, we derive the CNT--CPB interaction and its dispersive limit, showing how phonon number and parity can be mapped onto the CPB through Ramsey interferometry and detected using quantum-capacitance readout. The resulting framework identifies the conditions under which localized AFM actuation, nonlinear quantum dynamics, and superconducting state-resolved detection can operate within a single CNT device.

papers.title: Stacking, symmetry and exciton fine structure in boron nitride bilayers
papers.summary: Engineering of two-dimensional material heterostructures offers a broad range of degrees of freedom through the selection of type and number of layers and their relative stacking configurations. In these compound materials, the stacking sequence plays a central role in determining electronic, mechanical, and optical properties. Here, we present a theoretical study of its signature on the excitons of hexagonal boron nitride bilayers based on first-principle calculations within the GW approximation and the Bethe-Salpeter equation. We explain how stacking-dependent symmetry variations lead to distinct electronic structures, particularly near the band edge around the K high-symmetry point, and consequently to markedly different excitonic landscapes. Indeed, we analyze the symmetry-governed character of the low-lying excitonic states, identifying their bright or dark nature for each stacking configuration and performing a systematic comparison. Our results clarify how van der Waals interlayer coupling reshapes excitons in hexagonal boron nitride bilayers and outline prospects for twist-controlled exciton engineering in this material.

papers.title: Physics Informed Priors for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials with Uncertainty Quantification
papers.summary: Standard uncertainty quantification methods for machine learning interatomic potentials often fail to quantify the effects of model misspecification despite its prominence as a source of error. To combat this, misspecification-aware uncertainty schemes have been gaining attention, pointwise optimal parameter set regression (POPS-Regression) among them. However, no guarantees on the physicality of the posterior distribution are given and uncertainty estimates can be conservative compared to the true error. To combat this, we present a model misspecification aware scheme that builds on POPS-Regression by allowing users to specify physical priors that are enforced across the obtained ensemble of models. This allows the user to incorporate misspecification-aware uncertainties without compromising on physical properties. The scheme is applicable to any physical quantity that can be represented by a convex set of parameters and so is robust for a wide variety of static properties which can help inform dynamical simulations. Here, we demonstrate the scheme for phononic vibrations and elastic properties. The scheme is also applied to both linear and message-passing neural network potentials by exploiting the linearity available in both architectures; for neural network potentials we approximate the readout layer as a linear model based on fixed non-linear features. The versatility of the method provides an alternative to hand-crafted or active learning approaches to data-set construction to correct physical failures by adding data thus reducing the computational overhead for designing potentials for specific applications.

papers.title: Momentum-space engineering in van der Waals heterostructures
papers.summary: Twenty years of graphene research have established Dirac fermions as a versatile platform for exploring quantum topological phenomena. Yet control over graphene's low-energy spectrum mostly follows the route of miniband engineering using real-space superlattices. Here we introduce a complementary approach based on momentum-space 'Umklapp' band engineering. This is realised by matching reciprocal space positions of band edges of two adjacent highly incommensurate 2D crystals to coincide upon a boost from their Bragg vectors, creating resonant interlayer hybridisation that qualitatively reconstructs their spectra. To demonstrate this approach experimentally, we use monolayer graphene on MoS$_2$, twisted such that MoS$_2$ Q-valley states are brought by Umklapp into energy-momentum resonance with graphene's Dirac cones. The ensuing hybridization results in the formation of a clear additional Dirac-like spectral feature, identified by a distinct Landau-level fan and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations characteristic to Berry phase $π$ electrons. These new topological spectral features create a spin-valley locked Ising system which is robust against small twist-angle variations that can be further tuned by an external displacement field. More broadly, Umklapp band engineering offers a practical strategy for tailoring the electronic structure in van der Waals heterostructures, expanding the design space of quantum materials beyond moiré superlattices and weak proximity effects.

papers.title: Symmetry-Gated Sliding: Decoupling Interlayer Translation from Polarization Reversal in Boron Nitride Ferroelectrics
papers.summary: Electric-field-driven polarization switching in sliding ferroelectrics depends on how local interlayer motion is accommodated by the surrounding structure. Yet the relationship between sliding, domain-wall (DW) propagation, and collective domain evolution under changing vector fields remains unclear. Here, we show that local symmetry governs the coupling between field-induced forces and interlayer sliding, while DW connectivity determines how local motion contributes to net domain conversion. These effects are examined across three structural scales, from monodomains and isolated DWs to reconstructed moire networks. We investigate bilayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) using molecular dynamics with a machine-learning interatomic potential that incorporates field-dependent electric enthalpy. An initially monodomain bilayer switches through directional wrinkling and interlayer sliding, while the barrier along a constrained flat path remains finite. Pre-existing DWs propagate with velocities governed by their shear and tensile character, and an additional in-plane field tunes wall velocity and width according to its orientation. In reconstructed triangular moire networks, shared junctions and boundary curvature mediate domain evolution and recovery after field removal or reversal. Most strikingly, a rotating in-plane field translates the layers and displaces the moiré nodes by approximately 1 AA yet leaves the AB/BA domain-area ratio without detectable change, because threefold connectivity cancels the contributions of individual walls. We term this response polarization-silent sliding. These results distinguish local sliding, DW translation, and net domain conversion as different responses to electric fields and establish how local structural symmetry and DW connectivity shape their selective control.

papers.title: Microscopic theory of exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides
papers.summary: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. Although this dressing fundamentally renormalizes the effective mass and mobility of carriers, its impact on electrically neutral exciton polarons in 2D semiconductors has received limited attention. In particular, despite the growing interest in polaronic effects in atomically thin semiconductors, only a few theoretical studies have addressed spectral signatures and renormalized properties of exciton polarons in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic model to describe exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides. Applying this model to $1s$ acoustic polarons in an MoSe$_2$ monolayer, we reveal a distinct kink in the polaron dispersion, accompanied by a pronounced broadening of its spectral function. These spectral signatures mark a critical transition from a regime of well-defined bound exciton polarons, characterized by a renormalized energy, reduced group velocity, and enhanced effective mass, to a regime dominated by exciton-phonon scattering. Furthermore, by incorporating intervalley exciton-phonon interaction, we demonstrate that the energetic position of momentum-dark excitons strongly modifies the exciton-polaron lifetime. Overall, our work provides a microscopic framework for determining renormalized properties of exciton polarons and establishes experimentally accessible polaron signatures in 2D semiconductors.

papers.title: High-Volume Wurtzite MnSe in MnSe/CdSe Superlattices: Structure, Magnetism and Optical Response
papers.summary: Polymorphism in Mn-based chalcogenides offers access to magnetic semiconductors with distinct crystal symmetries, polar structures, and different magnetic orders. In particular, wurtzite MnSe exhibits an appealing interplay of electric polarization and several competing magnetic phases including altermagnetic order. However, stabilizing metastable polymorphs, such as wurtzite MnSe, in experimentally useful volumes remains challenging. Here, we show that a nanoscale-period MnSe/CdSe superlattice stabilizes wurtzite MnSe over micrometer-scale total thickness while suppressing the formation of the thermodynamically favored rock-salt phase. The increased magnetic volume enables bulk-sensitive characterization of this polar polymorph. The room-temperature lattice parameters of wurtzite MnSe are studied by independent experimental techniques and determined to be $a = (4.18 \pm 0.03)\,\mathring{A}$ and $c = (6.78 \pm 0.03)\, \mathring{A}$. SQUID magnetometry reveals antiferromagnetic ordering with $T_N = 62\,\text{K}$, which is accompanied by an anomaly of the MnSe lattice parameter, as oberved by temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction. Optical measurements reveal excitonic transitions pointing to the band gap at around 3.4 eV. These results highlight the utility and importance of heterostructure engineering for detailed studies of metastable phases of magnetic semiconductors, in particular wurtzite MnSe.

papers.title: A Compact High-Repetition-Rate Intense THz Source for Atomic-Scale Materials Characterization
papers.summary: High-intensity terahertz (THz) sources combining high repetition rates, strong field amplitudes, and long-term stability are key enabling technologies for next-generation ultrafast photonics. However, simultaneously achieving these characteristics in a compact and practical architecture remains a major challenge. Here, we report a high-performance tabletop THz source delivering intense single-cycle pulses at 100 kHz, generated by optical rectification in lithium niobate using an optimized echelon-based tilted-pulse-front scheme and driven by an industrial-grade ytterbium laser. The source achieves optical-to-THz conversion efficiencies exceeding 0.13% at room temperature, peak electric fields of several hundred kV/cm, and excellent long-term stability, establishing a robust platform for high-average-power strong-field THz applications. As a proof of concept, the source was integrated into an atom probe tomography (APT) instrument. APT reconstructs the three-dimensional chemical composition of materials through field-induced ion emission from a sharp nanotip. While THz-assisted ion emission has been shown to improve analytical performance by reducing thermal effects, previous demonstrations were limited to low-repetition-rate THz sources, restricting throughput and accessible analysis volumes. Using an aluminum nanotip, we demonstrate efficient THz-assisted APT at 100 kHz and benchmark its performance against conventional voltage- and laser-assisted operation. The high repetition rate enables rapid large-volume acquisition while improving mass resolving power, reducing thermal tailing, and preserving high-quality three-dimensional reconstructions. Beyond APT, this work establishes a compact and scalable high-repetition-rate THz platform for strong-field physics, nonlinear THz photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and material characterization at the nanoscale.

papers.title: Spontaneous Formation of Lateral Defect-Density Gradient in CVD-Grown MoS2 Monolayers
papers.summary: Defect engineering in two-dimensional materials is a powerful strategy for tuning electronic, optical, and catalytic properties. While pristine molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) has been thoroughly studied, defective MoS2 remains poorly understood due to the complexity and inconsistency of controlled defect creation. Here, we report a defect-density gradient that forms spontaneously in MoS2 flakes during chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth. Photoluminescence and Raman spectroscopy mapping reveal the lateral arrangement of this gradient across a single flake. Deconvolution of the excitonic photoluminescence emission identifies electron doping as the key factor governing the spatial variation in optical response. This doping likely originates from sulfur vacancies formed during CVD growth, as further supported by the observed Raman mode shifts. We propose that this gradient arises from precursor depletion near the nucleation center during growth, resulting in a gradual variation in defect density. This lateral defect structure provides a convenient platform for systematically characterizing defective MoS2 across a continuous range of defect densities within a single sample. The sulfur-vacancy-driven surface activation identified here can also be important for future catalytic applications.

papers.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
papers.summary: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU and an operational figure of merit of 40 $\mathrm{RIU}^{-1}$, this low-loss HfO$_{2}$ metasurface provides a robust foundation for label-free DUV biosensing.

papers.title: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
papers.summary: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time. We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian $SU(2)$ symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes $U(1)$ and $Z_2$ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.

papers.title: Redox-coupled ZnCl2 water-in-salt electrolyte enables high capacity and long-term cycling stability in Ti3C2Tx MXene supercapacitors
papers.summary: Water-in-salt electrolytes coupled with redox species (RC-WiSEs) can be promising candidates for 2D Ti3C2Tx MXene supercapacitors due to their expanded electrochemical stability window (ESW) and enhanced diffusion-controlled contributions. Herein, the incorporation of RC-ZnCl2 WiSE into a Ti3C2Tx MXene supercapacitor enables a wide ESW of 1.6 V, along with high capacity and ultrastability. The Ti3C2Tx MXene supercapacitor delivers a maximum energy density of 36.7 Wh kg-1 and a power density of 3065 W kg-1. Notably, the device retains approximately 80% of its capacity even after 100,000 continuous galvanostatic charge–discharge cycles and also maintains stable capacitive performance over a broad temperature range from -5 °C to 45 °C. A thorough in situ Raman and UV-Vis spectroelectrochemical investigation, combined with electrochemical analysis, reveals that redox species directly regulate interfacial chemistry, thereby enhancing the capacity and stability of the electrode. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of RC-WiSE systems and encourages their use to enhance the charge storage capacity and cycling stability of MXene-based systems.

papers.title: Lithium Metal Phosphate Cathodes for Energy Storage: Production Routes, Structure–Performance Relationships, Scale‐Up Challenges, and Recycling Perspectives
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Olivine‐type LiMPO 4 (M = Fe, Mn, Co, Ni, and mixed‐transition‐metal compositions) cathodes are among the most robust positive‐electrode families for rechargeable lithium‐ion batteries, offering high thermal stability and favorable safety characteristics for transportation and stationary energy storage. Practical performance is strongly governed by synthesis–structure–interface coupling: modest variations in particle size and morphology, anti‐site disorder, carbon topology, or surface chemistry can shift the dominant limitation from bulk diffusion to interfacial charge transfer or interphase transport. This review summarizes recent progress in LiMPO 4 production routes and relates processing parameters to microstructure and electrochemical behavior. Solid‐state, sol–gel, hydro/solvothermal, precipitation‐assisted, and rapid‐heating approaches are discussed in terms of how they control nucleation and growth and thereby determine primary‐particle geometry, secondary agglomeration, and accessible surface area. Strategies to mitigate intrinsic transport limitations are evaluated, including conductive‐carbon architectures, aliovalent and isovalent doping, mixed‐cation tuning in Li(Fe,Mn)PO 4 , defect engineering to reduce Li/Fe anti‐site formation, and interface stabilization via electrolyte/additive selection and surface coatings. Finally, electrode engineering, testing protocols, and scale‐up constraints are considered to outline practical pathways toward manufacturable LiMPO 4 cathodes with balanced rate capability, durability, and sustainability. By integrating production routes, structure–performance relationships, scale‐up constraints, and recycling perspectives, this review provides a practical framework for selecting LiMPO 4 cathode design strategies according to the dominant limitation of each chemistry.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Structural Engineering of Zn Anodes for Advanced Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Prospects
papers.summary: Abstract Benefiting from their intrinsic safety, earth-abundant zinc resources, low manufacturing cost, and environmentally benign chemistry, aqueous zinc-based batteries have emerged as a compelling candidate for next-generation sustainable energy storage systems. Although metallic Zn anodes offer a high theoretical capacity and an advantageous redox potential, their practical application is severely hindered by interfacial instability issues, including dendritic growth, dead-Zn formation, hydrogen evolution, and corrosion, leading to poor Coulombic efficiency and limited cycling durability. While extensive research has focused on materials-level optimization, the translation of lab-scale advances into commercially viable devices hinges on scalable and controllable manufacturing technologies. In this review, we address this gap by presenting a manufacturing-centric analysis of three-dimensional (3D) Zn anode engineering. We systematically evaluate how advanced manufacturing processes, including additive manufacturing, laser ablation, electrospinning, template imprinting, and electrodeposition, enable precise regulation of electrode architecture, local electric fields, and Zn2+ transport pathways. These advantages collectively promote uniform Zn plating/stripping, suppress dendrite growth, and alleviate parasitic side reactions. This review provides a systematic overview of recent progress in topology-guided 3D Zn anodes, encompassing representative fabrication strategies. Furthermore, structure-performance relationships across various 3D designs are elucidated. Finally, we outline remaining challenges and future research directions toward durable, scalable, and high-performance zinc-based energy storage.

papers.title: Unlocking Neutral Hydrogen Evolution via a Lattice‐Proton‐Mediated Pathway on a Pt/h‐WO 3 Single‐Atom Catalyst
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Sustainable hydrogen production from abundant natural water is severely hampered by the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in neutral media, a fundamental bottleneck for large‐scale water electrolysis. Herein, we report a novel synergistic strategy to circumvent this limitation by designing a platinum single‐atom catalyst supported on hexagonal tungsten oxide (Pt/ h ‐WO 3 ). Our theoretical and experimental results show that the H x WO 3 support acts as a lattice‐proton reservoir that captures and stores protons (H + ) from water within its lattice. The stored H + ions are subsequently utilized by the atomic Pt sites, which serve as catalytic sites that open a low‐energy pathway and bypass the high activation barrier of conventional water dissociation. This unique mechanism, directly verified by in situ Raman spectroscopy, endows the catalyst with strong acid‐like HER activity in neutral media, achieving an overpotential of only 22 mV at 10 mA cm −2 . This work establishes a powerful design principle that synergizes lattice‐level reactant storage with atomic‐level catalytic sites and offers a new paradigm for overcoming kinetic barriers in challenging electrochemical reactions.

papers.title: Atomic-Scale Origin of Spatially Heterogeneous Insertion in Hollandite-Type MnO2
papers.summary: Abstract Hollandite-type α-MnO2 is a prototypical tunnel-structured host for rechargeable batteries, yet the atomic-scale mechanisms governing multivalent-ion insertion remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal how guest-ion species dictate electrochemical reaction pathways through distinct occupation modes within the one-dimensional tunnels of α-MnO2. By combining electrochemical analyses, atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, and soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we directly correlate reaction kinetics with guest-ion configurations and the accompanying structural and electronic responses of the host framework. Electrochemical measurements reveal substantial diffusion-controlled contributions for both Na+ and Mg2+, whereas Ca2+ exhibits predominantly surface-controlled behavior. Atomic-resolution imaging demonstrates that, despite their comparable macroscopic kinetic contributions, Na+ and Mg2+ exhibit distinctly different microscopic insertion modes: Na+ homogeneously occupies the tunnel-center sites throughout the particles, whereas Mg2+ occupies both tunnel-center and off-center sites, with pronounced near-surface enrichment accompanied by local tunnel distortion. In contrast, the Ca2+ reaction is largely confined to the near-surface region, with no clearly detectable occupation of the internal tunnel sites. Soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy further reveals spatially heterogeneous Mn reduction, with more pronounced reduction near the structurally less constrained particle surface. These results establish a direct relationship between guest-ion occupation modes, electrochemical reaction pathways, and the resulting structural evolution, providing an atomic-scale design principle for engineering tunnel-type host materials for multivalent-ion insertion.

papers.title: Progress on Failure Mechanisms and Modification Strategies of Ni‐Rich Ternary Cathode Materials
papers.summary: Ni‐rich ternary cathode materials deliver high reversible capacity and energy density, making them leading candidates for next‐generation high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries. However, increasing Ni content inevitably destabilizes the layered structure, accelerates interfacial side reactions, and induces mechanical degradation, creating a trade‐off between capacity and longevity. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of the coupled failure mechanisms that underlie this trade‐off. Cation mixing and lattice oxygen release are identified as primary triggers that initiate irreversible phase transitions and surface reconstruction, which in turn promote microcracking and electrolyte infiltration, establishing a self‐amplifying degradation loop that accelerates capacity fading. Based on this mechanistic understanding, recent advances in modification strategies are critically examined, including elemental doping, surface coating, concentration‐gradient design, single‐crystal engineering, defect regulation, and morphology optimization. The review highlights a paradigm shift from isolated modifications toward synergistic, multiscale design that integrates bulk structural stabilization, surface and interfacial protection, and particle mechanical integrity. Finally, future directions are proposed, emphasizing the extension of these synergistic design principles to all‐solid‐state battery systems, where solid–solid interfacial compatibility poses new challenges and opportunities.

papers.title: A Novel Composite Cathode of Indanthrone/Graphene Oxide with an Expanded Ion Transport Channel for Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
papers.summary: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) have attracted extensive attention owing to their abundant raw material reserves and superior safety. Compared with traditional inorganic cathode materials, organic cathodes exhibit promising prospects for next‐generation batteries. Indanthrone (RD) consists of two imine‐bridged anthraquinone units. The numerous redox‐active sites within RD allow efficient coordination with Zn 2+ . To further improve the discharge performance of AZIBs, a novel RD/G composite cathode is fabricated via a hydrothermal method in this work, where RD is tightly coupled with graphene oxide (GO) possessing large interlayer spacing. In the RD/G composite, π–π stacking interactions between RD and GO construct a stable stacked architecture, accelerating electron transport and reinforcing structural integrity. Galvanostatic charge/discharge measurements reveal that the Zn|aqueous ZnSO 4 |RD/G‐2 full cell delivers an initial discharge capacity of 83.5 mAh g −1 at 800 mA g −1 , and maintains a capacity of 83.7 mAh g −1 wth 80.4% capacity retention after 2500 cycles. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations verify that the incorporation of GO increases the number of active sites, enhances cathode conductivity, and strengthens Zn 2+ binding affinity, thus accelerating Zn 2+ storage kinetics. This work offers a viable strategy and new insight toward developing high‐performance aqueous zinc‐ion batteries.

papers.title: Azobenzene‐based molecular solar thermal integrated with phase change materials for smart thermoregulating textiles
papers.summary: Abstract Molecular Solar Thermal (MOST) energy storage provides a molecular‐level route to convert intermittent sunlight into on‐demand heat via reversible photoisomerization of photoswitches. Azobenzene (Azo) and its derivatives stand out for wearable thermal management, as their photochemistry, thermal reversion kinetics, molecular packing, and interfacial interactions are amenable to systematic molecular engineering. We survey recent progress in azo‐based MOST textiles synergized with phase change materials (PCM), tracing the trajectory from molecular design to hybrid energy‐storage architectures and ultimately textile integration. Key strategies for enhancing azo energy storage are critically examined, including template confinement, polymer topology control, dynamic coordination, heteroaryl and ortho ‐substituent engineering, and alkyl‐chain‐mediated phase regulation. Particular emphasis is placed on Azo@PCM systems, in which the PCM matrix serves as a solid‐state solvent that promotes isomerization while contributing latent heat, enabling dual‐mode energy storage and light‐triggered heat release via controlled phase transitions. Representative textile fabrication methods, including coating, microencapsulation, electrospinning, wet‐spinning, coaxial spinning, and Janus architectures, are systematically reviewed. Persistent challenges in energy density, solar‐to‐thermal conversion efficiency, wearability, and scalable manufacturing are identified, offering perspectives for the rational design of next‐generation smart thermoregulating textiles.

papers.title: One‐Pot Synthesis of WO 3 /WS 2 Composite for High‐Performance Supercapacitor Electrodes
papers.summary: The development of efficient electrode materials through simple and scalable synthesis routes is essential for advancing high‐performance supercapacitors. Here, we report the synthesis of a tungsten oxide‐tungsten disulfide (WO 3 /WS 2 ) composite material using a facile one‐pot hydrothermal method. The coexistence of WO 3 and WS 2 materials is confirmed using TEM, XRD, XPS, and Raman spectroscopy. In the composite, the WS 2 layers provide mechanical stability and high conductivity, whereas WO 3 nanoparticles enhance the capacitance significantly through pseudocapacitive charge storage. The electrochemical measurements in a three‐electrode system with 1 M H 2 SO 4 electrolyte delivered a specific capacitance of 578.7 F/g at 1 A/g. A symmetric supercapacitor device fabricated with the composite presented an energy density of 10 Wh/kg at a power density of 800 W/kg, with nearly 100% capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles.

papers.title: Dual-Role Catalyst: Influence of Multi-Nonmetal Incorporation in Bi2WO6 for Comparative Photocatalytic Water Purification and Electrocatalytic Oxygen Evolution
papers.summary: Sustainable energy generation and environmental remediation heavily depend on the development of highly efficient noble metal-free catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and advanced photocatalysts for the degradation of contaminants. In this study, we synthesized sulfur-doped, boron-doped, and sulfur–boron co-doped Bi 2 WO 6 via a hydrothermal process to compare dual functional performance. Of the samples, boron-doped Bi 2 WO 6 exhibited the best catalytic activity. X-ray diffraction (XRD) showed that a crystalline orthorhombic structure was formed with lattice distortions and the diffraction plane shifting. Ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) spectroscopy showed that the optical band gap value was 2.7 eV, suitable for visible-light-driven photocatalysis, and it allowed radicals to generate efficiently and achieved 89% methylene blue (MB) degradation. The combined use of Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) showed a defined crystalline structure with no signs of molecular clustering. X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) analysis also confirmed oxygen vacancies, which were demonstrated by the shifts in the oxygen peaks with the associated binding energy. The presence of surface oxygen vacancies aids in supplementing photocatalytic activity by providing a pathway for charge transfer while preventing the recombination of an electron-hole pair during the photocatalytic reaction that contributes to the overall efficacies displayed in a multistep OER mechanism. Additionally, boron-doped bismuth tungstate oxide showed an exemplary efficiency as an electrocatalyst since it indicated a correlative low overpotential of 394 mV (without iR-compensation), current density of 10 mA cm -2 and Tafel slope of 142 mV/dec. It also exhibited lower resistance values, which improve reaction kinetics, and showed no decomposition through a seven-hour measurement period indicating good cyclic stability.

papers.title: Anisotropic reaction–transport dynamics in Ti-substituted tunnel sodium cathodes: A three-dimensional critical-rate framework
papers.summary: High-rate performance in anisotropic sodium-ion cathodes emerges from coupled particle-scale transport and reaction processes that cannot be represented adequately by a single effective diffusion coefficient. This study establishes a three-dimensional finite-element framework for rod-like Ti-substituted Na₄TiᵧMn₉₋ᵧO₁₈ tunnel cathodes by coupling tunnel-informed anisotropic Na transport, state-dependent diffusivity, concentration-dependent Butler–Volmer kinetics, finite electronic transport, and composition-dependent material properties. A model-derived critical rate, C crit , is introduced to identify the transition from quasi-uniform Na redistribution to transport-limited operation using the coupled evolution of concentration heterogeneity, reaction localization, and Na utilization. For the reference low-Ti particle, C crit was 2.35 ± 0.18C2.35\pm0.18 C. Increasing transport anisotropy raised C crit from 1.92 C at AD= 2–2.61 C at A D = 10, followed by a decline to 2.48 C at AD= 20, revealing diminishing benefit once transverse redistribution becomes limiting. Ti substitution produced a similarly non-monotonic response, with C crit increasing from 1.95 C for the Ti-free composition to 2.55 C at x Ti = 0.29, before decreasing to 1.88 C at x Ti = 0.56. Increasing particle aspect ratio from 3 to 8 reduced the threshold from 2.72 C to 1.86 C. Independent validation produced a GITT deviation of 9.7%, a rate-response NRMSE of 5.64%, and a MAPE of 6.38%. Notably, reaction localization emerged before pronounced loss of average Na utilization, identifying spatial reaction heterogeneity as an early marker of transport instability. The framework defines a composition–anisotropy–morphology design space for particle-scale control of high-rate sodium storage rather than a single optimum material configuration.

papers.title: Interface‐Engineered CuO / GO / TiO 2 Ternary Heterostructures for Adsorptive and Photocatalytic Removal of AY ‐25 Dye
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Acid Yellow‐25 (AY‐25) dye is a toxic pollutant that poses significant threats to both human health and the environment when discharged into aquatic systems. To resolve this problem, we have prepared graphene oxide (GO) nanoparticles (NPs), their binary (CuO/GO), and ternary (CuO/GO/TiO 2 ) nanocomposites (NCs). Pristine GO were synthesized by modified hummer's method, while copper oxide (CuO) and titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) were integrated using simple co‐precipitation approach. The preparation of this system is supported by structural, surface, thermal, and morphological analysis. Under UV–Vis light irradiation, the CuO/GO/TiO 2 NCs degraded 93.79% of 80 ppm AY‐25 dye in 240 min at pH 5, catalyst loading of 0.03 g, and 303 K, surpassing GO and CuO/GO which exhibited degradation efficiencies of 71.47% and 84.96%, respectively, under identical conditions. The process of degradation was tested using pseudo‐first‐order and pseudo‐second‐order kinetics models, and thermodynamics approach: which gave information about the physicochemical nature of the photocatalytic process. Furthermore, the simultaneous incorporation of CuO and TiO 2 into GO enhanced light absorption, charge separation, and prolonged the lifetime of charge carriers, thereby increasing the photocatalytic activity. This study offers a straightforward method for designing and fabricating a novel ternary NCs photocatalyst with potential applications in wastewater treatment.
