papers.title: Aldehyde or Carboxylic Acid: Defining the Selectivity of Electrochemical Oxidation of Aliphatic Alcohols by Tuning the Surface Phase of NiO(OH)
papers.summary: Abstract Nickel oxyhydroxide (NiO(OH)) is the catalytically active species during electrochemical alcohol oxidation at nickel electrodes. Herein, we demonstrate that the adopted phase structure of NiO(OH) (β- and γ-NiO(OH)) can dramatically influence the catalytic properties of nickel electrodes. We show that β-NiO(OH) oxidizes aliphatic alcohols preferentially to aldehydes and that carboxylates are formed at γ-NiO(OH). By combining the effect of the NiO(OH) phase with reagent effects (electrolyte pH, alcohol concentration, and trace amounts of Fe), we achieve aldehyde formation with ∼90% selectivity or carboxylate formation with ∼85% selectivity. Furthermore, we perform an in situ Raman spectroelectrochemical study to elucidate the reaction conditions that favor the formation of β- and γ-NiO(OH) phases, respectively. Freshly deposited nickel electrodes form γ-NiO(OH) phases upon oxidation, whereas an electrochemical conditioning protocol can be employed to transform γ- to β-NiO(OH). Finally, we show that the efficiency of this transformation depends on the precise reaction conditions and the precursor used. Hence, we showcase that the exact surface structure of the phase formed in situ on top of transition metal (oxides) affects the product distribution of electrochemical reactions. Moreover, we highlight how the “history” of these catalysts affects their performance via an intricate interplay among the reaction environment, pre-treatment, and surface structure.

papers.title: Formation‐Stage Interfacial Regulation of δ‐MnO 2 Enables Stable and Reversible Aqueous Zn‐Ion Storage
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Layered δ‐MnO 2 is a promising cathode for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries, yet its practical application remains hindered by the coupled challenges of sluggish Zn 2+ storage kinetics and persistent Mn dissolution. Here, we develop a precursor‐embedded Fe interfacial regulation strategy to modulate the nucleation and growth of δ‐MnO 2 on porous carbon nanofibers (δ‐MnO 2 @Fe‐PCNFs). Rather than being dominated by homogeneous bulk substitution, the introduced Fe is predominantly present as low‐content, highly dispersed surface‐/interface‐associated species established during δ‐MnO 2 formation, where it regulates the local Mn─O environment and consequently modulates nanosheet growth and the accessibility of the reaction interface. The Fe‐regulated δ‐MnO 2 framework exhibits improved kinetic accessibility and suppresses Mn dissolution without altering its intrinsic Mn‐based redox chemistry. Consequently, the δ‐MnO 2 @Fe‐PCNFs electrode delivers an initial capacity of 409.29 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 and excellent long‑term cycling stability, maintaining a capacity of 243.64 mAh g −1 at 1 A g −1 after 1000 cycles and excellent capacity retention of 81.1% after 3000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . This work highlights formation‐stage interfacial regulation as an effective strategy to couple reaction accessibility with structural durability in Mn‐based aqueous zinc‐ion battery cathodes.

papers.title: Post‐Synthetic Cerium Modification of Commercial NCM811 for Concurrent Cycling and Safety Upgrading
papers.summary: ABSTRACT The widespread use of Ni‐rich LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cathodes in high‐energy batteries remains limited by structural degradation, side reactions, and oxygen release, yet most modification strategies prove incompatible with commercial materials. This work presents a facile solid‐state method that achieves synergistic cerium ion (Ce 3+ ) doping and CeO 2 coating on commercial NCM811 by mixing with CeO 2 nanoparticles followed by calcination. Structural and morphological analyses confirm Ce incorporation into the near‐surface lattice and the formation of a nanoscale CeO 2 layer without disturbing the layered framework. Electrochemical tests demonstrate that the optimal 1 wt.% Ce‐modified sample exhibits superior rate capability and long‐term stability, retaining 82.04% of its initial capacity after 500 cycles at 1 C, compared to 74.10% for pristine, owing to suppressed cation mixing, enhanced structural stability, and improved Li + diffusion kinetics. Crucially, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry shows Ce modification curtails O 2 release and reduces H 2 and CO 2 generation across various rates, effectively mitigating gas evolution associated with safety degradation. Accelerating rate calorimetry further confirms delayed thermal runaway and improved adiabatic stability. Overall, this work establishes a scalable post‐treatment route to simultaneously boost the electrochemical performance and safety of commercial nickel‐rich cathodes, offering a practical solution for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries.

papers.title: Design, Construction and Applications of Multidirectional Tactile Sensors
papers.summary: Flexible tactile sensors must resolve not only the magnitude but also the direction, position, and mode of mechanical stimuli to support reliable perception of complex contacts. This Review critically examines how material selection, microstructural anisotropy, device architecture, and signal processing jointly enable multidirectional tactile sensing. We first relate flexible substrates, electrodes, and active layers to directional encoding by oriented pores and fibers, localized cracks and interfaces, and mechanically asymmetric structures. We then compare planar multiaxis assemblies, three-dimensional arrays, and monolithic multichannel devices and assess their use in human-motion monitoring, environmental sensing, and human–machine interaction. Across these systems, reliable vector reconstruction depends on identifiable mechanical transfer pathways and complementary outputs that decouple coupled loads, rather than on peak sensitivity or channel number alone. Current devices, however, remain constrained by fabrication variability, crosstalk, calibration drift, integration complexity, and limited validation under combined loads and realistic operating conditions. Progress toward deployable systems therefore requires programmable and reproducible anisotropy, mechanically isolated channels, scalable fabrication, adaptive decoding, and standardized evaluation that reports reconstruction uncertainty and long-term robustness.

papers.title: Structural Strategies for Buffering Volume Expansion in Transition-Metal Oxides and Related Conversion/Alloying-Type Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
papers.summary: Abstract The growing problem of energy shortage has undoubtedly promoted research and development in energy storage. Against this background, rechargeable sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are considered one of the most promising candidates for replacing lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) due to their advantages of low cost, good thermal stability, and superior low-temperature performance. Therefore, the development of SIBs has received much attention and focus. Currently, research on SIBs faces the critical problem of large volume change of anode materials during charging and discharging. Despite the volume change problem, past research has been trying to buffer the volume changes, and there’s been a lot of progress. Transition metal oxides (TMOs) based on conversion reactions have become potential anode materials for SIBs due to their more stable crystal structures and good cycling stability. In this review, we first analyze the energy-storage principle of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Then, we outline a series of structural strategies for SIBs concerning the large volume change of the anode material during charging and discharging processes, and we classify and discuss the existing studies on nanostructures according to their morphological features. Finally, we summarize the challenges and future trends of TMOs for electrochemical energy storage in SIBs.

papers.title: Signature of chiral anomaly in a graphene-based heterostructure
papers.summary: Chiral anomaly is a fundamental manifestation of topological matter caused by chirality imbalance. It can be of great practical value by providing a mechanism for dissipationless transport. The phenomenon is highly sensitive to the system dimensionality, disappearing in the 2D limit. Different schemes have been proposed to observe the chiral anomaly in graphene-based systems but experimental evidence has been lacking. Here, we synthesized two types of the Gr/Sr/SiC nanostructure - with 2D and 3D, bulk-like, layers of Sr - the difference being the amount of Sr intercalated under graphene. In contrast to the 2D material, 3D Gr/Sr/SiC exhibits a signature of the chiral anomaly - quadratic negative magnetoresistance in parallel magnetic and electric fields. Also, the functional form of the temperature dependence of the magnetoresistance agrees with the chiral anomaly. In addition, the 3D heterostructure exhibits suppressed conductivity and quantum oscillations in graphene. These effects may be associated with the graphene layer incorporated into a complex 3D heterostructure. Hopefully, the discovered signature of chiral anomaly in the built-in graphene would spur research on the phenomenon in topological nanomaterials.

papers.title: Composition-dependent charge-storage kinetics and heterojunction charge-transfer dynamics in $$\:{\text{WO}}_{3}/{\text{g-C}}_{3}{\text{N}}_{4}/{\text{BiVO}}_{4}$$ nanocomposites
papers.summary: Optimizing electrode materials for supercapacitors requires a precise balance between electronic conductivity and rapid ion-diffusion kinetics. In this work, a ternary \(\:{\text{WO}}_{3}/{\text{g-C}}_{3}{\text{N}}_{4}/{\text{BiVO}}_{4}\) heterostructure nanocomposite was synthesized via hydrothermal and sonication-assisted routes to investigate composition-dependent charge-storage kinetics and interfacial charge-transfer dynamics. Structural (XRD), morphological (SEM/EDX), and chemical (XPS) analyses confirmed multi-phase heterojunction formation, high elemental purity, and intrinsic microstrain ( \(\:\epsilon\:=0.0136\) ). UV–vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) demonstrated enhanced visible-light response with a narrowed bandgap ( \(\:{E}_{g}=2.14\text{\:eV}\) ), indicating improved electronic coupling across phase boundaries. Electrochemical evaluations in a three-electrode setup ( \(\:3\text{\:M\:KOH}\) ) revealed that while the binary \(\:{\text{WO}}_{3}/{\text{g-C}}_{3}{\text{N}}_{4}\) matrix provides high surface-controlled capacity ( \(\:26.85{\text{\:mAh\:g}}^{-1}\) at \(\:2{\text{\:A\:g}}^{-1}\) ), incorporation of \(\:{\text{BiVO}}_{4}\) modulates the underlying charge-storage mechanism. Power-law kinetic fitting ( \(\:b=0.4071\) ) and low-frequency Warburg impedance analysis confirm that charge storage in the ternary composite ( \(\:{Q}_{s}=4.32{\text{\:mAh\:g}}^{-1}\) at \(\:2{\text{\:A\:g}}^{-1}\) ) is governed by semi-infinite bulk diffusion rather than rapid surface pseudocapacitance. EIS analysis demonstrated a significant reduction in charge-transfer resistance ( \(\:{R}_{ct}\approx\:80\:{\Omega\:}\) ) compared to pristine \(\:{\text{BiVO}}_{4}\) ( \(\:\sim\:450\:{\Omega\:}\) ), while long-term GCD testing showed stable cycling with \(\:\sim\:75\text{-}76\%\) capacity retention after 5000 cycles and high Coulombic efficiency ( \(\:\sim\:98.5\%\) ). This study clarifies that \(\:{\text{BiVO}}_{4}\) incorporation acts as a kinetic tuner modulating interfacial mass-transport dynamics rather than a total capacity booster, offering critical insights for engineering multi-phase metal oxide heterostructures.

papers.title: Ni-induced Structural Spring Effect in High-performance Mn-Rich P2-Type Sodium Cathodes
papers.summary: Abstract Anionic redox chemistry offers a promising pathway toward high capacity in P2-type Mn-rich layered cathodes. However, the practical application is hindered by sluggish redox kinetics, severe oxygen loss, and structural deterioration, leading to poor cycling performance and particularly inadequate activity under high-current conditions. Herein, we propose a Ni-induced structural spring effect in P2-Na5/6Li1/4Mn3/4O2 (NLM) by partially substituting Li with Ni. This Ni-induced covalent strengthening acts as a structural "spring" that dynamically buffers mechanical stress during Na⁺ extraction/insertion, effectively suppressing phase transitions at deep desodiation states and preserving structural integrity. Meanwhile, Ni incorporation effectively mitigates the Jahn–Teller distortion of Mn3+ by modulating the local coordination environment, thereby alleviating anisotropic lattice strain. Concurrently, the Ni–O octahedral spring effect bonding accelerates oxygen redox kinetics, mitigates voltage hysteresis, and suppresses irreversible oxygen release, thereby stabilizing the anionic redox activity at high rates. The resulting material, P2-Na0.73Li0.15Ni0.1Mn0.75O2 (NLNM), exhibits nearly twofold reduction in overpotential during oxygen redox, delivers a specific capacity of ~150 mAh/g at the average voltage of 3.4 V, and retains 82% capacity after 200 cycles at 600 mA/g. This work demonstrates the strategy of Ni-induced spring effect for stable anionic activation and structural robustness, consequently achieving long-term cycling stability in high-performance oxide cathodes.

papers.title: Advances on triply periodic hyperbolic surface structures: from biological inspiration to artificial self-assembly
papers.summary: Triply periodic hyperbolic surfaces (TPHSs) are a class of complex structures that extend periodically throughout three-dimensional space and possess smooth surfaces with non-positive Gaussian curvature. They appear in a wide range of natural systems, from cellular membranes to butterfly wing scales and beetle exoskeletons. Owing to their unique geometries and extraordinary properties, TPHSs have attracted extensive attention and research interest. Detailed structural characterizations of naturally occurring TPHSs have been performed, and a variety of artificial analogs have been fabricated by top-down physical methods and bottom-up chemical approaches. These efforts have deepened our understanding of TPHSs and broadened their application scope. This review discusses the progress on TPHSs in biological systems and their artificial synthesis, and it surveys current applications of these structures in fields such as photonics, energy storage and conversion, catalysis, sensing, thermal management and mechanical metamaterials. It thereby provides a new framework linking biological structures to artificial structures. Finally, this review concludes by outlining current challenges and proposing directions for future research.

papers.title: Interface engineering in sodium metal anodes: challenges, design strategies and perspectives
papers.summary: Abstract Sodium metal anodes (SMAs) possess a high theoretical capacity (1166 mAh g⁻¹), a low redox potential (−2.71 V vs. SHE), and abundant sodium resources, making sodium metal batteries (SMBs) highly promising next-generation energy storage systems. However, their practical applications remain severely constrained by instability at the electrode–electrolyte interface, leading to persistent side reactions, sodium dendrite growth, low coulombic efficiency, and a decline in cycle life. These issues are all closely related to the formation, evolution, and failure of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). This paper constructs an analytical framework for the interfacial chemistry of SMBs centered on the dynamic evolution of the SEI. It systematically elucidates the mechanisms of SEI formation, evolution, and failure, further systematizing interface regulation strategies in both liquid and solid electrolyte systems, with a particular focus on the fundamental differences between liquid and solid interfaces in terms of formation mechanisms, failure behavior and regulation principles. Building on this, strategies for constructing high-energy-density SMAs are discussed from the perspective of interface–structure synergistic design. Finally, in light of the key challenges currently facing research in this field, future directions are outlined, including the mechanisms of dynamic SEI evolution, descriptor-guided interface design, the chemical–mechanical coupling at solid-state interfaces, and evaluation systems tailored to real-world operating conditions. This review aims to deepen the understanding of interfacial chemistry in SMBs and to provide a theoretical basis and design guidance for the rational design and practical development of high-safety, long-lifespan SMBs.

papers.title: MXene–carbon nanotube composites in batteries and supercapacitors: recent advances and future perspectives
papers.summary: MXenes, two-dimensional transition metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides (M n+1 X n T x ), have emerged as promising electrode materials for next-generation energy storage owing to their metallic conductivity, hydrophilicity, and tunable surface chemistry. However, pristine MXene electrodes suffer from nanosheet restacking, which limits ion accessibility, and oxidative degradation, which compromises long-term stability. This review systematically examines MXene–carbon nanotube (MXene/CNT) composites across the synthesis–structure–property–application chain, comparing MXene and CNT synthesis routes, composite assembly strategies, and interfacial engineering approaches, including defect and strain engineering. Applications in lithium-ion, sodium/potassium-ion, zinc-ion, and lithium–sulfur batteries, and supercapacitors are surveyed, where composites achieve conductivities of 10 4 –10 5 S m -1 , specific capacitances of 800–1200 F g -1 , and cycling stability exceeding 90–95% after 10,000 cycles. Key challenges relating to mass loading, rate capability, voltage window, and scalable manufacturing are discussed, along with future research directions for advancing MXene/CNT composites toward practical energy storage devices.

papers.title: Heat Transport Mechanisms in MOF-5
papers.summary: We find that MOF-5 supports both long-lived phonons and linker vibrations whose split spectra signal a breakdown of the phonon quasiparticle approximation. Combining mode-projected molecular dynamics spectra with spectral Wigner heat transport, we resolve two contrasting transport channels: low-frequency particle-like phonon propagation decreases strongly from 200 to 500 K, whereas wave-like phonon coherence remains nearly constant and supplies about half the intrinsic conductivity at 500 K. A phenomenological extrinsic scattering model provides a plausible explanation for the discrepancy between calculated and measured conductivities in terms of both its magnitude and temperature dependence. We also identify signatures of phonon quasiparticle breakdown in the linker vibrations of ZIF-8 and HKUST-1, indicating that this feature extends to other metal-organic frameworks.

papers.title: Zero-Point Renormalization Reshapes the Shift Current: The Role of Electron-Phonon Coupling
papers.summary: Shift current (SC) drives the bulk photovoltaic effect, holding promise for near-instantaneous, low-dissipation photodetection and energy conversion. The current understanding of SC relies primarily on a single-particle picture, in which the SC is determined purely by band dispersion. While many-body effects from directly excited quasiparticles, such as excitons, magnons and phonons, have been explored, the renormalization of electronic states by quantum virtual-phonon coupling --- inherent in essentially all solids and particularly decisive for transport --- remains unaddressed. Here, using first-principles calculations, we identify this missing channel --- band-renormalized shift current (BRSC) --- in monolayer MoS2. We find that the zero-point renormalization alone, without any polarization-carrying photoexcited phonons and with barely any alteration of the band dispersion, dramatically reshapes the SC spectrum: emergent low-energy peaks arise from phonon-assisted optical transitions between momentum-distinct states, with a pronounced redshift of higher-energy features. A mere 1.0% strain sharply tunes the BRSC, whereas raising the temperature enhances it. Our findings overturn the band-structure-only paradigm, establishing electron-phonon coupling as an indispensable ingredient for nonlinear photocurrent and opening a strain-thermal route for engineering next-generation optoelectronic responses.

papers.title: Observation of ultra-low thermal conductivity in ultra-thin single-crystalline PbI2 nanosheets
papers.summary: Low thermal conductivity materials are key for next-generation thermal management. However, non-destructive characterization of ultra-thin single crystals remains challenging. Here, we report a room-temperature thermal conductivity of 0.24 W/(m·K) in 7.9 nm single-crystalline PbI2 nanosheets, representing an experimentally realized ultra-low value in the ultra-thin single-crystal regime. This observation is enabled by an integrated in‑situ growth‑location‑measurement strategy that couples aqueous‑solution nucleation with gas‑flow‑assisted alignment, enabling the non‑destructive transfer of nanosheets onto a suspended thermal bridge. Combining first‑principles density functional theory calculations and Raman spectroscopy, we trace the suppressed thermal transport in PbI2 to flattened flexural acoustic phonons with markedly low group velocities and short lifetimes. Furthermore, this suppression is exacerbated by thickness-induced vibrational softening, while in-situ irradiation allows for dynamic thermal modulation. This work establishes a robust experimental framework for characterizing ultra-thin single crystals with ultra-low thermal conductivity, bridging theoretical prediction with experimental realization for advanced flexible thermal management applications. The authors report low room-temperature thermal conductivity (0.24 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹) in 7.9 nm single-crystalline PbI₂ nanosheets. Non-destructive suspended-device measurements and theory reveal flexural-phonon suppression, while irradiation enables dynamic thermal tuning.

papers.title: Advancing Research Fronts of Polymeric Membranes for CO2 Capture: Bibliometric Analysis, Performance Gaps, and AI-Driven Horizons
papers.summary: Current polymers used for carbon capture are limited by their toxic footprint during manufacturing and degradation over time. This review aims to propose a new paradigm for designing membranes for carbon dioxide capture using data-driven approaches to bibliometrics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning with the goal of creating next-generation, sustainable polymers for carbon dioxide capture. Bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix will be used to present the most commonly used keywords, people, and countries that are working more on this topic. Furthermore, an exposing of the gaps between the performance of membranes under laboratory settings versus in real world environments will be conducted. AI and machine learning approaches will be investigated to fill these performance gaps. Methods for shifting towards a circular economy with the inverse design of bio based polymers, green fillers, and low carbon, non toxic solvents will be discussed. Finally, the virtual discoveries in the field of polymers for carbon capture will be correlated with the current industrial world to formulate a roadmap for these materials to reach high technology readiness levels for use across the globe.

papers.title: Negligible Kitaev interaction in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ revealed by neutron spectroscopy
papers.summary: Using time-of-flight neutron spectroscopy, we have mapped out the magnetic excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ over a broad range of energies and momenta. The observed well-defined magnon dispersions are quantitatively reproduced by linear spin-wave theory based on a minimal bilinear Hamiltonian that includes Heisenberg exchange interactions up to third-nearest neighbors, interlayer couplings, and a single-ion anisotropy term, with no need to invoke a Kitaev interaction. This finding is consistent with the fact that bromine is lighter than iodine, leading to weaker ligand-mediated spin-orbit coupling in NiBr2 than in NiI2, and consequently a reduced Kitaev interaction. Our results establish NiBr$_2$ as a Heisenberg-dominated van der Waals antiferromagnet and support the view that the ligand spin-orbit coupling governs the strength of the bond-dependent interactions within the NiX$_2$ (X = halogen) family.

papers.title: Anisotropy lifts topological protection of transport in pumped spin chains
papers.summary: We investigate the prospect of topological spin pumping and transport in a dimerized spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ anisotropic XY chain with tunable in-plane anisotropy. Through a Jordan-Wigner transformation, the system maps onto an extended Rice-Mele-type fermionic model whose momentum-space band structure exhibits gapped regions characterized by nonzero Chern numbers ($\pm 1$) as well as trivial and gapless regimes. Conventional momentum-space analysis therefore predicts quantized Thouless-type spin pumping in parts of the Chern number diagram. However, real-space time evolution under open boundary conditions reveals that the spin transport is generally not quantized away from the isotropic limit. In the anisotropic regime, eigen-energy states within the transporting subspace hybridize during the driving cycle, leading to a transport that depends on details of the driving protocol. Quantized pumping and transport survive only in the isotropic limit, where the Hamiltonian reduces to decoupled Rice-Mele sectors and the transported spin component is conserved. Our results demonstrate that momentum-space topological invariants alone do not guarantee quantized spin transport in anisotropic spin chains. More broadly, they show that the conventional Thouless-pumping framework does not straightforwardly extend to situations where the transported quantity is not conserved, highlighting the importance of real-space diagnostics in topological transport phenomena.

papers.title: Probing Non-Abelian Topology through Quench Dynamics
papers.summary: Quench dynamics offer valuable insights to topological matter, wherein the emergent topological phenomena serve as a dynamic probe to the topology of static Hamiltonians. While such a practice has been widely applied to detect the Abelian band topology or the Euler-class topology of band nodes, little is known regarding the quench dynamics of non-Abelian topological insulators in multiband systems, where the intertwining geometry of all eigenstates necessitates the description of noncommutative topological charges. Here we propose a quench protocol for non-Abelian topological insulators, so that the underlying topology can be systematically probed using dynamic signatures. Specifically, we develop a band-projection scheme to extract the gap-resolved topology from dynamic skyrmions in the emergent quasimomentum--time manifolds of the quench processes. These skyrmions are characterized by a series of gap-resolved dynamic Chern numbers, which enable us to reconstruct the full non-Abelian topology of the post-quench Hamiltonian, including the global non-Abelian topological charge and edge-state patterns under the open-boundary condition. Our proposal offers dynamical access to non-Abelian topology in multiband systems, and can be readily implemented using photons or cold atoms.

papers.title: Ni ordering in the van der Waals gap of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$: from disorder through $2\times2$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order to stripe order
papers.summary: We report a synchrotron x-ray diffraction study of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$ over the range $0.18 \le x \le 0.57$, with Ni contents measured by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Powder diffraction on the whole series shows that the NbS$_2$ host is preserved, while the Ni ions in the van der Waals gap evolve from a disordered arrangement to $2\times2$ order at $x=1/4$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order at $x=1/3$, through a range where both motifs coexist, to an orthorhombic stripe-type order at $x=0.57$. The in-plane lattice parameter increases with Ni content, whereas the interlayer spacing remains nearly constant except for a pronounced minimum at $x=1/4$, which density-functional calculations reproduce for the ordered structure. Single-crystal diffraction on the two commensurate phases shows that the $x=1/4$ structure, with Ni on a single site and a trimerized Nb lattice, is free of stacking faults, whereas the chiral $x=1/3$ structure contains Ni on the nominally empty site, inversion twins and stacking faults of the Ni layers. The comparison between powders and crystals shows that grinding mainly degrades the stacking of the Ni layers. These results establish the structural phase diagram of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ and the intercalant disorder to be taken into account in the interpretation of its magnetic properties.

papers.title: Functional roles of non-redox active dopants in sodium layered oxide cathodes
papers.summary: Sodium layered oxide cathodes offer high energy density and structural versatility but suffer from irreversible phase transitions, transition-metal migration, and poor air/moisture stability. This review examines how non-redox-active dopants address these challenges through distinct roles in Na and transition-metal layers, including pillar effects, modulation of interlayer spacing and transition-metal-oxygen bonding, regulating Na + transport kinetics with enhanced environmental stability, and provides guidance for rational dopant selection.

papers.title: Strengthening TMP‐Derived Phosphate SEI via Sn Scaffold and BF 4 − Interphase Chemistry for Ultra‐Stable, High‐Rate Zn Metal Anodes
papers.summary: ABSTRACT While dynamic solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) construction and solvation engineering have transformed aqueous zinc‐ion batteries, translating these approaches to Organic electrolytes (OE) remains a challenging endeavor due to fundamentally different interfacial environments, solvation thermodynamics, and anion decomposition pathways. Despite providing superior thermodynamic stabilization to Zn anode, OE exhibits low ionic conductivity, thereby limiting operational current densities. Herein, we report the first demonstration of Sn(BF 4 ) 2 /H 2 O (SFB) additive integration in a non‐flammable trimethyl phosphate (TMP)‐ethanol (EtOH) (2:1 v/v) OE to architect a gradient SEI interphase on Zn anodes. The multifunctional integration of SFB facilitates the formation of a Sn‐coated Zn surface, a BF 4 1− ‐derived SEI@Zn, and H 2 O molecules as a proton source, collectively contributing to enhanced capacity. This strategic solvent‐salt‐metal synergy enables bi‐layered interfacial engineering within a single electrolyte system, significantly improving the reversibility and stability of the Zn anode. Consequently, SFB enables a robust SEI, achieving exceptional Zn anode durability (7000 h), high‐rate capability (10 mA cm −2 ), and a high Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.8%. Full cells with SFB outperform controls in coin and pouch configurations. Given the rarity of additive(s) in OEs, this study offers a new path to boost stability and lifespan of non‐aqueous Zn batteries.

papers.title: Structural evolution of Li/Fe³⁺-doped forsterite (Mg2−2xLixFe³⁺xSiO₄) and the crystal-chemical viability of the LiFeSiO₄ olivine
papers.summary: Abstract The structural evolution of forsterite (Mg₂SiO₄) upon heterovalent coupled substitution with Li⁺ and Fe³⁺, forming the solid solution Mg(₂₋₂ₓ)LiₓFe³⁺ₓSiO₄, has been investigated up to 𝑥 ≈ 0.30. Single crystals were synthesized via high-temperature flux growth and characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Crystal structure refinements confirm a 2Mg²⁺ = Li⁺ + Fe³⁺ substitution, where Li⁺ occupies the smaller, less distorted M 1 octahedron, while Fe³⁺ occupies the larger M 2 octahedron, in agreement with charge-balance and bond-valence constraints. This substitution induces a linear contraction of the unit-cell volume, driven primarily by a decrease in the c -parameter, while concurrently causing a systematic expansion of the M 1 octahedron and a contraction of the M 2 octahedron. All measured structural parameters— such as mean bond distances, polyhedral volumes, and distortion indices—vary linearly with composition, indicating a continuous virtual solid solution up to x = 1.00. Extrapolation of the trends and subsequent Distance Least-Squares modelling predict a structurally viable atomic arrangement for the hypothetical LiFe³⁺SiO₄ endmember, which is crystal-chemically feasible as well as comparable to the known LiScSiO₄ olivine-type structure. These findings address conflicting literature reports by demonstrating that the olivine structure can accommodate the complete Li⁺ + Fe³⁺ ↔ 2Mg²⁺ substitution, thereby supporting the potential of LiFeSiO₄-type compounds as candidate cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Low-valence & large-radius cation doping strategy of TiNb2O7 for ultra-high rate anode material
Influence of 6‐Trifluoromethyluracil Versus Chloride Counterions in the Properties of Bis‐(1,10‐Phenanthroline)chloridecopper(II) Motif: Spectroscopic and In Vitro Biological Activity Assays
papers.summary: Copper(II) metallonucleases have emerged as a promising class of compounds to serve as alternatives to the platinum drugs. Here, we evaluated how different counterions, 6‐trifluoromethyluracil (6tfmu) and chloride, impact the biological activity of copper(II) complexes containing the bis‐(1,10‐phenanthroline)chloridecopper(II) motif. Compounds were characterized by chemical and spectroscopic measurements. Crystallographic studies were conducted for [Cu(phen) 2 Cl]6tfmu (1), while data from complex [Cu(phen) 2 Cl]Cl (2) were previously described. In vitro antiproliferative assays demonstrated that both complexes exhibited lower IC 50 values than cisplatin, with melanoma A375 cells as the most sensitive, being 1.3 and 0.9 µM 1 and 2, respectively. Both compounds bind DNA to an indistinguishable extent, through a hybrid mode combining minor‐groove recognition with partial intercalation of a single phenanthroline ligand. Molecular dynamics performed on the common [Cu(phen) 2 Cl] + cation and microplate fluorophore assays converge on this mode. The main reactive oxygen species generated by complexes 1 and 2 were ·OH and H 2 O 2 , respectively. Substrate depletion assays in a human Topoisomerase‐I‐mediated DNA relaxation experiment indicated the preference of the [Cu(phen) 2 ] 2+ motif for degrading the DNA substrate over directly inhibiting the enzyme itself. The counterion modulates antibacterial potency and identity of the dominant reactive species, while leaving DNA recognition by the shared cation essentially unchanged.
authors: Fernanda V. P. de V. Azevedo

papers.title: Toward Predictive Modeling of Layered‐Oxide Cathodes in Na‐Ion Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Layered Na x TMO 2 transition‐metal oxides are among the most promising cathodes for Na‐ion batteries, yet their predictive computational modeling remains intrinsically challenging. Their electrochemical behavior emerges from a delicate interplay between multivalent redox chemistry, structural flexibility, configurational disorder, and kinetic evolution during cycling. In this perspective, we provide a methodology‐centered overview of the main theoretical challenges associated with modeling these materials and discuss practical strategies to bridge electronic accuracy and structural/chemical complexity. We first examine the capabilities and limitations of density functional theory (DFT) in describing cationic and anionic redox processes, highlighting the role of self‐interaction error and the complementary use of DFT+U and hybrid functionals. We then address the explicit treatment of configurational disorder, emphasizing special quasi‐random structures (SQS) and antisite defect modeling as essential tools to capture entropy‐driven stabilization in realistic local environments. Finally, we discuss the interplay between thermodynamics and kinetics in Na intercalation, connecting voltage calculations, ion diffusion barriers and phase‐transition pathways described via NEB methods. Rather than advocating a single best technique, we argue that predictive modeling of Na‐ion cathodes requires integrated multiscale frameworks in which electronic‐structure methods, statistical sampling, and emerging machine‐learning potentials operate synergistically. In this evolving landscape, DFT‐based first‐principles calculations remain the indispensable foundation for transforming atomistic insights into rational materials discovery.

papers.title: Structural and functional tuning of carbon-supported NiMo hydrogen evolution reaction electrocatalysts for anion exchange membrane water electrolysis
papers.summary: s NiMo/C electrocatalyst (EC) can be a promising alternative to scarce and overpriced platinum group metals (PGMs) for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). However, resolving the optimal Ni-to-Mo ratio and understanding how the carbon support helps develop a suitable electrocatalytic architecture remain unclear. Therefore, two EC series with varying Ni-to-Mo ratios, supported over two different carbon substrates, i.e., Vulcan and Ketjenblack (KJB), were developed and thoroughly investigated. Structural characterizations via X-ray diffraction and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) highlighted that initially the Mo tended to substitute within the host nickel’s FCC lattice; however, increasing the Mo content led to the enhanced formation of bulk oxide phases, whereas different morphological makeovers were observed for both Vulcan- and KJB-based samples through the scanning transmission electron microscope. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated the highest Ni 2+ /Ni 0 ratio in Ni70Mo30/KJB; however, in both sample series, further increasing the Mo content led to a progressive enrichment of surface MoO₃, causing decay of HER performance. In the same samples, operando XAS specified beneficial Mo dissolution-redeposition while maintaining the Ni sites, primarily in a metallic state during HER, with limited and reversible hydroxide formation predominantly in the electrochemically active α-Ni(OH) 2 in the HER regime. The highest half-cell HER activity was achieved at a Ni: Mo ratio of 70:30, particularly with Ni70Mo30/KJB requiring an overpotential of only 119.6 mV. Eventually, when tested in AEMWE operating at 80 ºC with a NiFe 2 O 4 anode, it realized a current density of 3.82 A cm -2 at 2.2 V along with excellent operational durability.

papers.title: Longitudinal and Transverse Thermoelectric Properties in Topological Quantum Materials
papers.summary: Thermoelectric materials can be topologically trivial or non-trivial, enabling reversible interconversion of heat and electricity using a solid-state technology. Incidentally, few of the first experimentally discovered 3D topological materials, namely, Bi, Sb, Sn and Pb-based chalcogenides, were long known as good thermoelectric materials. In these compounds, the heavy atoms that give rise to strong spin-orbit coupling often become essential for band inversion and non-trivial band topology. They lead to low lattice thermal conductivity, linearly dispersing Dirac-like bands induce high electrical mobility, and a band-inverted electronic structure with multiple band extrema gives rise to high Seebeck coefficients. In materials, where the applied temperature gradient induces electrical voltage (Seebeck effect) in the same direction, they are termed as longitudinal thermoelectrics. On the other hand, when the generated electrical voltage and applied thermal current remain orthogonal to each other, the materials are termed as transverse thermoelectrics. The transverse response can be driven by an additional external magnetic field (ordinary Nernst effect), intrinsic remanent magnetisation, or non-zero Berry curvature of a material, which arises from their non-trivial topology (anomalous Nernst effect). We discuss another class of quantum materials, known as goniopolar materials, that exhibit axis-dependent conduction polarity and hence transverse thermoelectric effects, which are based on mechanisms of longitudinal thermoelectric properties. In this review, we cover both types of thermoelectricity, focusing on materials that possess non-trivial topological order. We make connections between their structures, topology and transport properties and suggest tunability of thermoelectric properties going beyond conventional mechanisms such as electron-phonon interactions.

papers.title: Anomalous thermal transport in isotope-enriched germanium carbide
papers.summary: Advances in modern electronics demand the dissipation of heat fluxes approaching 1000 W cm$^{-2}$, which drives an urgent need for materials with thermal conductivity ($κ$) exceeding 1000 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. Here, by solving the Boltzmann transport equation considering both three- and four-phonon interactions, we observe that isotopically pure cubic germanium carbide (GeC) exhibits a remarkable $κ$ of 1018 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is further corroborated by state-of-the-art machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations. Two unique mechanisms underlie this anomalously high $κ$: a remarkably strong isotopic enhancement effect (289%) and a surprisingly modest suppression due to four-phonon scattering (22%)-despite the presence of a wide acoustic-optical phonon gap. Moreover, we find that GeC defies the conventional Leibfried-Schlomann formula and exhibits a non-monotonic variation of $κ$ with external hydrostatic pressure at elevated temperatures. Our findings establish isotope-enriched GeC as a material of ultrahigh $κ$ and an ideal platform for exploring exotic phonon physics.

papers.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
papers.summary: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations show that this Si layer opens new channels for phonon transport across the interface. The engineered interface raises the interfacial thermal conductance to 165 MW m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$ -- the highest value yet reported for $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC interfaces. These results offer an effective way to manage heat in $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ devices and point to a general approach for building phonon-bridging interfaces that improve heat dissipation in heterogeneous systems.

papers.title: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals
papers.summary: The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $σ_h$. For electronic states of mirror parity $s_n(\mathbf{k})$ and $s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})$, and a phonon mode of parity $χ_ν(\mathbf{q})$, we show that the e-ph matrix element $g_{mn,ν}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})$ vanishes identically unless $s_n(\mathbf{k})\,χ_ν(\mathbf{q})\, s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})=+1$. The rule follows from the covariance of the phonon-induced deformation potential under $σ_h$, constitutes the $C_s$ case of the general group-theoretical selection rule for matrix elements, and partitions the e-ph interaction throughout the Brillouin zone into symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden scattering channels. Consequently, mirror-even phonons couple electronic states of the same mirror parity, either even--even or odd--odd, whereas mirror-odd phonons couple only states of opposite mirror parity, for both intra- and interband processes. We illustrate the selection rule through first-principles calculations for the two-dimensional superconductor $\mathrm{Sc_2BCH_4}$, where mirror parity is well defined throughout the entire Brillouin zone and symmetry-forbidden matrix elements vanish up to numerical precision. We then extend the analysis to bulk $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, where the rule applies exactly only on mirror-invariant planes of the three-dimensional Brillouin zone. Moving away from these planes removes the exact mirror constraint and activates scattering channels that are symmetry forbidden when the mirror eigenvalues are well defined. Our results establish horizontal mirror symmetry as an exact and practical filter of e-ph scattering processes.

papers.title: Ferron polariton Hall effect: Deflecting optically rectified polarization with magnetic fields
papers.summary: Ferrons are elementary excitations of ferroelectric order that can propagate and transport polarization when excited with light. Here, we show theoretically that ferron polaritons exhibit a Hall effect: an applied magnetic field generates polarization transport perpendicular to the propagation direction of a ferron polariton excited by an incident terahertz pulse. We demonstrate this effect for the example of ferroelectric SnTe using first-principles calculations and a microscopic theory of the phonon-polariton current. The direction and magnitude of the transverse polarization transport can be controlled by the polarization of the terahertz pulse and the applied magnetic field. Our results establish a route toward light-controlled directional transport of electric polarization in ferroelectrics.

papers.title: greenWTE: Frequency-domain solver for the phonon Wigner Transport Equation with arbitrary heating using Green's functions
papers.summary: Heat transport in solids is usually described in a phenomenological way via Fourier's law. However, at small time and length scales in low thermal conductivity materials, a microscopic description is needed. This is traditionally done by invoking the phonon Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE), which has been successful in describing transport in high thermal conductivity materials. Recently, a generalization of the BTE, the Wigner Transport Equation, was developed to be able to microscopically describe transport in low thermal conductivity materials by taking into account not only phonon scattering processes but also phonon tunneling processes, so-called coherences. We present a Python package that solves the Wigner Transport Equation (WTE) in spatial and temporal Fourier space for arbitrary source terms, thereby enabling the study of heat transport at small space and time scales. This allows one to compute both static and dynamic thermal conductivities from bulk to nanoscale. Beyond that, it can be used to study the response of phonon systems in materials to arbitrary heat sources.

papers.title: Gravitational anomaly spectroscopy of a Kitaev spin liquid
papers.summary: The chiral central charge $c$ measures the gravitational anomaly of a two-dimensional topological phase and fixes the heat current along its edge. It has been accessed through thermal transport, where phonons complicate the signal, or through wave-function probes that need a pure ground state. Here we show that a calibrated combination of directional edge absorption weights determines $c$. A modulation of the edge couplings that travels along the edge is absorbed according to the Virasoro algebra, and a static change of the same couplings measures the unknown probe normalization. Two harmonics then cancel the dependence on the edge state, so the estimator returns $c$ in any state of the ideal edge theory. A ratio of line weights with and without a vison gives the conformal spin of the Ising anyon. For the Kitaev honeycomb model, exact calculations recover $c=1/2$ and $h_σ=1/16$ to $10^{-5}$ and give $c$ within about $1\%$ on 96 spins. Compiled into gate circuits on the physical spins of a square-lattice quantum simulator, the protocol returns $c$ within $5\%$ on 48 qubits. For stochastic gate errors it requires two-qubit error rates of $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-5}$.

papers.title: Roadmap Challenges and Opportunities in 2D Materials: An Indian Perspective
papers.summary: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) materials (Graphene, 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (MX 2 ), hBN) have emerged as exciting materials for discovering novel physical phenomena, and have great potential for electronic and optoelectronic devices, as well as energy and catalysis applications. Further, materials such as Cr 2 X 2 Te 6 (X = Si, Ge), VSe 2 , Fe 3 GeTe 2 , CrX 3 (X = Cl, Br, I) and MPX 3 (M = Mn, Fe, V, Zn, Co, Ni, Cd, Mg; X = S, Se) have emerged as fascinating platforms for 2D magnetism. The heterostructures of these 2D materials, and the twist angle between layers are opening new possibilities of studying the effect of Moiré potential, exotic topological phases, magnetic-proximity effects, and strong correlations. At the same time, the research is leading towards many application-based directions such as in excitonics, valleytronics, straintronics, and quantum technologies. In this context, growth of novel 2D materials and heterostructures, as well as large scale growth becomes critically important. This roadmap aims to provide a comprehensive overview of 2D materials research in India and across the globe. The roadmap is broadly divided into six themes: 1. Topology in 2D Materials, Magnetism, Exotic Physics and Emergent Phenomena; 2. Moiré Physics in 2D Heterostructures; 3. Excitonic Physics and Optical properties, including Defects; 4. Transport Phenomena in 2D Materials; 5. 2D Materials Synthesis and Growth; and 6. 2D Materials Electrical Devices and Applications. This roadmap highlights the cutting edge-research being done by Indian and global researchers, emphasizes the challenges, and suggests possible technological solutions.

papers.title: Flexible and stretchable strain sensors: from conductive materials to emerging applications
papers.summary: The escalating necessity for versatile, soft-body electronics has catalyzed the development of stretchable and wearable strain sensors. These devices play a pivotal role in various domains, ranging from biomechanical motion tracking and physiological health monitoring to advanced human-machine interactions and soft robotic systems. This review systematically examines the latest technological strides in fabricating flexible strain-sensing platforms, elucidating the fundamental principle of transforming mechanical strain into measurable electrical outputs. We provide a comprehensive analysis of diverse substrate matrices and the integration of various nanomaterials. Crucially, this paper explores the underlying physics of sensing, specifically focusing on disconnection, tunneling, and crack propagation mechanisms. Additionally, a comparative evaluation of key performance metrics—including sensitivity, linearity, stretchability, hysteresis, and dynamic stability—is presented. The discussion concludes with an overview of the transformative potential of these sensors in future technological landscapes.

papers.title: Why strong spin-orbit coupling does not destabilize the Dirac spin liquid in the Yb delafossites
papers.summary: The Yb delafossites NaYbSe$_2$, KYbSe$_2$, CsYbSe$_2$ and NaYbO$_2$ are candidates for the U(1) Dirac spin liquid (DSL) of the triangular lattice. Strong spin-orbit coupling gives their exchange an XXZ anisotropy $Δ$ and bond-dependent couplings $J_{\pm\pm}$, $J_{z\pm}$ that lock the spin frame to the lattice. We show that, within a single layer of a stable Heisenberg DSL, these couplings generate no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator of their own. Inversion at the bond centers removes the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya channel that gaps the kagome DSL, so the locked symmetry forbids a mass, density or current at any order and, assuming continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. Every Lorentz-scalar four-fermion operator induced by spin-orbit coupling shares an SU(4) multiplet, and hence its scaling dimension, with a Heisenberg-allowed one, and the nine non-scalar quartics without such a partner arise only at second order and are irrelevant at large $N$. The Heisenberg DSL itself allows a Lorentz-vector quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, which a stable phase must also render irrelevant. Beyond a single layer, spin-orbit coupling opens an interlayer monopole channel in rhombohedral stacking. If the Heisenberg DSL is instead multicritical, an anisotropy as small as that of KYbSe$_2$ matters only below tens of mK. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, and exact diagonalization indicates that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not yet fix the K-point exponent, and gapless out-of-plane spin fluctuations at the K point would test the chiral-Ising selection.

papers.title: Altermagnetism-induced higher-order topological Dirac semimetals in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems
papers.summary: We propose an altermagnetism-induced route to a two-dimensional higher-order topological Dirac semimetal in a trilayer nonsymmorphic Dirac system. Interlayer hybridization preserves the nonsymmorphic bulk Dirac crossings and generates helical edge states in the trilayer phase. Introducing outer-layer $d$-wave altermagnetic order gaps the helical edge states, while only the symmetry-protected Dirac crossing at high-symmetry point $M$ remains gapless. The resulting phase hosts a surviving bulk Dirac point, gapped edge spectra, and corner states. An exact layer-space decomposition further reveals that these features arise from the coexistence of a gapless Dirac sector and a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological sector. Our results establish altermagnetism as an effective mechanism for engineering higher-order topological Dirac semimetals in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems.

papers.title: Bottom‐Stack Shear Transfer in Thin‐Film Flexoelectric Measurements
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Bending‐based measurements are widely used to probe flexoelectricity in ferroelectric thin films, but the measured response is often shaped by mechanical boundary conditions beyond the intrinsic flexoelectric coefficient. Here we show that the conducting bottom stack acts as a hidden electromechanical boundary condition in mica‐supported BaTiO 3 (BTO) capacitors. Dynamic bending measurements reveal opposite bottom‐layer‐thickness dependences for two‐dimensional and oxide electrodes, while a BTO(001)/LSMO(001)/MoS 2 /mica hybrid exhibits an intermediate response at the same nominal BTO orientation as the MoS 2 ‐supported films. Interface‐resolved first‐principles calculations show that the hybrid retains a stiff BTO/LSMO contact above substantially more compliant LSMO/MoS 2 and MoS 2 /mica junctions. A reduced shear‐transfer model combines the local interface stiffnesses into an effective interfacial‐path stiffness, and finite‐element simulations confirm progressive suppression of interfacial slip with increasing tangential stiffness. These results identify the complete bottom‐stack shear‐transfer pathway as a mechanical control of bending‐induced polarization and piezoelectric admixture in ferroelectric thin‐film flexoelectric measurements.

papers.title: Resonantly interacting $2e/3$ anyons: a controlled microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity
papers.summary: We develop a microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity that connects electronic interactions in a lightly doped Laughlin state to the universal physics of a resonantly interacting anyon gas. Using geometric quantization of Laughlin quasiholes, we derive the effective many-body Hamiltonian of dilute charge-$2e/3$ anyons, including their valley structure, dispersion, and statistical and short-range interactions, together with an explicit map between anyon and electron observables. This reduces the dilute many-body problem to a few parameters fixed by data computable from few anyon numerics. In analogy with resonant Fermi and Bose gases, we organize the dilute anyon problem around a two-body binding resonance and its relevant and marginal perturbations. For a three-valley gas of charge-$2e/3$ anyons, we identify a resonance whose long-distance theory is governed by an Aharonov-Casher anyon Hamiltonian whose magnetic field is the statistical Chern-Simons field and whose ground state is exactly solvable. Using the ground state wavefunction, we demonstrate Cooper-pair off-diagonal long-range order directly in electron coordinates and determine the pairing symmetry and vortex-lattice structure. The leading perturbations at the fixed point are a relevant pair detuning and a marginal three-body contact in the valley-singlet channel, which determine the compressibility and sound velocity. A repulsive three-body coupling is marginally irrelevant, allowing the fixed point to control a parametrically broad dilute regime near pair resonance, while attractive three-body interactions instead generate charge-$2e$ trimers. More broadly, our results show that binding thresholds between competing anyon composites host universal resonant regimes that are not captured by the lowest-energy anyon species alone, providing a new setting for controlled theories of anyon matter.

papers.title: Asymptotic electromagnetic transition conditions for thin layers: the arithmetic-mean field and susceptibility hybridization
papers.summary: Effective transition conditions that replace a thin polarizable layer by a zero-thickness sheet are commonly applied in electromagnetic models of two-dimensional (2D) materials and metasurfaces. These conditions usually take the arithmetic mean of the fields on either side as the polarizing field at the boundary, and characterize the layer by the $0^\mathrm{th}$ moment of its susceptibility, but both choices are typically imposed rather than derived. We derive transition conditions for a finite-thickness, in-plane homogeneous, in-plane isotropic layer with a general nonlocal susceptibility, using a single-scale asymptotic expansion in $η= l\max(k_0,q)$, where $l$ is the layer thickness, $k_0$ the free-space wavenumber and $q$ the in-plane wavenumber. The sheet limit must be taken after resumming the out-of-plane depolarizing field, as this ensures that the resulting sheet susceptibility is independent of the material thickness. The arithmetic mean then emerges as the leading-order polarizing field for general susceptibility profiles. Asymmetries in the layer profile modify the effective susceptibility appearing in the transition conditions, rather than altering the arithmetic-mean field prescription. If the spatial profile is not even in both out-of-plane coordinates, in-plane and out-of-plane response hybridize, turning the diagonal volumetric susceptibility into a $q$-dependent effective tensor surface susceptibility with off-diagonal components. Mirror symmetry alone does not remove this hybridization. Comparison with exact solutions for local and separable layers shows that the derived conditions remain accurate to $O(η)$ across propagating and evanescent excitations, whereas the standard sheet conditions fail once hybridization becomes appreciable.

papers.title: When are Two‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks Good Electrodes for Lithium Ion Batteries? A Data‐Driven Analysis
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are emerging as sustainable organic electrode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries. Despite more than a decade of research, existing heuristics for designing electroactive COFs lack generality, and the suitability of these materials as alternatives to conventional electrodes remains poorly resolved. Here, we map structure–electrode–function relationships across 1099 experimentally synthesized 2D COFs from the CoRE COF database by developing a data‐driven framework integrating density‐functional theory computations with machine learning models and establishing atomic‐level design rules governing electrode behavior. We uncover that cathode‐like character originates from dense, multidentate nitrogen and oxygen rich coordination pockets at pore walls, characteristic of imide, acylhydrazones, keto–amine linkages, and π‐macrocycles, whereas anode‐like behavior is encoded by spatially separated redox sites and π‐rich interlayer galleries that sustain weak, reversible Li + intercalation. Sequential voltage, capacity, and conductivity‐based screening across the database yields 14 anode and 14 cathode candidates. We show that the known chemical space of 2D COFs cannot outperform inorganic electrodes in terms of operating voltages. However, strategic pairing of 2D anode|cathode pairs within an all‐organic lithium battery architecture delivers full‐cell voltages exceeding 2 V with capacities above 200 mAh g −1 on both electrodes, surpassing small organic molecules and polymer counterparts.

papers.title: Structural evolution of Li/Fe³⁺-doped forsterite (Mg2−2xLixFe³⁺xSiO₄) and the crystal-chemical viability of the LiFeSiO₄ olivine
papers.summary: Abstract The structural evolution of forsterite (Mg₂SiO₄) upon heterovalent coupled substitution with Li⁺ and Fe³⁺, forming the solid solution Mg (2-2x) Li x Fe³⁺ x SiO₄, has been investigated up to ≈ 0.30. Single crystals were synthesized via high-temperature flux growth and characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Crystal structure refinements confirm a 2Mg²⁺ = Li⁺ + Fe³⁺ substitution, where Li⁺ occupies the smaller, less distorted M 1 octahedron, while Fe³⁺ occupies the larger M 2 octahedron, in agreement with charge-balance and bond-valence constraints. This substitution induces a linear contraction of the unit-cell volume, driven primarily by a decrease in the c -parameter, while concurrently causing a systematic expansion of the M 1 octahedron and a contraction of the M 2 octahedron. All measured structural parameters— such as mean bond distances, polyhedral volumes, and distortion indices—vary linearly with composition, indicating a continuous virtual solid solution up to x = 1.00. Extrapolation of the trends and subsequent Distance Least-Squares modelling predict a structurally viable atomic arrangement for the hypothetical LiFe³⁺SiO₄ endmember, which is crystal-chemically feasible as well as comparable to the known LiScSiO₄ olivine-type structure. These findings address conflicting literature reports by demonstrating that the olivine structure can accommodate the complete Li⁺ + Fe³⁺ ↔ 2Mg²⁺ substitution, thereby supporting the potential of LiFeSiO₄-type compounds as candidate cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Electronic Structure Engineering Enables Dynamic Interfacial Adaptation of Zinc Anodes
papers.summary: ABSTRACT In aqueous zinc‐ion batteries, Zn plating/stripping is accompanied by continuous evolution of the local electric field, solvation structure, and interfacial chemical environment. Therefore, conventional electrolyte additives that rely on fixed adsorption or static interfacial layer construction are insufficient for sustained interfacial regulation. Herein, we propose an electronic structure regulation strategy that endows electrolyte additives with dynamic interfacial adaptability through molecular engineering. Using pyrrolidone derivatives as model molecules, we demonstrate that vinyl functionalization strengthens π‐electron delocalization and enhances the polarization response of N ‐vinyl‐2‐pyrrolidone (NVP). Such electronically adaptive behavior allows NVP to respond to the evolving local interfacial environment via electronic redistribution, thereby adaptively modulating the Zn/electrolyte interface while simultaneously optimizing interfacial Zn 2+ solvation, water distribution, and Zn deposition behavior. Consequently, the ZSO+NVP electrolyte enables a Zn//Zn symmetric cell to operate stably for over 4000 h at 10 mA cm −2 , while the Zn//NH 4 V 4 O 10 full cell delivers 92.6% capacity retention after 1500 cycles at 2 A g −1 . This work reveals the critical role of additive electronic responsiveness in stabilizing dynamic Zn/electrolyte interfaces.

papers.title: In Situ Intercalation Polymerization Fabrication of Polyaniline/Graphene Composites via Supercritical CO2 Assistance: Toward High-Performance Supercapacitor Electrodes
papers.summary: Abstract Polyaniline/graphene (PANI/GR) composites are promising supercapacitor electrode candidates owing to its excellent electrochemical performance such as high theoretical specific capacity and good electrical conductivity. However, most reported ones suffer structural defects, leading to low specific energy and poor electrochemical stability. This work proposed a novel method to fabricate PANI/GR nanocomposite for supercapacitor. By synergizing supercritical fluid technology (SFT) and aniline cation (AN + ) intercalation, AN + realized effective intercalation and in-situ polymerization between graphite layers with assistance of supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO₂), enabling layer-by-layer assemble of PANI and GR (named SC). It is found that the layer structure of SC reduces PANI deformation, facilitates rapid ion diffusion, and extende interfacial interactions, therefore accelerating electron transfer throughout the electrode. The SC electrode achieves an exceptional specific capacitance of 669.0 F g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹, with merely 7.5% capacitance loss after 5,000 cycles, demonstrating outstanding cycling stability. The corresponding SC//activated carbon asymmetric supercapacitor delivers an energy density of 29.2 Wh kg⁻¹ at a power density of 650 W kg⁻¹. This work provides an effective strategy for designing layered graphene-based energy storage composites to achieve superior electrochemical performances.

papers.title: Synthesis of Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBenes in Molten Salts From Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives
papers.summary: ABSTRACT The unique properties and application possibilities of two‐dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti 2 InB 2 with ZnCl 2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBene. Upon etching, indium atoms are completely removed from the precursor and replaced by chlorine surface terminations with a coverage of 1.1 < x < 1.4. Further, in situ x‐ray diffraction indicates a direct biphasic transformation from Ti 2 InB 2 to ml‐MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml‐MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A‐element substitution into the 3D Ti 2 ZnB 2 phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li‐ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.

papers.title: Anion Engineering Enables Concurrent Optimization of Phonon and Carrier Transport in AMg$_2$X$_2$ Zintl Thermoelectrics
papers.summary: The simultaneous suppression of lattice heat transport and enhancement of carrier transport is central to the development of high-performance thermoelectric materials. Here, we investigate the microscopic mechanisms governing phonon and carrier transport in CaAl$_2$Si$_2$-type AMg$_2$X$_2$ (A = Ca, Sr, Ba; X = P, As, Sb, Bi) Zintl compounds using first-principles calculations, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and Boltzmann transport theory. As X changes from P to Bi, the widening phonon band gap restricts three-phonon scattering channels and increases the relative importance of four-phonon processes. In CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ and BaMg$_2$Bi$_2$, four-phonon scattering dominates the relaxation of low-frequency heat-carrying modes at 900 K. The Bi-based series also exhibits an anomalous increase in lattice thermal conductivity from Ca to Ba despite the increasing cation mass. Mode-resolved analysis links the lower thermal conductivity of CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ to reduced low-frequency group velocities and stronger anharmonic scattering, with Ca-related mid-frequency vibrations providing additional four-phonon scattering channels. Including both particle-like and coherent contributions, its lattice thermal conductivity reaches 0.23 W$\cdot$m$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$ at 900 K. Meanwhile, the increasing covalent character of the vertical Mg-X bonds is accompanied by enhanced band-edge dispersion and reduced carrier effective masses. These electronic changes, together with conduction-band convergence, favor n-type transport and yield a predicted peak $ZT$ of 3.68 at 900 K in CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$. These results elucidate the interplay of phonon spectral structure and higher-order anharmonicity in thermal transport, alongside the distinct electronic response to anion substitution.

papers.title: Phonon Angular Momentum Multipoles and Nonlinear Thermal Responses
papers.summary: Chiral phonons carry angular momentum and couple lattice dynamics to magnetic and transport phenomena. In magnets, however, a systematic classification of momentum-space phonon angular momentum (PAM) textures and experimental signatures of the resulting thermal responses remain elusive. Here we classify the PAM textures for all 122 magnetic point groups (MPGs) using two equivalent approaches: directly solving the linear symmetry constraints on the multipole expansion coefficients and constructing the allowed textures from group-representation basis functions. Both methods yield the same fivefold classification according to the leading nonzero order: $s$-wave (monopole), $p$-wave (dipole), $d$-wave (quadrupole), $f$-wave (octupole), and $g$-wave (hexadecapole). We further show that a temperature gradient generates a nonequilibrium PAM density whose $n$th-order term in $\nabla T$ contains an energy-weighted PAM $2^n$-pole tensor and a kinematic remainder, thereby linking the response order and partial-wave channel through exact selection rules. Because the Berry curvature obeys the same symmetry constraints, this taxonomy is in one-to-one correspondence with Berry-curvature multipoles and their nonlinear Hall responses. We propose a cantilever torque measurement whose allowed angular harmonics are fixed by the MPG, with period $2π/n$ for a pure $n$th harmonic, providing a direct probe of the partial-wave content of PAM in both nonmagnetic and magnetic materials.

papers.title: Ab Initio strain-dependent vibrational analysis of different silicene structures for 2D devices
papers.summary: We report first-principles phonon dynamics studies in isotropically strained mono-layer silicene films of various topologies by density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory methods. The strain introduced in the sheets are of both tensile and compressive nature and its effect on the thermal transport properties are analysed using the Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE) reported. We performed electronic and vibrational analysis of each silicene topology and concluded that hhk-silicene is a potential candidate for next generation electro-thermal devices due its molecular stability, bulk-Si like bandgap and tolerable thermal performance that can be engineered by strain. The novel hhk-silicene topology offers excellent thermal and electronic capabilities that are sensitive to strain along with the band gap following a near-linear monotonically decreasing trend making it suitable for strain-tronics applications.

papers.title: Ultrathin and efficient wearable EMI shields with integrated self-powered sensing and information coding
papers.summary: Abstract Developing ultrathin and robust high-performance electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials with multifunctional integration for wearable electronics is imperative yet remains challenging. Here, we report a bioinspired versatile and wearable MXene/cellulose nanofiber-silver nanowire (MXene/CNF-AgNW) composite film with superior mechanical strength, high-efficiency EMI shielding and integrated self-powered sensing capabilities. The film achieves superior mechanical robustness with a high tensile strength reaching 315 MPa through a multiscale reinforcement strategy that combines hybrid sandwich and nacre-like structures. The sandwiched AgNWs with MXene/CNF-based shells impart the composite film with high electrical conductivity and excellent EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SE) reaching 62 dB for a tiny thickness of 23 μm, corresponding to an outstanding specific EMI SE (SSE/t) of 16550 dB·cm2·g-1, together with remarkable electrothermal conversion capability. Furthermore, the flexible and antibacterial film can also serve as wearable electronic skin with self-powered sensing for human activity monitoring and information coding. Notably, by integrating a machine learning algorithm, the system can enable intelligent handwriting recognition with an accuracy of 100%, establishing an advanced communication interface. This work provides a facile multiscale engineering strategy for constructing multifunctional composite films that seamlessly integrate protection, perception, and communication functionalities for next-generation smart wearable electronic applications.

papers.title: Writing with Near-Field: towards Atomic Resolution in Material Processing
papers.summary: Direct laser writing with ultra-short pulses is the most flexible route to two- and three-dimensional (2D/3D) material modification, yet its resolution is judged against the optical diffraction limit. This review argues the opposite: the finest, most reproducible modifications come not from shortening the wavelength but from localising the absorber. Through the threshold effect and a transient epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) state - the dielectric-to-metal (Die-Met) state of the excited solid - the deposited energy is confined to a dipole-like nano-seed whose near-field intensity falls as r^-6 (ideal point dipole). The localisation is thus set by the seed size, not the focal wavelength, and the final feature is shaped by the material response: post-pulse heat flow, cavitation and quenching. We show that polarisation controls the anisotropy of deposition: the quasi-static near-field and interface boundary conditions select the writing direction and the modification orientation, down to a single defect. We survey energy-deposition mechanisms from 100 nm to the single-nanometer scale and link them to working engineering: stitch-free large-area patterning and record aspect-ratio (10^3-10^4) dicing and wafering of transparent crystals. Finally, we conjecture guided volumetric deposition, in which laser-inscribed lossy nano-seeds act as antennas that let cavity microwaves anneal the modified nano-volumes from within, as a 2.45 GHz oven heats food through water-dipole absorption. Throughout, atomic resolution is used in a quantum-confined sense and denotes a direction of travel: 10-20 nm features are demonstrated, while deterministic single-defect and single-bond modification remain goals. The thesis is that ultrafast direct write beats diffraction-limited intuition because the material itself forms a transient nanoscale absorber whose near-field and boundary conditions govern energy deposition.

papers.title: Electrically tunable moiré hybridization in scalable twist-with-a-spacer structures
papers.summary: Moiré superlattices emerge from the interplay between interlayer hybridization and long-wavelength periodicity, both set by the twist angle between layers in direct contact. Here we show that moiré minibands and pronounced Brown-Zak oscillations persist even when twisted graphene layers are separated by an atomically thin spacer, such as a misaligned graphene monolayer. This twist-with-a-spacer architecture reduces interlayer coupling, such that moiré hybridization can be tuned with a modest displacement field without changing moiré periodicity, allowing us to disentangle the roles of those parameters in miniband formation. Importantly, the spacer suppresses atomic relaxation, enabling highly uniform, rigid superlattices at twist angles down to ~0.1 degree. This robustness allows twist-with-a-spacer structures to be grown directly by scalable chemical vapour deposition (CVD): devices fabricated from CVD-grown structures exhibit the same moiré physics phenomena as those assembled manually. Our work provides insights into the physics of moiré bandstructure formation and opens a route towards scalable moiré systems.

papers.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
papers.summary: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

papers.title: Quantum Dipolar Magnon Drag in Conducting Magnetic Bilayers
papers.summary: We predict electrical drag between two electrically isolated metallic ferromagnets mediated by quantum dipolar magnon coupling. A charge current in one layer generates a nonequilibrium magnon current whose momentum is transferred across an insulating spacer through interlayer dipolar interactions. The resulting magnon current in the passive layer produces a measurable voltage through electron-magnon scattering. We show the combination of resonant quantum momentum transfer and magnetic tunability through the control of magnetization configurations distinguish quantum dipolar drag from conventional drag mechanism.

papers.title: Synchronization and Spatiotemporal Phases in Driven Precessing Domain Walls
papers.summary: The dynamics of extended magnetic domain walls driven by constant and alternating magnetic fields are studied using a collective coordinate $u$-$φ$ model. While purely constant-field driven systems exhibit deterministic spatiotemporal chaos and roughening, the alternating component can lock the precessional frequency via Shapiro-like steps.
