Using linear stability analysis and Floquet theory, the phase boundaries of stable, synchronized flat wall states are mapped. By studying the nonlinear dynamics of the extended system, a rich phase diagram is identified, composed of five dynamical regimes characterized by the combination of domain wall spatial order (flat, rough, or periodic) and domain wall precession temporal order (pinned, synchronized, or unsynchronized). Notably, the macroscopic temporal order of the synchronized phases can lead to a flat domain wall or to a periodic structure dominated by a narrow band of linearly unstable modes, both with coherent precession of the domain wall magnetization, while unsynchronized phases can be flat, with coherent precession, or rough with spatiotemporal chaos and incoherent precession.

papers.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
papers.summary: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. With our approach, we show that populating quantum dots does not require engineered reservoirs, source/drain bias, ohmic contacts, or in-situ doping. As a result, the number of gates can be kept minimal and the fabrication process can be simplified. Moreover, this approach can be applied to a wide range of direct-bandgap semiconductor quantum dot systems. This hybrid device demonstration is a first step towards a different scalability approach for quantum dot arrays.

papers.title: Covariance-dependent participation scaling of Comtet disorder on open hyperbolic lattices
papers.summary: Negative curvature makes the electrostatic Green function decay exponentially, producing a finite disorder-variance budget even as radial volume grows exponentially. We investigate whether this near-field concentration also determines wave-function participation on open hyperbolic lattices. A Gaussian control preserves the full one-site distribution of Comtet disorder at every vertex while removing its off-diagonal covariance. Complete-window participation ratios on $\{7,3\}$ graphs with $N=847,2240,5887$ yield an effective-exponent difference of $-0.028$ at $W/t=0.5$ and $+0.116$ at $W/t=3$; both signs persist upon extending to $N=15435$. Size-resolved squared-kernel radii lie near $2.45\ell$ on the larger graphs of this sequence, below the cutoff-matched continuum value $3.12\ell$. Distance-shell weights resolve the finite discrete measure associated with this shift, while higher participation moments and spacing ratios characterize the accompanying wave-function and spectral structure. A marginal-matched exponential-kernel family gives positive exponent contrasts at all five sampled kernel lengths at $W/t=0.5,3$, separating the Comtet response from a description based on the decay length alone. These results distinguish a concentrated variance budget from the covariance-dependent participation response of finite open hyperbolic systems.

papers.title: Artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice: a tricritical bridge from square to kagome
papers.summary: Artificial spin ices (ASIs) are arrays of interacting nanomagnets in which phase transitions can be imaged and controlled. Studies of the thermodynamic have focused mainly on the square and kagome lattices, and on their variants. Here we study artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice, formed of squares and octagons. At fixed lattice constant, the ratio $r$ of the square and octagon link lengths tunes the interactions strongly while changing the geometry only slightly. Magnetic force microscopy and Monte Carlo simulations show a continuous bridge from square-ice-like to kagome-like behavior. At small $r$ the system has a single ordering transition, whereas at large $r$ it passes from a correlated paramagnet to charge order and then long-range order. The two regimes meet in a multicritical region, accurately modeled by a Blume-Capel model of the octagon toroidal moments. From this picture, we design a comparative magnetometry protocol that unambiguously separates interaction effects from single-nanomagnet effects in thermally active samples. Finally, the charge-ordered region maps onto a tunable dimer model, with a Coulomb phase and pinch points along the line between two ordered dimer phases. The CaVO ASI thus provides access to a rich phase diagram only through geometric tuning, without requiring extreme experimental conditions.

papers.title: Quantum dynamics of ultrasmall magnetic skyrmions in atomic-defect landscapes
papers.summary: Magnetic skyrmions are prime candidates for future information technology, and their fate in devices is settled by the defects they encounter. In ultrathin films, skyrmions can be as small as a couple of nanometers, carrying only a few tens of magnetic moments, while atomic defects reshape their energy landscape on the atomic scale. Here, we demonstrate that such ultrasmall skyrmions can behave quantum mechanically and that their quantum dynamics is unusual. Since the gyrotropic force dominates, the two coordinates of a ferromagnetic skyrmion are canonically conjugate and the skyrmion behaves as a particle in the lowest Landau level of an effective magnetic field, with a magnetic length of 0.6~Å. Utilizing skyrmion-defect interaction profiles of Cr and Fe adatoms and dimers in PdFe/Ir(111), obtained from atomistic spin simulations parametrized from first principles, we unveil quantized gyrotropic orbits with level spacings of 20--85~$μ$eV, bound not only by pinning defects but also, counter-intuitively, by repulsive ones. Saddle points of the energy landscape act as quantum beam splitters for skyrmions, and quantum depinning reaches rates of 1--100~Hz below the critical current. Embedded impurities, in contrast, bind the skyrmion so strongly that it ceases to behave as a rigid particle, defining a strong-coupling regime. For the Gilbert damping typical of ultrathin films, the quantized levels remain well resolved. The thermal-to-quantum crossover lies between 40 and 160~mK, which is within reach of millikelvin scanning tunneling microscopy, where tip-induced escape statistics and electron spin resonance STM can reveal the quantized gyrotropic motion of skyrmions pinned at defects crafted atom by atom.

papers.title: Advances in electrode materials and interfacial chemistry of lithium-ion-based energy storage devices
papers.summary: Recently, lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) have emerged as a new energy-storage technology that combines the characteristics of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and supercapacitors. Their development has been driven by the growing demand for electrified transportation, stationary grid-storage systems, and portable electronic devices. In this review, recent advances in electrode materials and electrolyte chemistry, as well as interfacial phenomena for performance evaluation of LIBs and LICs, are discussed. Various carbon anodes and cathodes, transition metal oxides, phosphates, and chalcogenide-layered materials, as well as aqueous, nonaqueous, solid-state, and gel-polymer electrolytes used in LIBs and LICs are reviewed. Performance comparisons among electrode materials and full cells are presented, and the limitations of using metal electrodes, as well as strategies to improve them, are evaluated. The kinetic trade-off between the battery anode and the capacitor cathode, the balancing of electrode mass ratios, and the SEI/CEI interphases under high-voltage and high-rate regimes are considered in detail, along with recycling technologies and environmentally friendly synthesis routes for biomass-based electrode materials. Through systematic comparison of materials, mechanisms, performance, and degradation pathways, this review offers a practical approach to screening suitable electrode-electrolyte pairs for safer, more durable, and higher-performing future LIBs and LICs.

papers.title: MLi 2 Ti 6 O 14 (M = 2Na, Sr, Ba, Pb) Titanate Anodes for Hybrid Lithium‐Ion Capacitors
papers.summary: Abstract (Hybrid) lithium‐ion capacitors (LICs) form high‐power durable energy storage devices combining battery anode and capacitor cathode. Here, we demonstrate combustion synthesized carbon coated nanometric MLi 2 Ti 6 O 14 (M = 2Na, Sr, Ba, and Pb; MLTO) titanate anodes with flat voltage profiles (1.2–1.4 V) for the first time as intercalation anodes in asymmetric lithium‐ion capacitors vs activated carbon (AC). The MLTO‐LICs delivered an energy density and power density in the range of 10–45 Wh kg −1 and 0.5–1200 W kg −1 . Further, we show that the appearance of a voltage step in MLTO‐LICs is critical for understanding performance variations and explain this behavior using structural insights (rod packing) related to Li‐storage sites within MLTO and their evolution during cycling. Additionally, we identify different Li‐storage site types, migration pathways, and associated barriers, establishing how intrinsic material effects govern early‐cycle performance, while extrinsic factors become dominant during the later cycles. Overall, this work presents MLTO titanates as a new potential class of faradaic anodes for LICs.

papers.title: Transient structural evolution during electrochemical doping revealed by time‐aligned operando GIWAXS on organic mixed ionic electronic conductors
papers.summary: Abstract Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibit dynamic structural transformations during electrochemical doping, critically impacting device performance in applications such as bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing. While operando grazing‐incidence wide‐angle X‐ray scattering (GIWAXS) has emerged as a powerful tool to probe such changes, its temporal resolution remains fundamentally mismatched with the rapid ion dynamics in OMIECs, often obscuring transient microstructural states. Here, we introduce a time‐aligned operando GIWAXS methodology that bridges this gap by extending the electrochemical doping time constant through engineered device geometry. This enables real‐time tracking of structural evolution during abrupt doping conditions. Using poly(2‐(3,3′‐bis(2‐(2‐(2‐methoxyethoxy)ethoxy)ethoxy)‐[2,2′‐bithiophen]‐5‐yl)thieno[3,2‐b]thiophene) polymers with distinct molecular weights, we reveal that the microstructural response under abrupt biasing diverges significantly from that observed under conventional voltage‐sweeping conditions. Notably, abrupt doping induces intercalation pathways and reorientation behaviors not captured in quasi‐equilibrium measurements. Our approach provides direct insight into doping‐pathway‐dependent structural dynamics and offers a generalizable strategy for resolving rapid ion–polymer interactions in functional OMIEC systems. These findings highlight the importance of kinetic control in operando measurements and inform the rational design of mixed‐conducting polymer devices for transient or pulse‐driven applications. image

papers.title: Alleviating the stability-energy density dilemma via electron-donor-mediated orbital symmetry regulation in sodium phosphate cathodes
papers.summary: Manganese-based sodium super ionic conductor-type cathode materials, leveraging the multielectron redox activity of manganese, represent a promising pathway toward high-energy-density sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, the unavoidable generation of Mn 3+ (3d 4 ) species during charge-discharge processes, characterized by asymmetric e g orbital occupancy, triggers octahedral symmetry breaking. This inherent electronic structural instability creates a fundamental contradiction between achieving high energy density and ensuring long cycle life that remains inherently difficult to reconcile. Here, we report an electron-donor–mediated (EDM) mechanism that suppresses Mn 3+ -induced octahedral distortion while preserving high-spin functionality. As electron-donating Fe 3+ and V 3+ are incorporated, Mn 3+ 3d electrons undergo partial delocalization. This electronic redistribution promotes orbital interactions between neighboring transition metal sites through the transition metal-oxygen framework, driving the e g orbitals toward a more symmetric occupation and suppressing octahedral distortion. The EDM-modified cathode demonstrates a high energy density of 492.06 Wh kg −1 . It delivers 178.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retains 80.2% of its capacity over 2000 cycles at 10 C, paving a novel pathway toward next-generation high-performance SIBs cathode materials.

papers.title: Temperature‐Regulated Morphological Evolution of NiCo‐Carbonate‐Layered Double Hydroxides for High‐Performance Supercapacitor Electrodes
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Supercapacitors, renowned for their advantages of low‐cost, high‐power density, excellent cycling stability, environmental benignity, and superior safety have gained widespread application in diverse fields. However, their further development is limited by drawbacks such as low energy density. NiCo‐carbonate layered double hydroxide (NiCo‐Carbonate LDH) is a promising electrode material, but its two‐dimensional (2D) nanostructures tend to agglomerate, reducing capacitance utilization. In this study, using nickel foam (NF) as the growth substrate, we systematically elucidate, for the first time, the temperature‐induced morphological evolution mechanism of NiCo‐Carbonate LDH from sheet‐like to needle‐like nanostructures by regulating hydrothermal temperature, and fabricate NiCo‐Carbonate LDH/NF composites with a unique needle‐like array architecture. By further optimizing reduced graphene oxide (rGO) loading, we construct NiCo‐Carbonate LDH/rGO/NF composite electrodes. The optimized NiCo‐Carbonate LDH/rGO/NF‐2 electrode delivers a remarkable specific capacitance of 1519 F·g −1 at 1 A·g −1 , which is attributed to the synergistic effect of the needle‐like structure and rGO‐effectively suppressing rGO restacking and promoting ion diffusion and electron transport. The charge storage mechanism is dominated by diffusion‐controlled processes, with the capacitive contribution increasing to 45.2% at high scan rates. This work provides a facile and effective strategy for designing high‐performance supercapacitor electrodes.

papers.title: Supercritical Fluid‐Based Synthesis of Nanomaterials for Energy Storage Applications: A Pathway Toward High‐Entropy Oxides
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Supercritical fluid processing has developed into a versatile and environmentally responsible approach for the controlled fabrication of nanomaterials, distinguished by low density, viscosity, high diffusivity, and negligible surface tension. These intrinsic features enhance nucleation, efficient mass transport, and accurate control over particle dimensions, morphology, and compositional uniformity. This review comprehensively examines the fundamental principles of supercritical fluids, encompassing phase behavior, thermophysical characteristics, and the mechanisms governing nanoparticle formation, along with important engineering aspects related to both batch and continuous‐flow reactor configurations. The preparation of metal, metal oxide, and composite nanostructures through supercritical techniques is critically evaluated, emphasizing their benefits compared with traditional solid‐state and solution‐based synthesis routes. Special attention is given to the evolution toward high‐entropy oxides, where supercritical conditions enable homogeneous multication distribution, enhanced phase development, and defect modulation under kinetically advantageous environments. By establishing clear relationships between processing conditions, structural characteristics, and electrochemical performance, this review highlights the promise of SCF‐enabled methodologies as scalable and sustainable pathways for designing advanced multicomponent oxide materials suited for energy storage and catalytic applications.

papers.title: MXene‐Based Photodetectors: Progress and Prospects
papers.summary: ABSTRACT MXenes, a novel class of 2D transition metal carbides, carbonitrides, and nitrides derived from layered MAX phases, have attracted considerable attention for future photodetector applications due to their unique structural, optical, and electronic properties. Their tunable surface terminations (–O, –OH, –F) and metallic conductivity enable precise modulation of work function and carrier dynamics, facilitating efficient charge transfer and reduced dark current when integrated into semiconductor junctions. This review systematically explores the impact of various synthesis methods, such as HF, in situ HF, electrochemical, and alkali‐assisted etching, on MXene morphology, surface chemistry, and interfacial quality, which are critical for device performance. Key material properties relevant to photodetection, including optical transparency, high carrier mobility, tunable plasmonic response, and adjustable work function, are thoroughly examined. Furthermore, the review underscores MXene role in diverse photodetector designs, highlighting its application as an electrode, charge transport, and active‐layer material. By correlating synthesis techniques with intrinsic properties and device performance, this review provides a comprehensive understanding of how MXene engineering can enhance responsivity, detectivity, and spectral range in optoelectronic systems. Finally, it addresses the current challenges and future opportunities for optimizing MXene‐based materials for high‐performance, broadband, and flexible photodetectors.

papers.title: Electrochemistry‐Enabled Optical and Plasmonic Programmable Metasurfaces
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Organizing metallic nanoparticles (NPs) into well‐defined arrays enables the design of complex, collective plasmon responses. In periodic lattices with controlled spacing, the plasmon modes of individual NPs can couple with the diffraction modes of the arrays, giving rise to lattice‐plasmon resonances. By controlling the geometry of the NP arrangement, the optical, electromagnetic, and chemical properties of the system can be precisely engineered, opening pathways to advanced technologies in electronics, optics, sensing, and catalysis. However, achieving such architectures over large areas while maintaining precise control over composition and morphology remains challenging. Electrochemically fabricated metasurfaces offer a complementary bottom‐up alternative to top‐down patterning, providing direct control over material composition and morphology through low‐cost processing. This Perspective discusses how techniques such as templated electrodeposition, in situ redox patterning, and electrochemical growth and dissolution enable the formation of subwavelength architectures with tunable functionalities, typically associated with more complex fabrication routes. Despite notable advances, the link between electrochemical growth mechanisms and the design of functional optical and plasmonic arrays remains fragmented across the literature. This Perspective synthesizes these developments, clarifies the advantages and current limitations of electrochemical approaches, and outlines emerging opportunities for scalable, electrochemistry‐enabled design of functional metasurfaces.

papers.title: Entropy Stabilized Li‐Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High‐Voltage Cathodes
papers.summary: ABSTRACT The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg −1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.

papers.title: Tailoring coordination environment of copper via carbon-intercalated clay nano-reactors for CO2 electroreduction to methane
papers.summary: The electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) to methane (CH 4 ) offers a promising strategy for converting CO 2 into valuable energy carriers. However, achieving high selectivity and productivity at industrially relevant current densities remains a major challenge. This study reports the one-pot synthesis of a homogeneous carbon-intercalated montmorillonite (MMT) catalyst, reduced graphene oxide (rGO)-intercalated Cu-MMT (rGO@Cu-MMT), designed to minimize the coordination number (CN) of active Cu sites. The rGO-intercalated architecture maintains a low CN and a low average Cu oxidation state under operating potentials, thereby favoring the CH 4 production pathway. In situ/Operando X-ray absorption near-edge structure and extended X-ray absorption fine structure analyses confirmed this mechanism. Consequently, the rGO@Cu-MMT catalyst achieves a CH 4 Faradaic efficiency of near 50% with a partial current density exceeding 195 mA cm −2 in neutral electrolyte and 281 mA cm −2 in alkaline electrolyte. Notably, this superior catalytic performance is retained in a 25 cm 2 industrial-scale flow cell, with performance comparable to that observed in laboratory-scale cells. These findings highlight the potential of clay-based materials as high-performance electrocatalysts and provide insights into structural control strategies for future catalyst design.

papers.title: Anisotropic Boltzmann transport in a tight-binding superlattice: Exact results for power-law energy-dependent scattering
papers.summary: We develop a complete Boltzmann transport theory for the in-plane ($σ_{xx}$) and out-of-plane ($σ_{zz}$) conductivities of an electronic superlattice consisting of a periodic stack of two-dimensional (2D) parabolic-band layers coupled along the superlattice axis by nearest-neighbor tunneling $t$, in the physically relevant regime $t\ll E_F$ where the Fermi surface is an open, corrugated cylinder. Within the relaxation-time approximation with a power-law energy-dependent scattering time $τ(E)\propto E^{p}$, we study the seven models $p=0,\pm1,\pm3/2,\pm2$ as functions of the 2D electron density $n$ per layer and temperature $T$. For $p=-2$ (in plane) and $p\le -1$ (out of plane), long-lived carriers at the miniband bottom can dominate transport at finite temperature. For $p=-2$, these carriers produce a pronounced peak in $σ_{zz}(T)$ at $T\sim E_F$. We find that the temperature dependence of the anisotropic metallic dc conductivity can be highly counterintuitive depending on $t$, $T$, and $p$, with no generic increase or decrease with temperature. The Lorenz ratio is determined by the energy variance of the current-carrying electrons; the Wiedemann-Franz (WF) law is exact as $T\to0$ for all models at fixed $t$, with anisotropic corrections at finite temperature. Band-edge carriers first enhance the interlayer Lorenz ratio up to several times its low-temperature value through thermal occupation of separated energy ranges within the same electron band and then suppress it at high temperature by energy filtering. Strong violations of the Wiedemann-Franz law can therefore arise from miniband structure and energy-dependent elastic scattering alone.

papers.title: Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
papers.summary: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. The method handles entangled bands and accurately reproduces TDDFPT at a fraction of its cost. We use it to compute the total dynamical electron-electron interaction, including direct Coulomb and phonon-mediated interactions with dynamically screened electron-electron and electron-phonon couplings, all on equal footing. In hole-doped monolayer hBN, the hybridization of the carrier plasmon with the longitudinal optical phonon makes the low-energy retarded interaction nonmonotonic in the carrier density, an effect missed by the adiabatic approximation. In metallic monolayer TaS2, nonadiabatic effects are weak and occur only due to the intraband electron-hole continuum and the nesting of nearly parallel Fermi velocities. We also validate the widely used screened-screened approximation for the phonon spectral function. This work opens the way to first-principles studies of spectral functions, transport, and superconductivity with dynamically screened interactions.

papers.title: Polymeric nanocomposites for eco-friendly and industrial applications: a comprehensive review
papers.summary: Abstract Polymeric nanocomposites (PNCs) are formed by dispersing fillers with at least one dimension in the 1–100 nm range in a polymer matrix, and the resulting materials often outperform either constituent alone. Because the interfacial area per unit volume scales inversely with the smallest filler dimension, a few volumes per cent of well-dispersed nanofiller can alter the mechanical, electrical, optical, magnetic and gas-barrier properties of the host polymer, at loadings substantially lower than those required with conventional micro-scale fillers. These benefits have attracted increasing attention from sectors such as water treatment, flexible electronics, aerospace shielding and food preservation. This review provides a thematically organised and critical overview of the PNC field. It first sets out the structure–property fundamentals (interfacial area, interphase volume, filler aspect ratio and dispersion state) that link nanoscale structure to macroscopic performance. It then compares four established fabrication routes (melt blending, in situ polymerisation, solution mixing and electrospinning) in terms of dispersion quality, interfacial bonding, scalability and environmental burden. Smart PNCs that respond to heat, light, electric and magnetic fields are compared with respect to mechanism, representative systems, advantages and limitations. The application sections compile quantitative data on dye and heavy-metal removal, sensing performance (detection limits and linear ranges), electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness and shelf-life extension, and discuss safety, migration and regulatory requirements for food-contact and biomedical uses together with life-cycle considerations. Finally, the review identifies persistent bottlenecks (filler agglomeration, cost, reproducibility, toxicological uncertainty and regulatory gaps) and sets out research priorities, including scale-up, long-term durability, standardised testing and techno-economic assessment, that could accelerate responsible commercialisation.

papers.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
papers.summary: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.

papers.title: Control-Noise Trade-offs in Industrially Integrated ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ Spin-1/2 Qubits
papers.summary: Scaling silicon spin qubits to fault-tolerant processors requires semiconductor foundry integration, yet it remains unclear how industrial fabrication and dense device integration affect qubit control and noise. Here we study ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ electron spin-1/2 qubits fabricated using Intel's industry-compatible 300 mm process and incorporating micromagnets for electrically driven spin resonance, using a high-performance device fabricated in the RIKEN research cleanroom as a reference. Primitive $π/2$-gate fidelities reach the 99.99% level in the Intel devices, which also exhibit longer idle coherence, weaker low-frequency correlations and reduced qubit-to-qubit variability across several measured characteristics. In the present Intel devices, the micromagnets are integrated inline with the back-end-of-line (BEOL) contact routing, with their separation from the quantum well set through the vertical stack design. Relative to the reference, their larger separation contributes to weaker longitudinal and transverse magnetic-field gradients. The weaker longitudinal gradient suppresses the conversion of charge noise into qubit-frequency fluctuations, whereas the weaker transverse gradient reduces electrically driven spin-resonance efficiency and makes drive-dependent errors relevant at lower Rabi frequencies. Additional BEOL routing and metal levels required for two-dimensional arrays make such placement decisions increasingly consequential when scaling. These results establish an integration-level control-noise trade-off linking micromagnet placement within densely routed layouts to achievable gate performance, while very high-fidelity operation remains possible in industrially fabricated devices.

papers.title: Anisotropic spin splitting in $α$-MnTe epilayers on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates
papers.summary: $α$-MnTe has emerged as a prototypical altermagnetic material, combining compensated antiferromagnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting. Here, we investigate the structural and electronic properties of epitaxial $α$-MnTe layers grown by molecular beam epitaxy on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates. The crystalline and surface quality of the epilayers was characterised by reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), confirming the formation of high-quality, single-phase films. The transport measurements were performed, confirming an antiferromagnetic transition and weak ferromagnetism. The electronic structure was studied using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). At 90 K, both samples exhibit relativistic anisotropic valence band splitting, which is substantially larger along the $Γ$-K direction, reaching approximately 300 meV, than along $Γ$-M, where values of about 150~meV are observed. The magnitude and momentum dependence of the splitting are very similar for $α$-MnTe grown on the two different substrates, indicating the robustness of the altermagnetic electronic structure with respect to the epitaxial environment.

papers.title: Polyoxometalate-metal organic framework hybrid materials for electrochemical energy applications
papers.summary: Energy materials play a crucial role in determining the performance of electrochemical systems, with continuous advancements enhancing energy utilization efficiency and enabling a broad range of applications. In this context, significant efforts have been devoted to the development of novel materials for further improving device performance. Polyoxometalate–metal organic framework (POM-MOF) composites have emerged as a promising class of hybrid materials due to their hierarchical structures, which enhance the availability of active sites, facilitate efficient charge transfer, and improve catalytic performance and mechanical stability. This review summarizes recent advances in the rational design and modification of POM–MOF-based energy materials, highlighting key performance-enhancing strategies such as morphology tailoring, doping, defect engineering, and the incorporation of other materials (conducting polymers, transition metals, non-precious metals, etc.), as well as the underlying design principles and structure–activity relationships governing their electrochemical behavior. Their applications are particularly emphasized in electrochemical energy conversion (fuel cells, water electrolyzers, and CO2 electrolyzers) and energy storage (batteries and supercapacitors). These advancements have enabled electrochemical systems with low overpotentials (< 100 mV), high capacities (~ 1000 mAh g⁻¹), outstanding cycling stabilities (> 90%), high power densities (~ 1000 mW cm⁻²), long-term operational stability (> 5000 h), Faradaic efficiencies above 90%, and wide pH operating ranges. Further, key challenges are discussed and future perspectives are provided to guide the design of efficient POM–MOF-based electrochemical energy materials, accelerating their transition toward practical applications.

papers.title: Na‐Site Energetics Reconfiguration Enables Full Capacity Utilization of Sodium Iron Sulfate Cathodes
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Sodium iron sulfates are promising high‐voltage cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries, but their practical performance is hindered by incomplete utilization of structurally available Na + and sluggish electronic transport. Here, we demonstrate a mixed‐polyanion electrostatic modulation strategy that reconfigures the Na‐site energy landscape of the sulfate‐based framework. This chemical regulation drives a fraction of Na + into the kinetically favorable Na2/Na3 sites to increase Na + accessibility, suppressing occupancy of the Fe–Na‐disorder‐prone Na4 site, and facilitating the subsequent extraction of trapped Na1 sites. Coupled with an electronic percolation network, the resulting cathodes deliver 100 mAh g − 1 at 0.1C in the hard carbon||Na 2.7 Fe 1.7 (SO 4 ) 2.9 (PO 4 ) 0.1 full cell, approaching its theoretical capacity of 102 mAh g − 1 , together with capacity retention of 90% at 5C after 1500 cycles. This work reveals hetero‐anion substitution as a site‐energy reconfiguring strategy for unlocking reversible Na + storage in kinetically constrained polyanion cathodes.

papers.title: Solid‐State Reductive Electrochemistry of Lapis Lazuli/Ultramarine
papers.summary: The reductive electrochemistry of different ultramarine specimens in contact with aqueous electrolytes is studied using the voltammetry of immobilized particles. This electrochemistry can be described in terms of the cathodic processes involving the chromophore species, S 3 − , S 2 − entrapped into the cavities of the lazurite lattice. Such processes involve a peculiar proton plus metal cation ingress into the solid framework, showing codiffusion effects characterized by chronoamperometric measurements.

papers.title: Surface Functionalization of Hexagonal WO 3 for Enhanced Pseudocapacitive Energy Storage
papers.summary: The development of sustainable and high‐performance electrochemical energy‐storage systems requires electrode materials capable of combining fast charge transfer, high power capability and long‐term stability. In this context, pseudocapacitive transition metal oxides have attracted increasing attention due to their ability to bridge the gap between conventional capacitors and batteries. Herein, a sustainable surface‐engineering strategy is proposed to enhance the pseudocapacitive response of hexagonal WO 3 nanoparticles through in situ functionalization with N‐ and S‐containing species during a simple aqueous hydrothermal synthesis. The introduced surface functionalities improve the electrochemical performance without altering the bulk crystal structure or morphology of WO 3 . In particular, the functionalized materials exhibit enhanced specific capacitance, improved coulombic efficiency, and remarkable cycling stability over 10,000 cycles, with S‐functionalized WO 3 showing the best overall response. Spectroscopic analyses suggest that surface electronic modulation and more favorable interfacial charge–transfer processes contribute to the improved pseudocapacitive behavior. Moreover, the exclusive use of aqueous synthesis, water‐based electrode processing, and aqueous electrolytes provides a greener route toward electrode fabrication. These findings highlight surface functionalization as a promising and sustainable strategy for tuning the interfacial properties of WO 3 ‐based electrodes for next‐generation energy‐storage technologies.

papers.title: Hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries: from mechanistic reconciliation, precursor-tailored microstructure regulation to industrial scale-up
papers.summary: Hard carbon is the leading anode candidate for sodium-ion batteries, yet its practical deployment remains constrained by three interconnected gaps: the sodium storage mechanism is disputed across competing models, no precursor classification framework links chemical composition to electrochemical function, and predictive structure–property relationships remain largely empirical. This review traces the precursor-to-performance pipeline. We show that the insertion-filling, adsorption-insertion, and adsorption-filling models converge on a multi-stage adsorption-intercalation-filling paradigm, where the intercalation-to-filling balance is governed by carbonization temperature, precursor chemistry, and pore architecture rather than by a single mechanism. We then introduce a three-dimensional precursor classification framework—spanning scalability, structural controllability, and performance ceiling—and deconvolute the component-specific pyrolysis pathways of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin to establish how molecular architecture is transmitted into carbon microstructure. Three microstructure engineering levers are critically evaluated: pore-structure manipulation to resolve the low-surface-area/high-closed-pore-volume trade-off, interlayer-spacing regulation via heteroatom doping and pre-oxidation, and defect engineering guided by the conductivity-capacity Pareto Frontier. The rapid industrialization of hard carbon—from laboratory discovery to 10,000-ton-scale manufacturing—is assessed, documenting how precursor diversification and process innovation have driven costs toward parity with graphite anodes. Finally, the current challenges and future development directions of high-performance and industrializable hard carbon anodes are prospected, aiming to provide systematic theoretical guidance and technical references for the further design, modification and large-scale application of hard carbon materials in advanced sodium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Synthesis and Morphological Evolution of MoO 3 ‐II Under High Temperature and High Oxygen Partial Pressure
papers.summary: ABSTRACT MoO 3 ‐II was synthesized from α‐MoO 3 at 5.5 GPa and 450°C–800°C to investigate the effects of synthesis temperature and the use of Ag 2 O as an internal oxidizing source on phase formation, surface oxygen stoichiometry, and particle evolution. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) showed a higher surface oxygen stoichiometry in the Ag 2 O‐assisted samples than in their Ag 2 O‐free counterparts, except at 450°C. X‐ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) further revealed distinct temperature‐dependent particle‐evolution behavior. Without Ag 2 O, both the apparent coherent‐domain size and particle size increased with synthesis temperature, whereas Ag 2 O‐assisted samples exhibited larger particles at 530°C‐600°C and finer particles at 670°C‐800°C. The contrasting trends are consistent with a possible competition between oxygen‐assisted growth and localized Ag–Mo–O reactions. These findings clarify how an internal Ag 2 O oxidizing source modifies the crystallization behavior and particle evolution of high‐pressure MoO 3 ‐II phase.

papers.journal: Journal of the American Ceramic Society

papers.title: Interlayer‐Expanded Ti 3 C 2 MXene/Mn‐Doped NH 4 V 4 O 10 Nanocomposite for Screen‐Printed Micro Supercapacitor Applications
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Non‐metallic charge carriers, especially NH 4 + ions, have recently attracted attention for energy storage, with Ammonium Vanadates (NH 4 V 4 O 10 ) gaining an early advantage in ammonium‐ion storage due to their large interlayer spacing. Here, we report the fabrication of a nanocomposite involving Ti 3 C 2 (MX) and Mn‐doped NH 4 V 4 O 10 (MVO). Bare NH 4 V 4 O 10 (NVO) has an interlayer spacing of 9.8Å corresponding to the major (001) peak. The interlayer spacing was enhanced to 10.81Å by doping with Mn 2+ ions. The H‐bonding interactions between the surface terminations of MX and the N─H bonds of MVO provide intimate contact, allowing faster ion diffusion, and contributing to predominantly diffusion‐controlled charge storage. The MX‐18 composite delivered a maximum specific capacitance of 260 F/g at 1 mA/cm 2 in a half‐cell configuration in 1 m NH 4 Cl, with the lowest charge‐transfer resistance among its counterparts. MX‐18, in an asymmetric device, yielded a maximum energy density (44.4 Wh/kg) at a power density of 289.04 W/kg, with 70% capacitance retention after 5500 cycles. The symmetric configuration of MX‐18 was fabricated as a screen‐printed micro‐supercapacitor with PVA/NH 4 Cl gel electrolyte, yielding an energy density of 5 µWh/cm 2 at a power density of 114 µW/cm 2 , showcasing good flexibility and long‐term stability.

papers.title: Tailoring the Structural, Optical, and Electrical Performance of PVA Through Sn0.8Mn0.2S Nanostructures Incorporation for Optoelectronic Applications
papers.summary: This work aims to produce a new nanocomposite of Sn0.8Mn0.2S nanostructures incorporated into polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) for optoelectronic applications. Sn0.8Mn0.2S/PVA nanocomposite was prepared by combining a precipitation-based synthesis of Sn0.8Mn0.2S with the solution casting of the PVA matrix. FTIR spectroscopy was used to examine the chemical interactions and bonding between the Sn0.8Mn0.2S nanostructures and PVA chains. Morphological properties were investigated by the SEM technique. The X-ray diffraction technique was used to study the structural properties. UV–Visible spectroscopy was applied to explore the optical properties. Optical analysis shows that the direct and indirect optical bandgap decreased from 5.36 and 4.95 eV for the plain PVA to 1.94 and 1.32 eV at the highest loading (10 wt.%), accompanied by an increase in the refractive index from 1.69 to 2.33. Both the dielectric constants and optical conductivity of PVA likewise enhanced markedly with an increasing Sn0.8Mn0.2S amount. Four-probe DC measurements performed across 300 to 400 K demonstrated a reduction in PVA resistivity together with a drop in the activation energy, from 0.39 eV down to 0.18 eV, as the loading increased up to 1.0 wt.%, identifying this concentration as the most favorable for electrical performance. These findings recommend Sn0.8Mn0.2S nanostructures as an effective means of engineering the structural, optical, and electrical characteristics of PVA, with a clear relevance to optoelectronic device applications.

papers.title: Synthesis of Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBenes in Molten Salts From Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives
papers.summary: ABSTRACT The unique properties and application possibilities of two‐dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti 2 InB 2 with ZnCl 2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBene. Upon etching, indium atoms are completely removed from the precursor and replaced by chlorine surface terminations with a coverage of 1.1 < x < 1.4. Further, in situ x‐ray diffraction indicates a direct biphasic transformation from Ti 2 InB 2 to ml‐MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml‐MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A‐element substitution into the 3D Ti 2 ZnB 2 phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li‐ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.

papers.title: Metal Glycerolate‐Based Synthesis and Structure–Property Relationships of LiNi 1− x − y Co x Mn y O 2 Cathodes for Lithium‐Ion Batteries
papers.summary: Lithium‐ion batteries are currently the dominant energy storage systems, with cathode materials playing a significant role in electrochemical performance, safety, and cost. Among these materials, layered LiNi 1− x − y Co x Mn y O 2 (NCM)‐based cathodes stand out due to their competitive cost, compositional versatility, high capacity and energy density. Controlling the Ni/Co/Mn ratio is a key strategy for optimizing the balance between capacity, structural stability, and electrochemical performance. In this work, metal glycerolates synthesized via a solvothermal route were employed as hybrid organic–inorganic precursors to prepare NCM materials. The compositional variation, spanning from low‐ to high‐Ni content, enabled a direct correlation between Ni content, structural disorder, and electrochemical performance. Increasing the Ni content promoted Li + /Ni 2+ cation mixing and structural disorder, resulting in reduced discharge capacity of Ni‐rich NCM cathodes. In contrast, low‐Ni NCM compositions exhibited improved structural ordering and electrochemical behavior, with Mg 2+ doping effectively improving the stabilization of the LiNi 0.33 Co 0.33 Mn 0.33 O 2 (NCM 333) structure and enhancing its rate capability and cycling stability. These findings provide important insights into the relationship between composition, structural ordering, and electrochemical behavior, while highlighting both the potential and current limitations of metal glycerolate‐based synthesis for NCM cathodes. Thus, metal glycerolates offer a basis for the rational design of cost‐effective and more sustainable energy storage materials.

papers.title: Influence of Water Content in the Pores of Hydrophobic Aluminum‐Based Adsorbent Particles on Lithium Adsorption Performance From Salt Lake Brine
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Hydrophobic aluminum‐based (Al‐based) adsorbent particles are used for the improved strength but sharply reduced adsorption capacity during lithium (Li) recovery from salt lake brines. Adequate wetting of hydrophobic particles is regarded as a key factor to achieve outstanding Li + adsorption performance. In this work, Al‐based adsorbents are granulated with hydrophobic binder and wetted with different physically adsorbed water contents of 0%, 7.2%, and 28.0%. The effects of water content are systematically investigated. Compared with the unwetted particles, the wetted particles exhibit a shorter Li + adsorption equilibrium time by 25.0%, a higher Li + saturated adsorption capacity by 33.6%, and a lower Mg/Li (mass ratio) in the eluent by 29.0%. The wetted particles also have good cyclic stability and mechanical stability. The acting forces between brine and particles during the adsorption are analyzed and show that brine is difficult to flow into the pores of hydrophobic particles. The adequate wetting is critical for the enhancement of Li + adsorption capacity and adsorption speed and the reduction of Mg/Li.

papers.title: Engineering topology by design in two-dimensional materials
papers.summary: Two-dimensional topological insulators (2D TIs) have emerged as a cornerstone of next-generation spintronic technologies due to their robust, dissipationless edge states protected by time-reversal symmetry. Initial realizations of 2D TIs have primarily focused on materials with strong intrinsic spin-orbit coupling capable of driving band inversion, an approach that significantly constrains the accessible materials landscape. More recently, a paradigm shift has occurred toward engineering topological phases in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures, where nontrivial band topology can arise from interfacial coupling rather than relying solely on intrinsic material properties. This framework provides an exceptionally versatile platform with multiple tunable degrees of freedom, including stacking configuration, twist angle, and chemical functionalization, allowing systematic manipulation of the band topology. Furthermore, external stimuli, such as electric fields, strain, and light-matter coupling, enable dynamic and reversible control of the topological character. The combined use of vdW interface engineering and external modulation allows the realization of 2D TI phases even in otherwise topologically trivial systems, substantially expanding the accessible materials landscape. This Research Update reviews key milestones in the development of vdW-engineered 2D topological quantum materials, critically assesses outstanding theoretical and experimental challenges, and outlines promising directions for future breakthroughs.

papers.title: Machine Learning‐Driven Vapor Passivation Enables Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) recently, yet the device instability induced by defects remains a bottleneck. Despite the effectiveness of passivation strategies in reducing defects, conventional solution‐based methods may compromise the perovskite crystallinity. Thus, vapor‐based molecules are expected to penetrate into crystals and reduce defects. Screening effective vapor‐assisted passivation materials usually takes substantial trial‐and‐error costs. Here, we propose a hybrid workflow integrating machine learning models with first‐principles calculations to screen the key functional groups for vapor‐assisted passivation molecules and provide physical insights. The phenyl and halogen atoms were identified by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis to be effective. Theoretical calculations also indicated that there was a strong cation‐ π interaction between Pb 2+ and benzene ring. Besides, halogenated benzene could intercalate into the iodine vacancies on perovskite surfaces. Such robust interactions synergistically contribute to the stability of [PbI 6 ] 4− octahedral framework, and thus the formation of defects and structural collapse could be effectively suppressed. Moreover, the thermal conductivity of modified perovskite films was remarkably enhanced. Finally, the device modified with iodobenzene vapor achieved the champion PCE of 26.94%. This workflow integrating data‐driven discovery and atomistic understandings, provides an innovative strategy to screen vapor‐assisted passivation materials.

papers.title: Structural and Mechanical Insights into Chemically Synthesized Si–C Composites for Lithium-Ion Battery Negative Electrodes
papers.summary: Abstract Numerous efforts have been made to utilize silicon-based negative electrodes in lithium-ion batteries (LiBs). The main challenge with Si-based anodes is their significant volume expansion and contraction during cycling, which degrades LiB performance . Silicon-carbon composites are known to address many of the challenges of large-volume expansion and can deliver high specific capacity alongside acceptable cycle life. In this study, various chemically synthesized Si-C composites with different porous hard carbon precursors were investigated to examine the evolution of the filling of the carbon precursor pores with Si during impregnation via chemical vapour deposition using SiH4 gas. These samples were later etched with a high-pH solution to remove the Si in several steps, returning the structure to that of the carbon precursor to backtrack the changes in the carbon precursor. The as-received carbon precursor and the etched samples were compared using small-angle X-ray scattering and X-ray diffraction. These techniques, combined with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, compression testing of the samples, and electrochemical performance measurements, provide a broad view of the evolution of the carbon precursor structure during Si deposition and during the charge/discharge processes in the LiB negative electrode, providing insight into the structure-performance-properties correlation of CVD-based Si-C composites.

papers.title: The Serendipitous Discovery of Rollover Cyclometalation: From Unrecognized Observation to Transformative Chemistry
papers.summary: Rollover cyclometalation is a distinctive variant of classical cyclometalation where a chelated heterocyclic ligand undergoes internal rotation, releasing one donor atom from coordination and subsequently activating a remote C─H bond with high regioselectivity. The resulting rollover complexes bear an uncoordinated donor atom that confers unique reactivity unavailable to conventional cyclometalated species. The discovery of rollover cyclometalation represents a remarkable example of serendipity in organometallic chemistry, a reaction observed multiple times over decades before being recognized as a distinct and valuable transformation. First appearing in the literature in 1975 and formally named in 1985, rollover cyclometalation involves an unconventional ligand rearrangement to form a new metallacycle. This review traces the serendipitous discovery narrative, emphasizing how early researchers observed the reaction without recognizing its novelty, and examines how subsequent mechanistic studies established rollover cyclometalation as a distinct reaction class. The review explores the reaction’s broad scope beyond 2,2′‐bipyridine, its novel features including reversible retro‐rollover processes, mechanistic insights in gas‐ and condensed‐phase, and growing applications in catalysis, materials science, and novel metallodrugs. This discovery exemplifies Thomas Kuhn’s observation that scientific (r)evolutions often begin with anomalies that challenge existing frameworks, demonstrating how preparedness and systematic investigation can transform unexpected observations into transformative knowledge.

papers.title: NiFe Metal–Organic Framework Film Infiltrated With Conjugated Molecules: An Efficient and Durable Anode for Alkaline Seawater Oxidation at Ampere‐Level Current Density
papers.summary: Although holding great promise to mitigate freshwater scarcity for green hydrogen production, direct seawater electrolysis is challenged by the anodic chloride oxidation reactions, which lowers the system efficiency and cause catalyst corrosion. Herein, we demonstrate a strategy for realizing efficient and long‐lasting alkaline seawater oxidation over a NiFe metal–organic framework (NiFe MOF) film supported on Ni foam via infiltratation with the conjugated molecule 7,7,8,8‐tetracyanoquinododimethane (TCNQ). Such TCNQ@NiFe MOF/NF anode is capable of attaining an industrial‐level current density of 1000 mA cm −2 with a low overpotential of 352 mV and maintaining 800‐h operational stability. The incorporated TCNQ molecules can enhance the electronic conductivity, effectively repel Cl − , and suppress Fe leaching. An anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer built from TCNQ@NiFe MOF/NF and Pt/C/NF operates stably for 450 h.

papers.title: Chloride‐Mediated Activation of Aluminum‐Alloyed Liquid Metal Anodes for Stretchable Asymmetric Energy Storage
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Gallium‐based liquid metals are attractive anodes for stretchable energy storage because they operate dendrite‐free, yet their bulk faradaic capacity remains locked behind a native oxide shell that conventional electrolytes cannot remove. Here, this passivation problem is resolved through the co‐design of an aluminum‐alloyed gallium–indium (AlGaIn) anode and a chloride‐rich water‐in‐ionic‐liquid (WIL) electrolyte, and the indium‐assisted electrochemical activation mechanism connecting them is identified. Al alloying converts the native oxide into a hydroxyl‐rich mixed Al–Ga–O shell susceptible to [GaCl 4 ] − ‐mediated etching, while the In(III) ions preferentially reduced into metallic patches that seed reversible Ga alloying/dealloying within the WIL. Potential‐resolved ex situ XPS indicates that in conventional TFSI‐based electrolytes, the electrode passivates beneath a TFSI‐derived interphase, whereas in the WIL, a chloride‐dominated electrode–electrolyte interphase forms instead. The activated anode gains 60% capacity during activation and retains ∼100% capacity over 1600 cycles at 500 mA g − 1 . Paired with a sonochemically derived GaOOH nanosheet cathode in a stretchable asymmetric cell, the asymmetric full cell delivers a maximum of 66.28 mWh cm −3 normalized to the active‐electrode volume, and 90% capacity retention over 4000 cycles. The halide‐mediated oxide‐displacement principle established here provides a generalizable electrolyte‐design strategy for oxide‐passivated liquid‐metal and post‐lithium anodes.

papers.title: Vanadium Oxide/MXene Composite Fiber Cathodes With Superior Spinnability Enabling High Electrochemical Performance for Fiber‐Shaped Zinc‐Ion Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Fiber‐shaped zinc‐ion batteries are highly deformable and can store energy in irregular spaces. Fiber cathodes with carbon fiber cores can be continuously prepared via wet spinning. In this work, MXene is introduced into the cathode by directly hybridizing with vanadium oxide, acting as a bridge to enhance the interfacial interaction within the cathode. MXene modifies the rheological behavior of the cathode slurry and facilitates the rearrangement of the active material during wet spinning, thereby effectively improving fiber spinnability and mitigating agglomeration of the active material. Additionally, MXene enhances the electrical conductivity of the active material and stabilizes the structure of VO 2 , enabling the composite cathode to deliver satisfactory specific capacity and cycling stability. The cathode achieves a specific capacity of 136 mAh g −1 at 3 A g −1 after 2000 cycles, which is 109% higher than that of the pure VO 2 cathode. The cathodes are assembled with MXene/chitosan‐coated fiber anodes and a hydrogel electrolyte to make full batteries. The resulting battery packs can power lighting and communication modules in small unmanned aerial vehicles. This work leverages the multiple advantages of MXene in various dimensions, proposes an optimization strategy for carbon‐fiber‐based fiber‐shaped batteries, and highlights their application potential.

papers.title: Supercritical Solvothermal Synthesis of Spinel ZnV 2 O 4 /Porous Carbon Composite Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT The electrochemical performance of vanadium‐based oxide cathodes in aqueous zinc‐ion batteries has long been constrained by their intrinsically low electronic conductivity, severe vanadium dissolution, and prolonged synthesis procedures. To address these limitations, a supercritical solvothermal strategy is developed for the rapid fabrication of a high‐performance spinel‐structured ZnV 2 O 4 /porous carbon (ZnV 2 O 4 /PRC) composite. Benefiting from the excellent mass transfer and heat transfer characteristics and mild reducing capability of supercritical ethanol, this approach effectively suppresses the formation of hydrated zinc vanadate phases, thereby significantly shortening the reaction time required for ZnV 2 O 4 formation. Meanwhile, the introduction of a porous carbon (PRC) framework provides efficient electrolyte penetration pathways, reduces the interparticle diffusion resistance of Zn 2+ ions, and minimizes the direct contact between ZnV 2 O 4 and the electrolyte. As a result, the electronic conductivity of the composite is substantially enhanced, Zn 2+ transport kinetics are accelerated, and vanadium dissolution is significantly mitigated. Owing to these combined advantages, the ZnV 2 O 4 /PRC cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 470 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 and retains 172 mAh g −1 after 5000 cycles at a high current density of 10 A g −1 , demonstrating outstanding long‐term cycling stability.

papers.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
papers.summary: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that lone-pair stereoactivity, not chalcogen mass, governs both properties. Path-integral molecular dynamics shows that the volumetric thermal expansion coefficient at 300 K decreases from 8.14 x 10^-5 K^-1 in Bi2O2S to 6.72 x 10^-5 and 6.61 x 10^-5 K^-1 in Bi2O2Se and Bi2O2Te, respectively, despite a 13% larger unit cell in the telluride, whereas substituting the S mass into Bi2O2Se changes its value by only 0.6%. Lone-pair-driven Bi off-centering in orthorhombic Bi2O2S makes b-axis expansion 1.63 times a-axis expansion yet leaves in-plane thermal conduction isotropic within 3%. Phonon transport calculations including four-phonon scattering and Wigner coherence predict a thermal conductivity maximum in Bi2O2Se (1.83 and 0.95 W m^-1 K^-1 in the in-plane and cross-plane directions, respectively, at 300 K) because Bi2O2S is limited by anharmonic scattering and Bi2O2Te by slow cross-plane phonons. Thermoreflectance measurements from 300 to 500 K and in situ X-ray diffraction on Bi2O2Se single crystals agree with these predictions within 6.4%. Phonon Boltzmann transport simulations of 12-nm-wide fins, which run hotter than Fourier diffusion predicts, show that Bi2O2Se minimizes the hotspot temperature and the thermal-mismatch strain at the gate dielectric.

papers.title: Gravitational anomaly spectroscopy of a Kitaev spin liquid
papers.summary: The chiral central charge $c$ measures the gravitational anomaly of a two-dimensional topological phase. It fixes the heat current carried along the edge. So far, it has been accessed through thermal transport, where phonons complicate the signal, or through wave-function probes that need a pure ground state. Here we show that $c$ is a spectroscopic quantity of the edge. A weak modulation of the edge couplings that travel along the edge is absorbed according to the Virasoro algebra. Normalized by the response to a static change of the same couplings, the absorbed weights obey $D_n=2n\langle L_0\rangle+\frac{c}{12}(n^3-n)$, so that $\mathcal{C}\equiv2D_2-4D_1=c$ in any state of the ideal edge theory, thermal or not. The central charge thus appears in transition weights, although it cancels from excitation gaps. The ratio of line weights with and without a vison in the bulk, $Λ=4h_σ/c$, needs no calibration and fixes the conformal spin $h_σ$ of the non-Abelian Ising anyon. For the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid we find $\mathcal{C}=0.49999$ and $h_σ=0.06250$ on 7168 spins. Calibrating with the shift of the measured line itself gives $c$ within about $1\%$ on 96 spins and within $1\%$ under $20\%$ random coupling errors. Interacting edge Majoranas in a fixed flux sector, treated with DMRG, keep $\mathcal{C}$ within $1.5\%$ while the edge velocity changes by $\pm13\%$. An exact simulation of a quantum-processor protocol, including the native Floquet circuit, returns $c$ within $3.5\%$ on 96 to 600 spins.

papers.title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
papers.summary: Tellurium dioxide (TeO$_2$) is a wide-bandgap oxide with attractive processing versatility and emerging p-type semiconducting behaviour, making it a promising material system for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications. However, TeO$_2$-derived thin films prepared by scalable manufacturing processes, such as vacuum sublimation, can contain residual metallic Te$^0$ species that introduce trap states, limit hole transport, and promote carrier recombination. Here, we demonstrate a selenium alloying strategy to control the defect chemistry of vacuum-sublimed TeO$_x$ films. TeO$_2$:Se powder mixtures (90:10~wt\%) were thermally evaporated and subsequently annealed in air at 225~$^\circ$C for up to 9~h, yielding amorphous TeO$_x$:Se films with an optical bandgap of 0.98~eV under optimised conditions. Structural, chemical, optical, and electrical analyses show that prolonged annealing promotes Se redistribution, suppresses residual Te$^0$ to approximately 0.4\%, reduces the film's surface roughness, and shifts the valence-band edge. To evaluate the potential of TeO$_x$:Se for photovoltaic applications, we fabricated thin-film solar cells with an ITO/ZnO/TeO$_x$:Se/MoO$_x$/Ag architecture. Devices based on an 80~nm TeO$_x$:Se active layer annealed for 9~h exhibit optimal performance, with broadband photocurrent generation from 300 to 1000~nm, yielding an open-circuit voltage of 0.50~V, a short-circuit current density of 8.50~mA~cm$^{-2}$, a fill factor of 0.44, and a maximum power conversion efficiency of approximately 1.87\%. These results establish selenium-alloyed TeO$_x$ as a viable oxide-derived absorber for thin-film photovoltaics and highlight chemical-state control as an effective route for improving photovoltaic performance.

papers.title: Drift-induced nonreciprocity in image-polariton-mediated dipole emission
papers.summary: Electrical current bias offers a magnet-free route to nonreciprocal light propagation at the nanoscale. Here, we theoretically explore drift-induced nonreciprocity in graphene heterostructures containing hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), where graphene plasmons interact with hBN phonon polaritons in the infrared. Both the random-phase approximation and the Boltzmann transport equation are used to characterize the nonlocal optical response of drift-biased graphene. We compare graphene on hBN with an image-polaritonic structure comprising graphene, a thin hBN spacer, and a gold substrate. Carrier drift produces pronounced directional shifts of the polariton dispersion, while coupling to hBN phonon polaritons strongly modifies the nonreciprocal response. In the image-polaritonic structure, the graphene polaritons become up to twice as confined while retaining a comparable Fizeau shift. The nonreciprocal polariton dispersion produces directional near-field emission and nonreciprocal dipole-dipole interactions, the latter quantified through the cross density of optical states, reaching a left-right dissymmetry of up to ~40%. Our results identify image polaritons in drift-biased graphene as a compact, electrically tunable platform for directional coupling between quantum emitters at the nanoscale.

papers.title: Analytical framework for interpreting thermoreflectance measurements of nanoline gratings under finite spot illumination
papers.summary: A frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR)-based technique is presented to measure the effective thermal properties of a material stack whose surface is patterned with metallic nanoline gratings that are heated and probed by lasers. An analytical heat diffusion model is derived for predicting the FDTR phase response that incorporates a finite laser spot radius with a Gaussian intensity profile for the pump and probe lasers, as well as the dimensions of the nanoline grating. The model is validated by comparing with measurements of Au nanoline gratings, with widths ranging from 100 to 1000 nm, fabricated on a-SiO$_2$ and $c$-sapphire substrates. Due to the short phonon mean free paths (MFPs) in these substrates, thermal transport remains in the diffusive regime for the whole range of nanoline widths. The model and the measurement show excellent agreement across different laser spot radii and nanoline widths, with a bulk thermal conductivity value of $c$-sapphire and the thermal boundary conductances at the Au-Cr/a-SiO$_2$ and Au-Cr/$c$-sapphire interfaces comparable to our prior measurements and the literature. The validated model will serve as a robust baseline for extending this method to measure effective thermal conductivity as a function of the heater size. This approach is particularly relevant for materials where non-diffusive thermal transport regimes enable probing phonon MFP dependent contributions to the thermal conductivity.

papers.title: Electric field control of anisotropic spin traffic between spin-filtering and magnon-scattering in a layered antiferromagnet
papers.summary: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. We present a dual-gate field-effect transistor based on CrSBr, a layered A-type AFM with pronounced transport anisotropy and complex spin dynamics. Our device provides independent control over carrier density and displacement field. Systematic transport measurements reveal that the displacement field, rather than doping, predominantly governs the sign and magnitude of magnetoresistance ratio (MRR). We identify the origins of both negative and positive MRR components and connect them to interlayer and intralayer spin-dependent transport mechanisms. We interpret these findings with ab initio calculations and an effective spin-circuit model that reproduces the anisotropic magnetotransport. Our results identify the displacement field as an efficient electrical control parameter of spin transport in CrSBr and suggest that multi-gate architectures could provide similar control in other layered antiferromagnetic semiconductors.

papers.title: Ghosts in the nanomachine: dynamical slowing-down in the phase-space of nanomechanical strings
papers.summary: The linear behavior of micro- and nanomechanical devices has been the topic of intense study over the past years. Their nonlinear behavior, on the other hand, continues to provide new and interesting dynamics. This work leverages a cavity opto-mechanical system whose very high sensitivity and low dissipation rate allows to capture the dynamics of fast transients that occur when strongly-driven nonlinear resonators relax to their equilibrium state. We experimentally study the ringdown dynamics of a nanomechanical Duffing resonator in both the time domain and in phase space. The resonator exhibits very different ringdown dynamics depending on whether it is subject to one or two tone driving. In the former case the ringdown follows a regular exponential decay, whereas the latter case shows exotic dynamics such as libration, slowing-down while scattering in phase-space, and ghost slowing-down. We demonstrate that this distinct difference can be attributed to the structure of the phase space itself. Surprisingly, we find that the energy in the resonator changes non-monotonously and that long delay between turning off the drive and the decay of the motion amplitude results in dynamical meta-states.

papers.title: Epitaxial Magnon Junctions with Y3Fe5O12/Gd3Ga5O12/Pt-nanoparticles/Y3Fe5O12
papers.summary: The excitation, propagation, manipulation, and detection of magnons lie at the core of magnonics. Among various device architectures, high-quality magnon junctions with a ferromagnetic insulator (FI)/antiferromagnetic insulator (AFI)/ferromagnetic insulator (FI) configuration are predicted to exhibit a near-100% magnon junction ratio (MJR), making them promising candidates for high-performance non-volatile memory applications. Yttrium iron garnet (Y3Fe5O12, YIG) is widely employed as the FI material in such structures for its exceptionally low magnetic damping. However, in previously reported magnon junctions, the epitaxial relationship between the two YIG layers is often disrupted by lattice-mismatched AFI spacers. Although this leads to distinct coercivities, it simultaneously degrades the crystalline quality of the top YIG layer, thereby limiting the magnontransmission efficiency. Here, an epitaxial magnon junction is demonstrated incorporating a hybrid Gd3Ga5O12 (GGG)/Pt-nanoparticles spacer that maintains coherent epitaxy while enabling an antiparallel magnetic configuration. Compared with nickel oxide-based magnon junctions, the coercivity-tuned top YIG layer in our structure exhibits superior crystalline quality and much lower magnetic damping. A clear magnon junction effect is observed with a 43% MJR achieved. The interlayer coupling between the two ferrimagnetic insulators is found to enhance the MJR. These results offer valuable insights for the development of advanced magnon-based spintronic devices.

papers.title: Moiré-enabled chiral plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands
papers.summary: Twisting two stacked graphene layers superimposes a moiré superlattice that reshapes their electronic structure, yet how it shapes the collective optical response of finite, nanoscale bilayers remains largely unexplored. Using an atomistic tight-binding and self-consistent density-matrix approach, we compute the twist-dependent plasmonic response of twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands comprising thousands of atoms. The spectra are strongly tunable and split into two regimes at a critical angle where a single moiré wavelength spans the island; beyond it, an ordered ladder of resonances emerges whenever an integer number of moiré periods fits within the overlapping bilayer. In doped islands, the interlayer coupling also produces a moiré-enabled Born--Kuhn chiral plasmon: opposite transverse dipoles in the two layers form an electric quadrupole that hybridizes with the bright dipole, opening an anticrossing near the critical angle, with a handedness that reverses with the twist direction. Triangular islands confirm that the moiré lattice, not the flake boundary, governs both effects, establishing twist as a mechanical handle on chiral graphene plasmons.

papers.title: Dissipation dilution enhances SiV coupling to vdW diamond nanomechanics
papers.summary: Solid-state color centers embedded into mechanical resonators, where orbital states mediate interactions between spins and long-lived phonons, are a promising platform for hybrid quantum systems. The negatively charged silicon vacancy center in diamond (SiV-) is particularly favorable for strain-coupling to nanomechanical resonators because of its large spin-strain susceptibility and compatibility with device integration. Tensioned nanomechanical resonators offer an attractive route due to their ultra-long mechanical coherence times enabled by diluting defect-induced dissipation, though it is unclear if the same dilution effect undermines strain-mediated coupling to material defect centers. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform that enables enhanced strain coupling to SiV- orbital states. Through monitoring the optical response of the SiVs to the static and dynamical strain of the mechanical resonator, we observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps of these resonators under static strain. This allows us to enhance SiV-mechanical coupling and the mechanical coherence simultaneously, and provide a SiV-strain sensitivity with greatly improved accuracy over previous literature values. Thus, our work opens a pathway towards seconds-long coherence hybrid quantum systems utilizing point defects in diamond nanomechanics for quantum information processing.

papers.title: Collective sliding relaxor ferroelectricity across thousand-layer van der Waals superstructures
papers.summary: Relaxor ferroelectrics are among the most important electromechanical materials owing to their exceptionally large electrostrictive responses. However, conventional relaxor behavior is generally associated with chemical complexity and structural disorder, where local compositional fluctuations generate polar nanoregions, making the microscopic origin of this behavior difficult to control and engineer. Here we report sliding relaxor ferroelectricity (S-RFE), a previously unknown relaxor state in which engineered stacking-phase heterogeneity enables cooperative interlayer sliding to generate collective relaxor behavior. Through stacking-phase engineering in rhombohedral boron nitride, we create sliding domains that act as structural analogues of polar nanoregions and cooperatively align under an electric field through interlayer sliding.
