This collective state produces reversible electromechanical deformation of up to approximately $-1.6\%$ with negligible hysteresis in approximately 300-nm-thick crystals, corresponding to approximately 1000 atomic layers. The resulting electrostriction coefficient ($Q_{33}$ of approximately $1200\,\mathrm{m}^{4}\mathrm{C}^{-2}$) exceeds those of most crystalline electrostrictors by orders of magnitude. Unlike conventional relaxors, whose electromechanical response is often suppressed by dipolar freezing at low temperatures, S-RFE remains active down to 1.6 K and maintains giant electromechanical functionality. Our results establish sliding relaxor ferroelectricity as a new route to relaxor behavior and reveal how atomic-scale interlayer motion can be amplified into collective mesoscale functionality across approximately one thousand layers, providing a materials-by-design platform for electromechanical, photonic, and quantum technologies based on van der Waals materials.

papers.title: Incoherent dark excitons extend Floquet-like physics across time and momentum
papers.summary: Floquet phenomena - where a coherent, time-periodic drive hybridizes the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band - have been demonstrated with intense optical fields and, more recently, other bosonic excitations. However, within mean-field approximations and the current understanding of Floquet phenomena, these effects survive only for the coherence time of the drive, limiting practical use and current demonstrations to the sub-picosecond regime. Here, consistent with recent theoretical predictions beyond the mean-field picture, using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy in WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructures, we show that incoherent, dense populations of dark interlayer excitons hybridize the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band, mimicking Floquet-like phenomena - now persisting for nearly a nanosecond. With increasing interlayer exciton density, the valence band and its replica evolve from an inverted-parabolic to a Mexican-hat dispersion, a signature of the predicted non-zero static coupling that hybridizes the bands and scales linearly with the exciton density. By tuning twist angle, we further show that dark excitons with net momentum create replicas that hybridize with bands offset not just in energy but also in momentum, providing another powerful degree of freedom beyond conventional Floquet engineering. These results establish a robust, long-lived route to engineering electronic states, beyond a coherent, zero-momentum drive.

papers.title: Exceptional Points as Witnesses of Non-Gaussian Noise
papers.summary: Efficient control of quantum devices requires the knowledge of their environmental noise, yet the commonly measured power spectrum does not fully characterize non-Gaussian fluctuations of realistic environments. Here we show that exceptional points (EPs) in the noise-averaged dephasing response can expose observable signatures of non-Gaussian statistics, distinguishing environments with identical lower-order statistics. We also introduce a theoretical model that describes dephasing environments in terms of identical independent noise sources while preserving the power spectrum. Given a calibrated single-source model, the largest EP order extracted from the measured dephasing response determines the number of sources and predicts the higher-order statistics of the combined noise. We illustrate an atomtronic readout that maps distinct EP signatures onto an evolving ensemble-averaged atomic interference pattern. Our results connect non-Hermitian dynamics to environmental noise statistics, providing a route to characterize noise in quantum devices used in computing, metrology, and precision measurement.

papers.title: Pulse Laser Deposited GaFeO3 Thin Film Grown on FTO: Correlated Ferroic Orders and Strong Magnetodielectric Coupling at Room Temperature
papers.summary: Room-temperature single-phase multiferroics exhibiting coupled ferroelectric and magnetic order are promising candidates for next-generation magnetoelectric memory and spintronic technologies. Here, we report the growth of approximately 100.6 nm thick polycrystalline orthorhombic GaFeO3 thin films on fluorine-doped tin oxide-coated glass (FTO) substrates by pulsed laser deposition. Core-level X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a reduced Fe2+ concentration and suppressed oxygen-vacancy formation, contributing to reduced leakage current and improved ferroelectric characteristics. The films exhibit robust ferrimagnetism and ferroelectricity at room temperature, confirming the coexistence of ferroic orders within a single phase. Piezoresponse Force Microscopy further demonstrates reversible local polarization switching, accompanied by an asymmetric butterfly loop with coercive voltages of -0.31 V and +1.07 V. The films also exhibit a high relative dielectric constant of approximately 1700 with a relatively low dielectric loss tangent of approximately 2.83 at 1 MHz. Moreover, a significant magnetodielectric coefficient of approximately 2.3% is observed under a relatively small magnetic field of only 0.1 kOe, highlighting strong magnetoelectric coupling. These results establish GaFeO3 thin films as a promising platform for room-temperature multifunctional devices, mainly low-field magnetoelectric memory and spintronic architectures.

papers.title: Multiple Current Enhancement Regimes and Interaction Induced Re-entrant Transport in a Quasiperiodic Hubbard Ring with Antiferromagnetic Order
papers.summary: We investigate persistent charge and spin currents in a one-dimensional quantum ring threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm (AB) flux, considering generalized Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) modulation with staggered onsite energies and antiferromagnetic (AFM) ordering in both the noninteracting and interacting regimes, with the latter treated using a self-consistent Hartree-Fock mean field theory (MFT). At half filling, two distinct current-enhancement peaks emerge as the modulation strength increases, with quasiperiodic hopping modulation playing a crucial role in establishing the two-peak structure within a restricted parameter regime. Spin-resolved bond-current profiles reveal a switch in the dominant spin contribution between the two peaks, while the inverse participation ratio (IPR) and flux-dependent spin-resolved ground-state energies provide complementary insights into the spatial characteristics of the eigenstates and their spin-dependent flux sensitivity. At quarter filling, the spin current exhibits a single enhancement peak, in contrast to the two-peak response observed at half filling. The Hubbard interaction affects the two half-filled peaks differently: it suppresses the primary peak, whereas the secondary peak exhibits a nonmonotonic, re-entrant response, with the current recovering at finite interaction strength. The interacting results are further characterized through the Drude weight, and comparisons with exact diagonalization (ED) and density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations for a finite half-filled system support the reliability of the MFT description. Our findings elucidate how quasiperiodic modulation, AFM order, band filling, and electronic correlations collectively govern the magnitude and spin-resolved character of persistent currents, giving rise to multiple enhancement regimes and interaction-induced re-entrant behavior.

papers.title: HERA: Assessing an Autonomous Agent for Quantum Device Measurement
papers.summary: Large language model agents have begun to carry out laboratory measurements, but their scientific conclusions are useful only if they hold up under scrutiny. Demonstrating this requires controlled studies because models are stochastic and the context a model is given steers its conclusions. Here we introduce HERA, an autonomous agent designed to carry out cryogenic transport measurements of quantum devices. HERA draws on a knowledge base curated by lab members that holds measurement protocols, software tools, and literature references. We assessed HERA with a blinded trial against an expert on the stacking order of two multilayer graphene devices, an ablation of its knowledge base, and hundreds of offline replays in which models designed the trial's central measurement without running it. HERA's conclusions matched the expert's sealed conclusions on both tested devices. The ablation and the replay studies measured the impact of the knowledge base across different models, showing that with it every model designed better measurements and reasoned more soundly. To test how readily HERA extends to a new problem, we tasked it with finding and characterizing superconductivity in a different material system. This required a few hours of expert time to develop a new experimental protocol, after which HERA did both autonomously. These results show that, with a knowledge base designed for the task, language model agents are capable of sound experimental science.

papers.title: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
papers.summary: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time. We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian $SU(2)$ symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes $U(1)$ and $Z_2$ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.

papers.title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
papers.summary: Surface morphology is widely considered an indicator of thin-film quality, with smoother films generally expected to exhibit more uniform optoelectronic properties. Here, we demonstrate that substantial surface evolution does not necessarily lead to increased electronic heterogeneity in mixed-dimensional perovskite heterostructures. We investigate how low-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper capping layers derived from the sterically hindered 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium cation affect the spatial distributions of photoluminescence (PL) characteristics and quasi-Fermi level splitting (QFLS) in 3D perovskites. By combining statistical atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis with confocal, spatially resolved PL spectroscopy, we correlate surface topography with microscale optoelectronic properties. Although capping increases surface roughness and height asymmetry, it does not increase electronic inhomogeneity. Instead, the heterostructures exhibit enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and improved spatial uniformity of radiative QFLS compared with pristine 3D films. Under accelerated aging, this contrast becomes more pronounced: pristine films develop substantial spatial fluctuations in emission and QFLS, whereas capped heterostructures largely preserve their optoelectronic homogeneity. These findings indicate that the low-dimensional capping layer suppresses aging-induced optoelectronic disorder, demonstrating that electronic uniformity can be maintained despite morphological irregularity. This decoupling provides a design principle for developing durable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

papers.title: Mechanistic discovery in grain boundary structure and deformation driven by agentic AI
papers.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending these capabilities to domain-intensive mechanistic studies remains challenging. General grain boundaries (GBs) exemplify this challenge, as their structural complexity complicates experimental characterization and atomistic modeling. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general GBs, which are common in real polycrystals yet remain understudied. By integrating large language models into a modular architecture, GBClaw effectively combines systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis through iterative workflow refinement and dynamic replanning. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, the framework characterized interfacial defect structures and deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. It established a general approach to identify previously unobserved, widely spaced secondary GB misfit dislocations (SGBMDs) alongside closely spaced primary GB misfit dislocations (PGBMDs) in simulated atomic configurations and experimental images. Comparisons of GB sliding with and without SGBMDs revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of misfit-dislocation hierarchies in sliding resistance. Researcher-guided follow-up calculations further elucidated the structural origins of shear asymmetry and an anomalous shear response. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening and deep mechanistic discovery at complex material interfaces.

papers.title: Cu intercalation and field-driven filament formation in vertically aligned MoS$_2$ memristors
papers.summary: Vertically-aligned MoS$_2$ films paired with a Cu top electrode have been used as electrochemical metallization cell memristor devices. The memristive switching has been attributed to the formation of conductive filaments, yet their exact structure has remained elusive. Here we carry out a multi-scale computational study of Cu intercalation, clustering, and field-driven dynamics to eventually model the filament formation under operating conditions. We use density-functional theory results to fine-tune a machine learning force field, and the most important physical phenomena are further distilled into multi-particle kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. By exhaustive enumeration of Cu intercalated structures, we find the most stable structure at MoS$_2$Cu$_{0.11}$ composition, with Cu atoms forming a dice lattice between the MoS$_2$ layers. These structures are shown to exhibit metallic character and can thus form conductive filaments under memristor operation. The simulated switching speed and threshold voltage agree well with the available experimental data. Our results give fundamental insights on the device operation mechanism and guidelines for maximizing switching speed and endurance.

papers.title: Trieffect Dense Organic‐Derived Coating Enabling Synergistic Bulk Stability and Interfacial Reactivity for Superb Zn‐Mn Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT The practical application of aqueous Zn‐MnO 2 batteries is hindered by sluggish Zn 2+ diffusion kinetics, severe Mn dissolution, and “dead” MnO 2 accumulation in Mn 2+ ‐containg electrolytes, leading to inferior rate capability and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we designed an organic‐modified MnO 2 uniformly encapsulated by 1,4‐dihydroxybenzene (HQ) to simultaneously regulate bulk stability and interfacial reactivity of HQ‐MnO 2 hybrid (denoted as H‐MnO 2 ) via a facile solvent‐free ball milling method. In/ex situ characterization and theoretical calculation results reveal that the dense HQ‐derived coating with Mn─O─C interfacial bonds significantly boost charge diffusion kinetics and improves the structural robustness of H‐MnO 2 . Furthermore, the redox‐catalytic HQ‐derived layer with C═O/C─OH couples efficiently promotes selective H + insertion ability as well as boosts cathodic Mn 2+ /MnO 2 conversion to prevent irreversible ZnMn 2 O 4 and “dead” MnO 2 accumulation simultaneously. As a result, the Zn//H‐MnO 2 battery exhibits an outstanding capacity of 575 mAh g −1 , superior rate performance, and ultra‐long lifespan over 15 000 cycles. Moreover, 192.5 Wh kg H‐MnO2 −1 pouch cell with practical high‐mass loading maintained 100% capacity retention after 130 cycles, demonstrating the effectiveness of trieffect‐integrated organic interfacial engineering for high‐energy and durable Zn‐MnO 2 systems.

papers.title: Adaptive Supramolecular Interactions Govern Redox‐Active Molecules in Aqueous Redox Flow Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Weak noncovalent interactions critically govern molecular behavior in solution, yet how they shape redox processes in aqueous electrochemical environments remains underexplored. Here, we demonstrate control over the solubility and redox stability of aromatic redox‐active molecules in aqueous redox flow batteries (RFBs). Zwitterionic substitution of naphthalene diimide (NDI) bearing quaternary ammonium and sulfonate groups shows weak π–π cohesion through steric and electrostatic effects, rendering otherwise insoluble NDIs responsive to external anions. Hydrophobic and weakly hydrated anions such as iodide and bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide disrupt residual stacking through anion–π interactions, enabling dissolution to concentrations approaching 1.3 M. Upon electrochemical reduction, these anions dissociate, and the reduced NDI species are instead stabilized through spin pairing and cation‐mediated intermolecular interactions, which suppress irreversible aggregation, slow self‐discharge, and enable rapid redox reactions. Operando Raman spectroscopy, 1 H NMR, and EPR elucidate the redox‐state‐dependent evolution of these supramolecular assemblies. Together, these results establish zwitterionic molecular design for adaptive supramolecular redox chemistry in aqueous RFBs.

papers.title: Dual‑Site V/F Engineering in Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 (P 2 O 7 ) Cathodes: Concurrently Boosting Ionic Kinetics and Interfacial Robustness
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Sodium iron pyrophosphate (Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 (P 2 O 7 ), NFPP) is a compelling cathode candidate for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). Nevertheless, practical implementation is intrinsically constrained owing to deficient electrical conductivity and lethargic Na + transport kinetics. Herein, dual‑site V/F modification enhances electronic transport and interfacial robustness, offering a facile route to circumvent these limitations. Fluorine incorporation induces Fe─O bond elongation, effectively widening Na + migration channels to facilitate ionic transport while simultaneously enhancing both the mechanical robustness of the cathode‐electrolyte interphase (CEI) film and interfacial electronic conductivity. Furthermore, trace V 3+ occupancy on the Fe crystallographic site serves to rigidify the lattice while simultaneously creating an electronic conduction pathway through its t 2 g orbitals, mediating electron transfer during Fe 2+ oxidation. Concurrently, aliovalent V 3+ doping triggers substantial bandgap narrowing, decreasing it from 1.138 to 0.179 eV, drastically improving electrical conductivity. The optimized Na 4 Fe 2.955 V 0.03 (PO 3.985 F 0.03 ) 2 P 2 O 7 @C (NFV0.03PP‐F0.03@C) cathode exhibits exceptional electrochemical performance, retaining 93.9% capacity across 2000 cycles at 5 C (ultralow decay rate: 0.00356 mA h g −1 /cycle). Moreover, hard carbon||NFV0.03PP‐F0.03@C full cells retain 86.56% capacity after 400 cycles at 1 C. The present work clarifies how V/F dual‐site engineering optimises bulk structure and surface properties, thereby establishing reliable design principles for polyanion cathodes with fast‐charging durability.

papers.title: Unraveling the effects of electrodeposition pathway, phase evolution, and Mn incorporation in Co(OH)₂/PEDOT:PSS hybrid electrodes
papers.summary: Conductive polymer-supported transition metal hydroxides are promising electrode materials for electrochemical energy storage owing to their high pseudocapacitive activity. However, the influence of deposition strategy, deposited phase thickness, and heterometal incorporation on their structure–property–performance relationships remains insufficiently understood. In this study, cobalt-based hydroxide and oxide structures were electrodeposited onto PEDOT:PSS substrate, and the effects of deposition route, phase evolution, film thickness, and Mn incorporation were systematically investigated. Electrochemical measurements revealed that Co(OH)₂ films prepared by cyclic voltammetry exhibited superior performance compared to chronoamperometrically deposited counterparts. Among the Mn-containing electrodes, the Co:Mn=3:1 composition delivered the highest areal capacitance of 22.34 mF/cm² at 20 mV/s, corresponding to a mass-normalized capacitance of 18.62 F/g, calculated using the experimentally determined deposited-mass loading of 1.20 mg/cm². The electrode retained 82% of its capacitance as the current density increased from 10 to 100 µA/cm², and retained 63.94% of its initial capacitance after 1000 charge-discharge cycles. Structural analyses indicated predominantly amorphous or poorly crystalline architectures, while Raman and FTIR spectroscopy confirmed the formation of Co–OH, Co–O, and Mn–O bonds. AFM measurements showed that surface roughness increased from 1.7 nm for PEDOT:PSS to 6.5 nm after Co–Mn incorporation. Four-point probe measurements demonstrated that Mn addition partially compensated for the conductivity loss caused by cobalt hydroxide deposition, while Seebeck analyses confirmed the preservation of p-type transport behavior. These results demonstrate that electrochemical performance is governed not only by deposited-mass loading but also by the synergistic optimization of morphology, structural disorder, and electronic transport properties, providing useful design guidelines for PEDOT:PSS pseudocapacitive electrodes.

papers.title: Strengthened D‐p Orbital Hybridization Via Interlayer Coupling Enables Sulfur Redox Kinetics in Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT The inherent wide bandgap and large d‐p band center energy difference (Δε d‐p ) of δ‐MnO 2 significantly impede electron transport and ion diffusion, limiting its catalytic efficiency in lithium‐sulfur (Li─S) batteries. Herein, we report an interlayer coupling strategy that intercalates cetyltrimethylammonium (CTA + ) cations into birnessite (δ‐MnO 2 ) to simultaneously modulate the Mn 3d‐O 2p orbital hybridization and expand the Li + diffusion channels. Synchrotron X‐ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the strong electrostatic interaction between CTA + and the MnO 2 host layers narrows the d‐p band center energy difference (Δε d‐p ) from 1.458 to 1.145 eV, substantially enhancing Mn 3d‐O 2p orbital hybridization. This optimized d‐p matching renders the Mn d‐band more compatible with the S 2p orbitals of polysulfides, synergistically optimize adsorption energies and conversion barriers. Meanwhile, the CTA + expanded interlayer afford ordered Li + diffusion channels with a high Li + transference number and uniform Li deposition. Consequently, the Li─S batteries deliver a remarkable capacity of 819.07 mAh g − 1 at 3.0 C and sustain 850 cycles at 1.0 C with an capacity decay of only 0.05% per cycle. Significantly, the Li─S pouch cell equipped with a Bir(CTAB)‐separator delivers a high energy density of 305.25 Wh kg −1 .

papers.title: Spin-Orbit-Torque-Driven Recurrent Motion of Synthetic Antiferromagnetic Skyrmions for Magnetic Clocking
papers.summary: Magnetic skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnets have emerged as attractive information carriers for spintronic technologies due to their compensated topology, which mitigates the skyrmion Hall effect and facilitates reliable current-driven transport. Here we present a frequency-tunable magnetic clocking concept based on the recurring translational motion of SAF skyrmions and define the material conditions needed to realize it in a Pt/Co/Ru/Pt/Co multilayer. Using micromagnetic simulations, we investigate the combined effects of interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and interlayer Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida exchange coupling, delineating the parameter space in which coupled Néel-type skyrmions with opposite topological charges form a stable, topologically compensated pair. Under spin-orbit torque excitation, the SAF skyrmions exhibit resilient longitudinal transport with minimal transverse deflection using periodic boundary conditions. Periodic boundary conditions serve as an idealized model for closed-loop racetrack geometries, facilitating the study of continuous transport cycles and long-range steady-state dynamics. The oscillation frequency is readily modified by the applied current density and material characteristics, offering a pathway to field-free nanoscale timing components. Moreover, the threshold-activated initiation of recurrent transport mimics tonic-spiking behavior, indicating possible use in neuromorphic signal generation. This work establishes SAF skyrmions as versatile building elements for future spintronic functional devices by integrating topological protection, controllable transport, and cyclic dynamics.

papers.title: Fracture Mechanics and Self-Healing in Molecular Crystal Resonators for Lasing
papers.summary: Microscale damage poses a significant challenge to the reliability and longevity of miniaturized photonic devices; however, the mechanisms and repair of microscopic cracks and fractures in organic optical crystals remain largely unexplored. Here, we employ a mechanophotonic approach to induce microscale cracks and complete fractures in single crystals of 3-[4-(dimethylamino)phenyl]-1-(2-hydroxyphenyl)prop-2-en-1-one (HDMAC) using an atomic force microscopy (AFM) cantilever tip. We demonstrate the self-healing capability of these crystals while retaining their optical waveguiding and resonator properties, which are essential for lasing applications. HDMAC microcrystals exhibit self-healing of cracks introduced along the (010) and (001) crystallographic planes, demonstrating the versatility of this phenomenon across distinct crystal orientations. Furthermore, we identify different fracture mechanisms and establish a comprehensive assessment of healing efficiency by integrating optical loss measurements, resonator characteristics, and nanomechanical analyses. This multifaceted approach enables fair evaluation of the recovery of structural integrity and photonic functionality following self-healing.

papers.title: Water at the molecular frontier
papers.summary: Much of the water that matters most - flowing through biological cells and membranes, percolating through soils and rocks, or processed by filtration and desalination technologies - is not bulk water. It is water in nano- and molecular-scale confinement or at interfaces. Nanoscale water is therefore central to many challenges of our time, from the global water crisis and the water-energy nexus to catalysis, electrochemistry, and health. Beyond its applications, nanoscale water has emerged as a rich scientific field in its own right: discoveries are accumulating rapidly, revealing that confinement and interfacial forces produce a range of behaviours absent in the bulk. Sometimes this amounts to a renormalization of bulk properties; in other cases, new and non-intuitive phenomena emerge - exotic phases, anomalous transport, and dielectric responses that defy continuum expectations. A convergence of atomically precise nanofluidic devices, novel spectroscopies and microscopy approaches, and machine-learning-accelerated simulations is now exposing the molecular mechanisms behind these behaviours. This Perspective argues that the recent findings should not be viewed as isolated nanoscale anomalies, but as evidence for a molecular regime of water in which continuum descriptions must be rethought and molecular-level understanding becomes essential. Recognising and exploring this regime should have consequences ranging from fundamental physics to the rational design of future technologies that rely on water and dissolved ions.

papers.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
papers.summary: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. After correcting for collection and propagation losses, we obtain fidelities to the ideal state and quantum purities above 95%, together with near-optimal quadrature squeezing. The ability to generate a wide variety of Wigner-negative states with mature semiconductor technology opens promising opportunities for continuous-variable optical quantum technologies.

papers.title: Three-dimensional quantum Hall insulators in magnetic pyrochlore systems
papers.summary: We show that a class of pyrochlore materials provides a route to realize 3D Quantum Hall insulators, based on magnetic texture and flat band interference. We study itinerant electrons on a pyrochlore lattice Kondo-coupled to localized moments living on another interpenetrating pyrochlore lattice, with the moments forming a field-selected three-in/one-out texture. The noncoplanar texture generates complex spin-dependent hopping amplitudes and unequal local exchange energies, reconstructing the compact-localized parent flat bands into narrow bands separated by a global three-dimensional gap. The low-energy states are concentrated predominantly on kagome planes within the three-dimensional lattice, reflecting the combined effects of quantum interference and the texture-induced sublattice potential. When the lowest band is fully occupied, the response is characterized by a Chern triplet $\mathbf{C}=(1,1,1)$ and reciprocal Hall vector $\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{H}}=(2π/a)(1,1,1)$, giving $σ_{yz}=σ_{zx}=σ_{xy}=e^2/(ha)$. The quantized bulk Hall response enforces chiral surface spectral flow, visible as noncontractible Fermi loops at the surface. Our work opens a new direction in the search for three-dimensional quantum Hall physics in magnetic pyrochlore systems, and suggests a broad design principle based on the interplay of magnetic texture and flat-band interference.

papers.title: Evaluation of upper-scale mechanical parameters of particulate aluminum-based nanocomposites from molecular simulations
papers.summary: This paper focuses on the numerical and analytical determination of the mechanical parameters of aluminum-matrix nanocomposites using atomistic-scale simulations within a multiscale modeling framework. Molecular statics simulations were employed to evaluate the tensile and compressive behavior of Al based composites reinforced with nanosized alumina particles. Two classes of atomistic models were investigated. First, a unit-cell model containing a single Al2O3 monocrystal embedded in an aluminum matrix was used to examine the influence of the volume fraction of the ceramic inclusion on the effective mechanical properties. Second, a polycrystalline RVE model comprising an alumina particle was analyzed to assess the effect of the number of Al grains on effective properties. For each case, the mechanical response was characterized by stress-strain curves, enabling the identification of upper-scale material parameters associated with the elastic regime (bulk, shear and Young's modulus) and the damage stage (ultimate strength, ultimate strain, and failure strain). The isotropized elastic constants evaluated from molecular simulations were compared with classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill bounds to assess their applicability in the elastic regime. Finally, atomistic-scale simulation outputs provided insight into the dominant deformation/damage mechanisms (brittle versus ductile) and fracture modes (transgranular versus intergranular).

papers.title: Tunable turning point of the frequency--temperature response in suspended bilayer SiN_x/Al nanofilms
papers.summary: Non-invasive thermometry is highly desirable in cryogenic experiments to avoid the self-heating inherent in conventional sensors. In previous work, temperature was probed via the vibrational eigenfrequency of a suspended single-layer SiNx nanofilm. However, the turning point of the frequency-temperature curve limited the usable measurement range. Moreover, the slow thermal response confined measurements to a stepwise protocol with only discrete temperature points. Here, we show that these limitations can be overcome with a suspended bilayer SiNx/Al nanofilm, whose temperature-dependent vibrational eigenfrequency provides a monotonic, continuous, and repeatable temperature readout. The frequency-temperature dependence is governed by the mismatch between the effective coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) of the bilayer and the substrate, which makes the turning point tunable through the thickness ratio of the two layers. Over the 90 K to 300 K range, we characterize three bilayer nanofilms with different Al layer thicknesses and show how the turning point shifts with the thickness of the Al layer. For the sample with 72 nm Al, the turning point is pushed beyond 300 K, yielding a monotonic negative temperature coefficient over the entire 90 K to 300 K range. Combining a thin Al layer on the SiNx film with improved thermal anchoring of the chip shortens the thermal response to below 1 s, enabling continuous frequency tracking at a ramp rate of 3 K/min. We also demonstrate that the nanofilm with a 72 nm Al layer achieves a repeatability better than 150 mK above 175 K, and the frequency resolution of 1 Hz corresponds to a temperature resolution of ~5 mK.

papers.title: Helical Keratin‐Derived Aqueous Binders for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) possess ultrahigh energy density, low cost, and environmental friendliness, making them strong contenders for next‐generation energy storage technologies. However, their development is hindered by multiple interfacial challenges, including the shuttling of lithium polysulfides (LiPS), sluggish reaction kinetics, and severe volume expansion of the cathode. To address these issues, a multifunctional biomass‐derived aqueous binder was designed by crosslinking an α‐helical protein (α‐HP) with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and glycerol (GL). The α ‐helical structure of α‐HP in the α‐HP/PVA/GL adhesive acts as a “molecular spring”, effectively buffering volume expansion and stabilizing the electrode structure. Additionally, its abundant N‐ and O‐containing polar groups efficiently anchor LiPS, significantly suppressing the shuttling effect and accelerating redox kinetics. Consequently, lithium‐sulfur batteries employing the α‐HP/PVA/GL binder exhibit exceptional long‐term cycling stability. The α‐HP/PVA/GL cathode delivers an initial discharge specific capacity of 737.3 mAh g −1 and retains 487.9 mAh g −1 after 600 stable cycles at 2 C, with an average capacity decay rate of only 0.056% per cycle. This study provides a green, facile, and efficient strategy for developing multifunctional binders to overcome practical bottlenecks in lithium‐sulfur battery applications.

papers.title: Ammonium vanadate cathodes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries: design strategies and research progress
papers.summary: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) have attracted increasing attention as promising candidates for large-scale energy storage, owing to their high safety, environmental friendliness, and abundant zinc resources. Nevertheless, the development of high-performance AZIBs is constrained by cathode materials. Traditional cathode materials suffer from structural collapse, slow ion diffusion, and poor conductivity. In contrast, ammonium vanadates (AVOs) are being widely applied due to their unique structural advantages and higher Zn 2+ diffusion coefficients. This review focuses on the recent advancements in AVOs as high-performance cathode materials for AZIBs, analyzing the morphological variations among different AVOs and comparing their structural and electrochemical characteristics to elucidate the underlying structure-performance relationships. Moreover, key strategies to optimize their electrochemical performance are systematically discussed, such as defect engineering, interlayer spacing modulation, and composite construction with conductive materials. Finally, the review outlines current challenges and future research directions for advancing AVOs’ cathodes in practical AZIBs applications.

papers.title: Highly Conductive and Transparent Coatings via Low‐Temperature Hydroiodic Acid Vapor Treatment of Oxo‐Graphene Thin Films
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Transparent conductive graphene films are typically fabricated at processing temperatures above 500°C, making the applied processes unsuitable for flexible polymer substrates and limiting their integration into semiconductor device technologies. Here we demonstrate a method for fabricating such films at temperatures below 200°C. To this end, oxo‐graphene flakes are assembled into continuous films using the double self‐assembly technique. Subsequent hydroiodic acid (HI) vapor treatment at 40°C removes the oxygen‐containing groups and, combined with a mild 180°C annealing step on heat‐stable substrates, lowers the sheet resistance by more than a factor of five to about 3 kΩ/sq while preserving optical transparencies of up to 88% at 550 nm wavelength. The trade‐off between sheet resistance and transparency is set by the number of stacked layers, and on flexible polyethylene terephthalate (PET), where the annealing step is precluded, the films reach a sheet resistance of about 2.8 kΩ/sq after the HI step alone. These results demonstrate that the double self‐assembly of oxo‐functionalized graphene flakes, combined with mild HI‐vapor reduction and a 180°C annealing step, can deliver highly transparent and conductive graphene films while remaining compatible with semiconductor device technologies.

papers.title: High-efficiency solid-state electrochemical thermal switching through phonon engineering of 2D materials
papers.summary: Reversible solid-state thermal switches with large thermal contrasts remain rare, yet are essential for advanced thermal management. Using universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) and density functional theory (DFT), we screen 57 transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), spanning the 1T and 2H phases with Li and Mg intercalation. Among the candidates, Li$_a$ZrS$_2$ combines exceptional thermal conductivity switching with low heat capacity. Lithiation to Li$_{0.125}$ZrS$_2$ reduces the cross-plane thermal conductivity from approximately 3.7 to 0.05 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. The switching behaviour exceeds that of previously reported solid-state electrochemical thermal switches. Device-level modelling further demonstrates the potential for waste-heat recovery, with a pulsed system capturing 86\% of the energy recovered by an ideal switch. We attribute the switching behaviour to substantial softening of the Zr--Zr framework, with the mean force constant decreasing from approximately 4.2 to 1.2 eV $\mathrm{\mathring{A}}^{-2}$, alongside enhanced scattering of heat-carrying acoustic phonons. These findings establish electrochemical intercalation as a promising route to engineering thermal transport in layered materials.

papers.title: Stabilizing Interfaces in Magnesium Solid‐State Batteries via High‐Throughput Coating Design
papers.summary: ABSTRACT To meet the growing demand for affordable and safe electrochemical energy storage systems with high energy density, all‐solid‐state magnesium‐ion batteries (ASSMBs) have emerged as promising candidates, because magnesium is naturally abundant and offers high volumetric capacity. However, the electrochemical stability of magnesium solid electrolytes (SEs), as well as their chemical compatibility with magnesium cathodes, remains underexplored. Herein, we assess the electrochemical stability window (ESW) of magnesium SEs and evaluate their interfacial reactivity with magnesium cathodes by calculating the decomposition energy for SE–cathode pairs. Consequently, the mismatch between the ESW of magnesium SEs and cathode requirements should be addressed, underscoring the need for protective strategies. Accordingly, a high‐throughput screening for relevant coating materials is conducted, identifying 14 experimentally observed candidates from 19 098 magnesium‐containing inorganic compounds after thermodynamical screening. These compounds are further evaluated by computing their migration barriers for vacancy hopping, excluding seven compounds with exceptionally high vacancy‐diffusion barriers and leaving seven remaining coating candidates. Following this hierarchical screening, seven Mg‐containing compounds remained as particularly appealing candidates: MgBr 2 , Mg 3 B 7 ClO 13 , MgBHO 3 , Mg 3 Si(O 2 F) 2 , MgH 8 (ClO 2 ) 2 , Mg 3 Si 4 (HO 6 ) 2 , and Mg 7 P 2 (HO 2 ) 8 . This work provides fundamental insights into magnesium SEs and their interfacial stability, establishing a rational design framework to enhance overall cell performance in ASSMBs.

papers.title: High-Q, high-power spin Hall nano-oscillators with thick NiFe layers enabled by SiC substrates
papers.summary: Spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) are nanoscale microwave sources with potential applications in local spin excitation, neuromorphic computing, and oscillator-based Ising machines. Further improvements in output power and coherence are essential for these applications, and increasing the thickness of the ferromagnetic layer offers a promising route toward this goal. However, this comes at the cost of higher drive currents, which increase Joule heating and can degrade device performance. Here, we show that this bottleneck can be overcome by SiC substrates. By comparing otherwise identical W/NiFe nanoconstriction SHNOs on Al2O3, Si, and SiC, we find that the high thermal conductivity of SiC enables stable auto-oscillations in NiFe layers as thick as 10 nm, while the optimum performance occurs at 7 nm. The best SiC device reaches an average output power of 13.1 pW and a mean quality factor of Q = 23,000, representing the highest reported simultaneous output power and coherence for a single free-running SHNO. These results establish SiC and thermal substrate engineering as a route to thick-ferromagnet spintronic oscillators for coherent microwave generation in nanoscale devices.

papers.title: Nonlocal Einstein Relation in Confined Phonon Hydrodynamics
papers.summary: Einstein relations connect carrier mobility to macroscopic transport coefficients and constitute a fundamental link between microscopic dynamics and transport. In phonon hydrodynamics, this connection is conventionally local: the drift-induced thermal conductivity is proportional to the local drift mobility. Here we show that this relation becomes intrinsically nonlocal under spatial confinement. We derive a nonlocal Einstein relation, $κ_H(y) = \int P(y-y')μ(y'),dy'$, in which hydrodynamic thermal conductivity $κ_H(y)$ at one position depends on collective drift mobility $μ(y')$ across the entire cross-section of the channel. In the small-Knudsen-number limit, our nonlocal theory recovers the viscous heat equation and the local Einstein relation. At finite Knudsen number, nonlocality produces intrinsic boundary slip and distinct size-scaling behavior of the drift mobility $μ$ and hydrodynamic thermal conductivity $κ_H(y)$. First-principles calculations for graphite show that nonlocality broadens the channel-size window over which thermal conductivity exhibits superlinear size dependence. Temperature-dependent simulations further show that the nonlocal theory captures the emergence of a hydrodynamic peak in thermal conductivity normalized by ballistic conductance, whereas the local theory fails to accurately predict its magnitude. Our results establish a microscopic connection between collective phonon mobility and heat conduction beyond local hydrodynamics.

papers.title: First-Principles-Informed Modeling of Thermal Transport and Laser-Induced Heating in Ultrahigh-Temperature Carbides
papers.summary: Using first-principles density functional theory and Boltzmann transport calculations, we systematically investigate the electronic structure, lattice and electronic thermal transport, optical response, and laser-induced heating of ultrahigh-temperature carbides (UHTCs), including Group IV (TiC, ZrC, and HfC) and Group V carbides (VC, NbC, and TaC), and SiC. The transition-metal carbides (TMCs) exhibit metallic electronic structures, whereas SiC exhibits semiconducting character. The calculated thermal transport properties reveal distinct contributions from phonons and electrons, with electronic heat transport becoming increasingly important at elevated temperatures in TMCs. The Group V carbides exhibit substantially lower lattice thermal conductivity than their Group IV counterparts, accompanied by pronounced Kohn anomalies and modified phonon dispersions associated with their distinct electronic structures, suggesting a possible connection between Fermi-surface topology, phonon dynamics, and lattice thermal transport. In contrast, SiC exhibits comparatively high lattice thermal conductivity, consistent with its long-lived acoustic phonons, but no electronic contribution due to its semiconducting nature. Optical calculations reveal relatively high reflectivity in the visible and infrared spectral ranges for the metallic carbides, whereas SiC exhibits lower reflectivity in the infrared region. Finally, one-dimensional and three-dimensional continuum heat-conduction models are employed to compare the thermal responses of these materials under specified laser irradiation conditions. The predicted temperature distributions depend on the thermal and optical properties of the materials as well as the specimen geometry.

papers.title: Simultaneous suppression and temperature-driven crossover of particle-like and wave-like thermal transport in trigonal CsAg$_3$S$_2$
papers.summary: The simultaneous suppression of particle-like ($κ_p$ ) and wave-like ($κ_c$) thermal transport channels in crystalline materials remains a challenging problem, as reducing one channel can enhance the other. Here, we investigate the thermal transport in trigonal $P\Bar{3}m1$ CsAg$_3$S$_2$ using self-consistent phonon theory with cubic and quartic anharmonicity and the unified theory of thermal transport. Our calculations predict an ultralow lattice thermal conductivity of 0.222 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at 300 K, featuring simultaneously low $κ_p$ and $κ_c$ with a weak temperature dependence of $\sim$T$^{-0.42}$, which deviates significantly from the conventional $\sim$T$^{-1}$ behavior. This simultaneous suppression arises from localized Cs modes, which enhance anharmonic scattering, and the softer Ag-S framework, which reduces phonon group velocities, together suppressing $κ_p$, in conjunction with sparse, well-separated high-frequency S-derived optical modes that suppress $κ_c$ by limiting the coherent coupling between the phonon modes. Furthermore, the dominant transport channel exhibits a temperature-dependent crossover, with $κ_p$ contributing $\sim$74 \% of total lattice thermal conductivity at 300~K and $κ_c$ contributing $\sim$63 \% at 700~K. Combining the ultralow thermal conductivity with electrical transport calculated within the momentum relaxation time approximation (MRTA), we obtain a $ZT$ of 1.28 for $n$-type doping at 700 K. The present work not only clarifies the microscopic mechanism of ultralow thermal conductivity in trigonal CsAg$_3$S$_2$ but also identifies the covalent M-Ch framework modification within the AM$_3$Ch$_2$ family of ternary chalcogenides as an additional tuning parameter for further reducing $κ_p$ within the bonding-hierarchy design principle.

papers.title: Optical Thermometry in Monolayer WS2: Raman and Photoluminescence Spectroscopy from 5 K to 1273 K
papers.summary: Reliable temperature measurement is essential for characterizing and engineering two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor devices, yet optical thermometry of 2D materials has so far been demonstrated only over narrow temperature windows spanning a few hundred kelvin. Here, we establish a comprehensive optical thermometry framework for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K. We show that: (i) the out-of-plane A1g Raman mode shifts linearly with temperature above 100~K, with a slope of -0.0138 cm^{-1}/K in non-encapsulated WS2 (fitted over 298-1223~K) and a measurably smaller slope of -0.0121 cm^{-1}/K in an hBN-encapsulated sample (fitted over 100-1273~K); (ii) photoluminescence spectra measured over the same 5--1273~K range provide an independent optical indicator of the temperature: the neutral-exciton emission redshifts continuously with temperature and is well described by the semi-empirical Pässler model. The two indicators probe distinct physical mechanisms, lattice anharmonicity and bandgap renormalization, and together provide contact-free thermometry for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K, an approach applicable to 2D semiconductors more broadly.

papers.title: Interfacial Orbital Rashba Edelstein Effect Identified in CoO/Cu/Pt Trilayers
papers.summary: We investigate the generation of orbital angular momentum currents at engineered Cu-oxide interfaces using CoO/Cu/Pt thin-film trilayers. Angular-dependent magnetoresistance measurements on samples with varying Cu interlayer thickness reveal systematic changes in both longitudinal and transverse resistance components, including a sign inversion of the signal. By systematically varying the Cu interlayer thicknesses, we disentangle the spin and orbital contributions to the magnetoresistive response. Our results show that large orbital currents originate from the interfacial orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect due to the presence of the Cu-O bonds at the CoO/Cu interface. Unlike previously studied CoO/Cu bilayers that rely on uncontrolled natural oxidation, our trilayer geometry enables reproducible and stable orbital-current generation at ambient conditions. Our results identify Cu-oxide interfaces as efficient sources of orbital angular momentum and clarify the microscopic mechanism underlying orbital current generation. Consequently, this work establishes a well-defined materials platform for all-orbitronic devices that does not require relativistic spin-orbit coupling or orbital-spin interconversion processes.

papers.title: Decoding Composition-Structure-Performance Relations in Sodium Layered Oxide Positive Electrode Materials
papers.summary: Layered sodium transition-metal (TM) oxides, Na$_x$TMO$_2$, are among the most promising sodium-ion positive electrode materials, yet their Na/vacancy orderings, layer stacking sequences, and cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions are known only for a few single-TM compounds. We compile the Na/vacancy orderings reported in earlier studies into a single library of 41 unique orderings and apply this uniformly to five single-TM and all ten Na$_x$TM$_{0.5}$TM$'_{0.5}$O$_2$ oxides (TM = Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni), screening more than 120,000 structures with machine-learning interatomic potentials prior to 1,025 accurate first-principles calculations. The phase diagrams explain the observed O3/P3/O1 sequences and voltages, and the O3-to-P3 competition hinges on ordering energies of a few meV per atom that scalar descriptors, such as the cationic potential and the interlayer-slab distance, miss. Our extensive analysis reveals that the redox couples form a nearly partner-independent ladder, Ti$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Mn$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Co$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Ni$^{2+/3+}$ $<$ Fe$^{3+/4+}$, explaining pristine charge transfer and the oxidation sequence. Van Vleck analysis of every TMO$_6$ octahedron reveals that TM mixing suppresses the cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions of Mn$^{3+}$ and Ni$^{3+}$ through charge transfer to Jahn--Teller-inactive states or dilution of Jahn--Teller-active centers. We formulate an energy-density-versus-strain map that yields a design rule: a high-voltage couple without Jahn--Teller strain, which Mn$^{4+}$/Ni$^{2+}$ charge transfer realizes in Na$_x$Mn$_{0.5}$Ni$_{0.5}$O$_2$, the most practical composition. We release the ordering-resolved dataset as a training set for subsequent training of accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials.

papers.title: Wrinkling dynamics of thin crystalline sheets and its dependency on topological defects
papers.summary: We investigate the wrinkling dynamics of thin crystalline sheets under uniaxial compression using a Surface Phase-Field-Crystal-Helfrich (SPFCH) model, which captures the coupling between crystalline order, out-of-plane deformations, and topological defects. In particular, the model allows us to track and characterize two distinct classes of defects, namely those forming in the underlying hexagonal crystal lattice, such as dislocations and grain boundaries, and defects in the wrinkling patterns, known as wrinklons. By resolving the evolution and interactions of these defects, we investigate how the interplay between in-plane and out-of-plane relaxation mechanisms influences wrinkling onset and the coarsening regime. Our results indicate that crystalline defects do not affect coarsening scaling, but they quantitatively affect the onset of wrinkling and the emerging wrinkling wavelength, promote more irregular wrinkle patterns with a higher density of wrinklons, and modify long-timescale morphological evolution.

papers.title: Phonon-assisted shift-current from first-principles: application to AlN monolayer
papers.summary: In this work, we present a first-principles approach to investigate phonon-assisted shift current in extended systems. Our method combines the special displacement technique with real-time simulations based on the dynamical Berry phase. Merging these two frameworks enables direct access to non-linear optical responses at finite temperatures, while naturally incorporating phonon scattering and phonon-assisted electronic transitions into the time-dependent dynamics. This allows us to capture temperature-dependent features and lattice fluctuations that are essential for a realistic description of non-linear photocurrent generation. As a representative example, we apply our approach to the shift-current response of a monolayer of hexagonal AlN (h-AlN). This system provides an ideal testing ground because it features an indirect band gap and lacks inversion symmetry. Moreover, h-AlN layers of different thicknesses have been fabricated and characterized in a variety of experimental settings, opening the concrete possibility of testing our predictions. Our results demonstrate the relevance of phonon-mediated processes and the importance of temperature in determining the magnitude and spectral features of the shift current in layered materials.

papers.title: Pulsed Laser Deposition of Ferroelectric SrTiO3 Shells Enables Polarization-Controlled Charge Separation in TiO2 Photoanode
papers.summary: Ferroelectric polarization offers a powerful route to govern the interfacial charge separation in photoelectrodes; however, chemically converted ferroelectric shells lack sub-nanometer thickness control, coherent strain retention, and chemically clean interfaces. Here, we use pulsed laser deposition to fabricate stoichiometric SrTiO3 shells on hydrothermally grown TiO2 nanorod arrays, achieving atomically defined core-shell architectures while preserving the one-dimensional transport geometry. The photocurrent density followed a volcano-shaped dependence on shell thickness and reached 1.9 mA cm-2 at 1.23 V versus RHE under AM 1.5G illumination for the optimized 15-mins sample, exceeding the established hydrothermal benchmark. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed a tetragonally distorted, oxygen-stoichiometric shell, identifying coherent interfacial strain rather than defect dipoles as the origin of the ferroelectric order. Kelvin probe force microscopy directly imaged a polarization-induced built-in electric field whose magnitude scaled with charge-transfer efficiency and photocurrent density. Together, these complementary structural, chemical, electrostatic, and device-level measurements established a quantitative strain-polarization-built-in field-charge separation relationship. This work transforms ferroelectric photoanode engineering from empirical optimization into an atomically controllable and predictive materials strategy for high-efficiency solar water-splitting devices. This approach is readily extendable to visible-light absorbers and complex ferroelectric heterostructures.

papers.title: Synthetic staggered fields switch Neel vectors probed by magnetic resonance
papers.summary: Electrical detection of antiferromagnetic order is a critical challenge for antiferromagnetic spintronics owing to their vanishing macroscopic magnetisation. While magnetic resonance has demonstrated sub-terahertz antiferromagnetic spin pumping and nonlinear magnon dynamics, its application to electrically contacted on-chip devices has room for further exploration. Here we show that magnetic resonance enables direct electrical detection of Néel vector states. A $180^\circ$ reversal in synthetic antiferromagnets is realised by current-driven effective fields with opposite polarisation acting on each magnetic sublayer, which we term synthetic staggered fields. The switching induces a $π$ phase shift of precessional motion in time, producing hysteretic rectified voltages in our phase-sensitive detection scheme. Angular-dependent resonance analysis offers further insight into the Néel vector directions, pointing to a model beyond the macrospin formalism. We address this by defect-incorporated micromagnetic simulations that reveal fragmented domain states after current excitation. An extracted current density of $7.4\times10^{9}$ A/m$^2$ is, to our knowledge, the lowest reported value for the room-temperature Néel vector switching and we show that it scales with the in-plane uniaxial anisotropy both experimentally and numerically. Synthetic staggered fields and the resonance-based methodology provide a research platform for nanoscale characterisation of electrically driven antiferromagnetic textures, guiding the development of high-frequency on-chip spintronic architectures.

papers.title: Lifshitz Phase of Quantum Gravity: The Infrared Fixed Point of the (2+1)D Unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons Model
papers.summary: We consider a nonrelativistic gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions with $w_\infty$ gauge symmetry that we call unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity. The theory has three dimensionless couplings, one of which is the Chern-Simons level $κ$. At large $|κ|$, the theory flows from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR fixed point with anisotropic scale invariance characterized by a dynamical critical exponent $z=2-\tfrac32|κ|^{-1}$. We speculate that unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity undergoes a phase transition from this scale-invariant phase to a confining phase when $κ$ drops below a critical value.

papers.title: Perpendicular Anisotropy and g-Factor of Sputtered Ni Films on Si(111) Studied by Angle-Dependent Ferromagnetic Resonance
papers.summary: Ni films with thicknesses of 312 and 1011\,Å were grown on Si(111) by dc magnetron sputtering at room temperature and studied by atomic force microscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, X-ray reflectivity, magnetometry and angle-dependent ferromagnetic resonance. Both films are polycrystalline fcc Ni with smooth surfaces, a bulk-like (111) lattice spacing and a saturation magnetization of ${\approx}480$\,emu\,cm$^{-3}$, and both are magnetized in plane. The angular dependence of the resonance field, from the film plane to the film normal, is described by a uniaxial anisotropy model with first- and second-order terms. From this model, $g = 2.160\pm0.005$ and $2.101\pm0.014$ and effective perpendicular anisotropies of $(6.0\pm0.4)\times10^{5}$ and $(4.5\pm0.6)\times10^{5}$\,erg\,cm$^{-3}$ were obtained for the thinner and thicker film, respectively. The conventional analysis of only the in-plane and perpendicular resonances gives $g$-factors that are lower by 0.02--0.04. The perpendicular linewidths give upper limits for the Gilbert damping of $α\le 0.030$ and $\le 0.038$.

papers.title: Co layer Thickness Driven Structural Evolution and Magnetic Behaviour of Co/Ir/Co Trilayers
papers.summary: Ferromagnetic heavy-metal (FM/HM) trilayer heterostructures provide a versatile platform for investigating the interplay between structural and magnetic properties. In this study, we investigate the effect of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of sputter-deposited $\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})/\mathrm{Ir}(5\,\mathrm{nm})/\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})$ varying from 2 to 10 nm. Structural characterization using grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) reveals a nanocrystalline structure, with the crystallite size increasing with Co-layer thickness. Furthermore, X-ray reflectivity (XRR) reveals a thickness-dependent variation in interface morphology, with the interface roughness ratio reaching a maximum at $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 4$ nm. Temperature-dependent zero-field-cooled and field-cooled (ZFC-FC) magnetization measurements reveal thickness-dependent characteristic temperatures and multiple relaxation regimes in selected samples, indicating complex thermally activated magnetic behaviour. In contrast, field-dependent hysteresis measurements reveal that the saturation magnetization increases with Co-layer thickness, whereas the coercivity exhibits a pronounced non-monotonic variation, with enhanced values at intermediate thicknesses. Moreover, low-temperature hysteresis loops display thickness-dependent exchange-bias-like shifts, particularly for $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 2$-$4$ nm. These findings highlight the strong influence of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of Co/Ir/Co trilayers.

papers.title: Dephasing-powered open quantum-dot battery
papers.summary: We propose a simple realization of an open quantum battery powered by local dephasing. The setup consists of a triple-quantum-dot chain coupled at one end to a thermal reservoir, with the dot at the opposite end strongly detuned to form a high-energy storage element. Local dephasing populates this highly excited state and autonomously drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state with high ergotropic efficiency. We find a limit where the ergotropic efficiency approaches unity, while the ergotropy itself approaches one-third of the energy detuning. We characterize the battery through its energy-storage performance, charging time, and stability, showing that the charged state remains long-lived after the dephasing source is switched off. We then demonstrate two complementary protocols for extracting the stored energy. First, nearly all the available ergotropy can be recovered through a simple cyclic unitary protocol involving only modulation of the detuned-dot gate. Second, coupling the detuned dot to an electronic load allows the extraction of electrochemical work exceeding the initial ergotropy, thereby accessing part of the battery's passive energy. Our results establish local dephasing as an autonomous resource for charging open quantum batteries and demonstrate simple routes for extracting the resulting stored energy in experimentally accessible mesoscopic platforms.

papers.title: Dynamic Solvation Perturbation Enables Fast‐Exchange Interfacial Water Regulation for Stable Aqueous Zinc Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Interfacial instability remains the major barrier for practical aqueous zinc batteries. Conventional electrolyte design mainly focuses on reducing water coordination number in the Zn 2+ solvation shell. However, this static criterion often neglects ligand‐exchange kinetics and can still leave highly reactive water at the interface. Herein, we propose a dynamic solvation perturbation (DSP) strategy to regulate Zn 2+ solvation through transient solvent coordination. Descriptor‐guided screening identifies methyl acetate (MA) as an optimal modulator with balanced Zn 2+ coordination and water regulation. MA forms a fast‐exchange mixed solvation sheath, shortens water residence time, and passivates residual water via dynamic solvation‐shell rearrangement. Additionally, MA exhibits facet‐selective adsorption on Zn anode, which suppresses direct water attack and promotes uniform Zn nucleation. As a result, the DSP‐regulated electrolyte enables the Zn anode to achieve long‑term cycling life over 8000 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . Remarkably, stable cycling is maintained for more than 2000 h at 32% DOD and more than 1000 h at 80% DOD. In addition, the Zn||V 2 O 5 pouch‐cell with the MA‐containing electrolyte exhibits approximately 80% capacity retention over 300 cycles at 0.1 A g −1 , highlighting its potential for practical applications.

papers.title: Amorphization Unlocks Active Sites in Organic Small Molecules for Ah‐Level Aqueous Ammonium‐Ion Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT The performance of most organic rechargeable batteries is strongly hindered by insufficient active site exposure arising from strong molecular stacking. To address this issue, an amorphization strategy is implemented to disrupt strong intermolecular π–π stacking in the small molecule 2,3,7,8‐tetraamino‐5,10‐dihydrophenazine‐1,4,6,9‐tetraone (TDT), thereby improving electrolyte accessibility and activating buried redox sites. Amorphous TDT exhibits a high specific surface area of 738 m 2 g −1 , delivers 242.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , and retains 87.1% of its initial capacity after 817 cycles over 2900 h. In situ ATR‐FTIR and EQCM‐D measurements reveal that NH 4 + is preferentially adsorbed and stored through coordination and deprotonation, while interfacial NH 4 + accumulation induces localized hydrolysis to generate H 3 O + for subsequent proton storage. The TDT||CuFe‐PBA full cell retains 100% of its initial capacity over 100 000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Moreover, the first Ah‐level AAIB pouch cell delivers 1.037 Ah at an average voltage of 1.14 V, demonstrating the practical promise of amorphous organic small molecule for durable, high capacity AAIBs.

papers.title: Proton diffusion in hydrogen tungsten bronzes and beyond: A comprehensive review
papers.summary: Abstract Hydrogen tungsten bronzes (H x WO 3 ) have attracted renewed interest owing to their high hydrogen incorporation capacity and fast proton diffusion, which underpin their emerging applications beyond conventional chromic devices. However, the reported proton diffusion coefficients ( D H ) in H x WO 3 exhibit a striking scatter over several orders of magnitude, hindering a unified understanding of proton transport. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of proton diffusion in H x WO 3 , with particular emphasis on the experimental methodologies used to evaluate the diffusion coefficients and the structural and electronic properties of WO 3 . We also summarize previous studies on the microscopic behavior of protons in electronically conductive H x WO 3 . Based on these findings, we discuss the factors governing fast proton diffusion in H x WO 3 . Proton diffusion in this system cannot be understood solely in terms of structural factors; rather, it is strongly influenced by the electronic carrier density and the degree of electron delocalization. These two factors have not been explicitly considered in conventional ion-conducting materials, highlighting the importance of an electronic-structure-based perspective. Such insights not only rationalize the unique proton transport properties of H x WO 3 but also provide a framework applicable to other hydrogen bronzes and mixed protonic-electronic conductors, thereby accelerating the development of hydrogen-related functional materials.

papers.title: Dual‐Functional Acetate Intercalation in NiMn‐LDH Cathode: Interlayer Pillaring and Electronic Delocalization Toward Advanced Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are regarded as attractive candidates for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their further development remains constrained by sluggish ion/electron transport and limited structural stability of cathode materials. To overcome these limitations, we designed an acetate‐intercalated NiMn layered double hydroxide cathode (Ac‐NiMn‐LDH) using a template‐guided assembly route. This approach effectively mitigates the restacking of NiMn‐LDH nanosheets, endowing the material with a robust structure and enlarged active surface area. Serving as functional pillars, the intercalated acetate anions expand the interlayer gallery and weaken Zn 2+ ‐host interactions, thereby reducing ion‐migration resistance and reinforcing the layered structure. Furthermore, the strong electronic coupling between the acetate groups and the host layers triggers localized charge redistribution, promoting d‐electron delocalization at Mn/Ni sites and enhancing charge transport. Benefiting from this coupled structural and electronic regulation, the Ac‐NiMn‐LDH cathode achieves a capacity of 274.6 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 and retains stable cycling at 1 A g −1 , corresponding to a low capacity decay of 0.002% per cycle over 2200 cycles. Moreover, flexible AZIBs assembled with this cathode operate steadily under bending deformation. This work offers a synergistic strategy for modulating both the physical architecture and electronic states of layered cathodes for advanced AZIBs.

papers.title: All-soft organic electrochemical diodes based on asymmetric active layers for signal isolation in deformable electronics
papers.summary: All-soft electronics have emerged as a promising platform for deformable and human-centric systems, yet the development of mechanically compliant diodes remains a major challenge due to limitations in material compatibility, device architecture, and stable operation under deformation. Electrochemical approaches offer a viable route to address this challenge by enabling bulk, low-voltage charge modulation in soft materials without relying on rigid junction interfaces. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first all-soft organic electrochemical diode (OECD) based on an asymmetric active-layer geometry. The device incorporates a transfer-printed ultrathin ion-gel interface that preserves conformal coverage and the active electrochemical architecture under strain. The device achieves high rectification through polarity-dependent electrochemical potential redistribution, with a rectification ratio of up to 2.23 × 10 4 at ±1 V and stable operation under tensile strains of up to 30% and repeated mechanical deformation. This ion-gel-based architecture preserves the electrochemical asymmetry required for diode operation while maintaining structural integrity under strain. Beyond the individual device, the all-soft OECD enables deformable rectifiers and logic gates and functions as a key signal-isolation element that suppresses cross-talk in a deformable pressure-sensing array. These results establish an electrochemical diode platform that combines mechanical deformability, high rectification performance, and circuit-level compatibility, providing a pathway toward fully deformable and integrated human-centric electronic systems.

papers.title: Synchronic Multilevel Assembly Toward Mesoporous Nanosized Intercalation‐Type Framework Anodes for Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Intercalation‐type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast‐charging sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation‐type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic‐scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M‐Na 4 Ti 5 O 12 /C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g −1 at 10 A g −1 ) and cycling stability (<0.023% capacity fade per cycle over 1000 cycles at 0.2 A g −1 ) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na + diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low‐barrier, nanoscale ion‐conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg −1 and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high‐rate battery materials.

papers.title: 3D‐Nanostructured ITO Enables High‐Loading Prussian Blue Cathodes for Zn‐Based Electrochromic Smart Windows
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Prussian Blue (PB) is an attractive electrochromic cathode material for aqueous electrochromic energy‐storage smart windows, but its performance remains limited by the low areal capacity of thin‐coatings deposited on planar transparent conductive oxides. Here, we overcome this limitation by combining galvanostatic electrodeposition with 3D‐nanostructured ITO electrodes, enabling conformal growth of PB with high‐loadings, while maintaining mechanical stability and fast electrochemical response. The resulting electrodes sustain charge densities up to 100 mC/cm 2 at relatively high rates. When integrated into Zn/PB smart window devices, they enable fast and homogeneous coloration/bleaching with enhanced optical contrast and charge storage capacity, while also exhibiting high cyclability. Device configurations based on reversible Zn electrodeposition onto a transparent ITO counter electrode enable improved control over optical contrast and electric field distribution, while a three‐electrode architecture incorporating a sacrificial Zn anode provides a route toward in situ regeneration of the electrochromic cathode and extended device lifetime.

papers.title: Intrinsic Paramagnetism of Optical Phonons and Thermal Hall Effect in Quantum Paraelectrics
papers.summary: We propose a microscopic theory of the phonon-mediated thermal Hall effect in quantum paraelectrics, driven by the intrinsic paramagnetism due to quantum fluctuations of the (nearly) critical optical phonon modes. The effective magnetization due to temporal fluctuations of the assosciated dipoles couple to an external magnetic field resulting the magnetoelectric term $\mathbf{H} \cdot (\mathbf{P} \times \dot{\mathbf{P}})$ in the effective Lagrangian density of the polarisation field $\mathbf{P}$. This coupling splits the transverse optical phonon spectrum into right- and left-circularly polarized chiral branches. Using the chiral phonon Green's functions and the Kubo formalism, we derive the thermal Hall conductivity $κ_{xy}$ from the heat-current correlation function. We observe that $κ_{xy}$ is proportional to the difference in spectral weights of the two chiral modes, $κ_{xy} \propto A_+^2 - A_-^2$, establishing a direct microscopic link between phonon chirality and transverse heat transport. Our theory predicts three key observations: (i) a linear-in-magnetic-field response $κ_{xy} \propto H$ at low fields, evolving into nonlinear behavior at higher fields (ii) a non-monotonic temperature dependence of $κ_{xy}$ with a peak arising from the competition between thermal population and phonon scattering and (iii) strong enhancement of $κ_{xy}$ near the quantum critical point $ω_0 \to 0$, it exhibits power-law scaling $κ_{xy} \propto T^α$ with $α\approx 0.41$. Our findings provide an understanding of thermal Hall transport in quantum paraelectrics due to intrinsic paramagnetism and is aligned with the observed behaviour in SrTiO$_3$ and related materials.

papers.title: Nanoscale origin of thermal anisotropy in monoclinic \texorpdfstring{$β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$}{beta-Ga2O3}
papers.summary: Monoclinic $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is a promising ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, but its low and anisotropic thermal conductivity limits heat removal, making it a compelling model system for nanoscale thermal transport studies. Here, we demonstrate a pronounced nanoscale enhancement of thermal anisotropy and uncover the underlying phonon mechanism by combining complementary thermal and acoustic spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations. Anisotropic thermoreflectance thermometry determines the full thermal-conductivity tensor from angular measurements within the (100), (010), and (001) crystallographic planes. Angle-resolved Brillouin light scattering reveals that low-frequency acoustic phonons exhibit only weak velocity anisotropy, insufficient to account for the measured thermal anisotropy. Frequency-resolved ab initio Green--Kubo calculations show that the bulk anisotropy pattern emerges only when the accumulated conductivity includes phonon modes above 4 THz, whereas the sub 3 THz acoustic contributions are nearly isotropic. Extreme-ultraviolet transient thermal grating spectroscopy reveals that reducing the grating period to 28 nm strongly enhances the in-plane thermal anisotropy, most markedly in the (001) plane, where it reaches nearly twice its macroscopic value. Reconstructed and calculated mean-free-path (MFP) accumulation functions link this enhancement to the stronger directional contrast of short-MFP phonons. Together, these results identify high-frequency, short-MFP phonons as the dominant origin of thermal anisotropy in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$, while low-frequency phonons attenuate the directional contrast at macroscopic scales.

papers.title: Thermoelectric properties and modulation doping of ultrawide-bandgap nitride monolayers
papers.summary: Two-dimensional III-nitride alloys provide a composition-tunable platform for exploring thermoelectric transport and intrinsic electric-field tolerance. We combine first-principles electronic-structure calculations with semiclassical transport for ordered monolayer B$_{x}$Al$_{1-x}$N and B$_{x}$Ga$_{1-x}$N. State-dependent momentum relaxation times computed with AMSET include acoustic deformation-potential and piezoelectric scattering. Using a common, temperature-independent lattice thermal conductivity of 550 W/mK, we predict maximum thermoelectric figure of merit ZT>2.5 for selected p- and n-type monolayers and ZT>2 at 300~K for n-type B$_{0.25}$Ga$_{0.75}$N. Composition-dependent band curvature, screening, and scattering help interpret the different p- and n-type responses. Vacuum-referenced band alignments identify candidate modulation-doping partners for both carrier types; explicit hGaN/V$_2$O$_5$ calculations yield a hole surface density of approximately 1.6$\times10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$.
