A separate phenomenological model using the band gap and maximum phonon frequency predicts intrinsic breakdown fields of 20.06 and 20.74 MVcm for the Al- and Ga-containing x=0.75 alloys, respectively. These results motivate further investigation for thermoelectric and high-field power-electronic applications. The ZT values apply to the specified scattering and lattice-conductivity models, while the breakdown estimates require validation for monolayers and do not resolve field direction.

papers.title: Excitonic Stark Response Induced by Quantum Capacitance in van der Waals Heterostructures
papers.summary: Precise electrostatic control in van der Waals heterostructures is commonly described by a geometric capacitor model, which assumes that the internal electric field is fully determined by external gate voltages. Here, we show that this description breaks down in the presence of interfacial charge transfer, where quantum capacitance modifies the internal electrostatics. Using interlayer excitons as local probes, we observe a dipole-dependent energy splitting that persists even when the gate-induced geometric field is nominally canceled. This splitting reflects incomplete cancellation between gate- and carrier-induced fields set by quantum capacitance, while many-body renormalization is largely symmetric with respect to the two opposite dipole orientations, allowing the splitting to provide a direct optical measure of the local chemical potential. Our results reveal the central role of quantum capacitance in interface electrostatics and provide a route to probe it in operando.

papers.title: Rationalizing charge transfer: a single-molecule case study across three distinct surfaces
papers.summary: Organic molecules are versatile building blocks for the formation of complex low-dimensional nanostructures on surfaces. Recently, interest has grown in translating on-surface synthetic protocols from noble metal surfaces to insulating surfaces, which offer technological relevance, and to magnetic or superconducting surfaces, which offer new routes to correlated phases. It is important, therefore, to understand how these alternative surfaces may alter the properties of adsorbates through processes like charge transfer and screening. Evidence for charge transfer is often obtained experimentally via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), and theoretically via density functional theory (DFT). In this work, we systematically compare the properties of isolated macrocyclic emeraldine (Me$_6$) molecules on three different surfaces: metallic Au(111), a semiconducting ferromagnetic monolayer of FeCl$_2$, and a cleaved superconducting surface of bulk 2H-NbSe$_2$. We show that STS and DFT alone are insufficient to quantify charge transfer for these cases. Instead, we complement these methods with Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements and model Hamiltonian calculations to demonstrate that on Au(111) and FeCl$_2$, Me$_6$ molecules donate a single electron to the substrate, whereas on NbSe$_2$ two electrons are transferred from molecule to substrate. Our work provides insight into the interplay of charge transfer, screening, and molecule-substrate coupling, and develops experimental and theoretical methods for comparing the properties of adsorbates across different surfaces for future studies.

papers.title: First- and Second-Order Electron Position Correlators Reveal Topological Phase Transitions
papers.summary: The theory of conventional critical phenomena is built around the concepts of fluctuations and correlators of local observables. Here, we show that topological phase transitions can also be characterized through spatial and temporal two-point correlation functions associated with fluctuations of the electronic position operator. The key object is the antisymmetric part of the position-position correlation function, which yields the Chern number in the equal-time and equal-space limit. When the system is translationally invariant in space or time (the latter case corresponding to an equilibrium condition), these two-point correlators reduce to one-variable functions of the remaining variable. Remarkably, these functions are both reminiscent of critical behaviour, including divergent correlation times and lengths signalling the phase transitions. Away from these conditions, namely in non-periodic systems or genuinely dynamical processes, criticality is instead better captured by higher-order Chern-Chern correlators constructed from local or dynamical markers obtained as coincident-point limits of the position correlators. These higher-order Chern-Chern correlators can be seen as double Levi-Civita contractions of second-order position correlators, selecting the antisymmetric sector in each index pair. We substantiate this framework through numerical simulations and analytic calculations. Our results establish a general correlator-based description of topological phase transitions, applicable to crystalline, noncrystalline, equilibrium, and dynamical systems.

papers.title: Side-Chain Engineering Controls Molecular Packing and Vertical Electron Transport in Discrete n-Type NDI-T2 Oligomers
papers.summary: High-efficiency vertical charge transport in multilayer organic optoelectronic devices highly depends on molecular structure and arrangement. Using two T2-(NDI-T2)2 conjugated oligomers with ethylhexyl (EH) and octyldodecyl (OD) side chains as a model system, their effects on electron transport are investigated using, among other techniques, atomic force microscopy (AFM), conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM), grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS), steady-state optical spectroscopy, and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations. The oligomers of both materials exhibit relatively disordered structures in the as-cast state, whereas annealing enhances structural order and leads to side-chain-dependent changes in molecular stacking. EH-based films show a smaller annealing-induced photoluminescence shift than OD-based films, suggesting less pronounced stacking and conformational rearrangements, consistent with TDDFT-supported exciton analysis. The current-voltage characteristics are analyzed using the space-charge-limited current (SCLC) model. After annealing, both materials exhibit improved vertical electron mobility. The EH-based films reach a maximum mobility of 1.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1. The combined results suggest that the shorter EH side chains modify the out-of-plane packing environment and facilitate vertical electron transport. These results establish a structure-property relationship between side-chain structure, molecular order, exciton coupling and vertical mobility, providing a molecular design basis for optimising organic semiconductors through side-chain engineering.

papers.title: Material criteria for angular-momentum transfer from twisted photons to photoelectrons
papers.summary: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an $n$-type semiconductor surface. Within a single-valley effective-mass model of surface photoemission, we calculate OAM-resolved spectra for GaAs, InSb, $\mathrm{InAs}_{0.34}\mathrm{Sb}_{0.66}$, and $\mathrm{Hg}_{0.76}\mathrm{Cd}_{0.24}\mathrm{Te}$ irradiated by twisted photons with Laguerre--Gaussian--like momentum profile. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. Efficient transfer requires the transverse momentum of the conduction electron to be much smaller than the transverse momentum width of the photon, which favors low temperatures, small conduction-band effective masses, and shallow donor levels. GaAs is less favorable within the present model because of its larger effective mass and deeper donor levels. We also discuss the demanding photon-wave packet parameters, possible extensions to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and post-emission OAM selection. Although the generation of vortex electrons with a vanishing OAM uncertainty via photoemission seems challenging, we argue that it is still possible to generate single-electron vortex states with a finite OAM dispersion.

papers.title: Cooperative Dual-Template Assembly of Bimodal Interconnected Mesoporous Carbon Nanospheres with Boosted Charge Transport
papers.summary: Abstract Mesoporous materials have attracted great research attention since their first advent in 1990s; however, the self-assembly of soft micelles can generate only unary periodicity. A feasible strategy capable of building multinary pore structures remains scarcely explored due to huge synthetic difficulty. Herein, we explore a cooperative dual-template assembly route, which allows for compatible interaction of Pluronic P123 and L64 in solution, to successfully construct a type of mesoporous carbon nanospheres with bimodal mesopores. The key to such construction of hierarchical mesopores from a pure soft-template process without recruitment of a hard template mainly relies on the formation of composite micelles with both suitable mutual interactions and individually stabilized condensed states. The resultant mesoporous carbon spheres possess good uniformity in morphology and mesoporosity, including a mean particle size at ∼200 nm, a high surface area of 537 m2 g–1, and an interconnected bimodal mesopore size centered at 11.1 and 4.2 nm along with a massive amount of micropores. Moreover, this dual-template assembly strategy allows for precise structural regulation over the pore curvature and pore size through tailoring the reaction conditions. As a proof of concept, the fabricated bimodal mesoporous carbon, as an ammonium-ion battery anode, showcases excellent electrochemical performances owing to its permeable and gradient porous structure for fast mass and charge transfer. Our study underscores a facile and extendable toolbox for synthesizing complex or hierarchical mesostructures as advanced energy model materials.

papers.title: Two‐Dimensional Few‐Layer Selenides: From Materials to Applications
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) few‐layer selenides attract much attention due to their unique electronic structures and layer‐dependent properties, which differ markedly from those of bulk layered selenides. Especially some transition metal diselenides, which undergo a transition from an indirect bandgap to a direct bandgap with reduced layer number, can meet the specific requirements of high‐performance optoelectronic devices. However, the stable, controllable, and large‐scale synthesis of few‐layer selenides remains a key bottleneck limiting their development. Furthermore, employing strategies such as edge engineering, heterostructure construction, and phase engineering to regulate their properties is equally important for maximizing their application value. Herein, the structural characteristics and layer‐dependent properties of various 2D few‐layer selenides are systematically introduced. Both top‐down and bottom‐up synthesis methods are emphasized. The relationship between the properties of 2D few‐layer selenides and their applications in energy storage, electronics, optoelectronics, thermoelectricity, and catalysis is revealed. Recent developments and potential directions for future research are discussed. This comprehensive review is expected to advance theoretical research on 2D few‐layer selenides and provide insightful guidance for their future functionalization and large‐scale applications.

papers.title: Electrolyte-pore interface architecture for high performance activated carbon supercapacitors
papers.summary: Redox-additive electric double-layer supercapacitors (EDLCs) were fabricated using phytagel-derived activated carbon (PhAC) electrodes and a cellulose acetate/EMImTFSI/KI redox biopolymer electrolyte. Activated carbons were synthesized via ZnCl₂-assisted chemical activation with varied precursor-to-activator ratios to tailor pore structure and surface area. The assembled symmetric cells (1 × 1 cm²) were systematically evaluated by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), cyclic voltammetry (CV), and galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD) in a two-electrode configuration, and the impact of redox additive, polymer electrolyte, and pore size of activated carbons is discussed. The incorporation of KI enabled reversible redox reactions at the electrode–electrolyte interface, providing additional pseudocapacitance beyond conventional double-layer charge storage. Among all devices, the PhAC-1–based supercapacitor exhibited the best overall performance due to its balanced micro/mesoporous architecture, delivering a high single-electrode-normalized specific capacitance of ~ 215 F g -1 at a current density of 0.5 A g -1 , together with a device-level energy density of ~ 7.47 Wh kg -1 and an effective power density of ~ 205 W kg -1 . Comparative studies with non-redox cells showed that the redox-additive electrolyte enhanced charge storage, although its effects on series resistance, relaxation dynamics, and effective power density depended on the electrode material and cell configuration. The PhAC-1-based redox supercapacitor exhibited nearly a fourfold enhancement in specific capacitance and energy density compared to its non-redox counterpart, while exhibiting a different effective power-density response due to the redox-mediated discharge behaviour. Cycling tests over 5000 cycles at 0.5 A g⁻¹ revealed an initial capacitance loss of approximately 48% in Cell#2 R (PhAC-based redox cell), followed by comparatively stable cycling with 95–98% Coulombic efficiency. These results demonstrate an effective strategy to improve EDLC energy density using sustainable porous carbons and redox-active polymer electrolytes.

papers.title: Deciphering Crystal Structure‐Lithium Storage Behaviors in Niobium Tungsten Oxides Toward High‐Power Lithium‐Ion Capacitors
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion capacitors (LICs) bridge the gap between batteries and supercapacitors, offering high energy/power density and long cycle life. However, their practical performance is limited by the scarcity of battery‐type anodes combining fast lithium‐storage kinetics with structural robustness, and by the difficulty of matching such anodes with capacitive cathodes of comparable rate capability. Here, a family of niobium tungsten oxides with distinct crystal structures, Wadsley–Roth phases (Nb 12 WO 33 , Nb 14 W 3 O 44 , and Nb 16 W 5 O 55 ) and a tungsten‐bronze phase (Nb 18 W 16 O 93 ), are systematically evaluated as high‐rate anodes. Their open frameworks endow high lithium intercalation potentials (1.57–1.67 V vs. Li/Li + ) and excellent rate capability. Among these, Nb 16 W 5 O 55 exhibits the lowest lithium‐ion migration energy barrier (0.15 eV), reflecting superior lithium‐storage kinetics. Pairing Nb 16 W 5 O 55 with capacitive carbon cathodes yields high‐performance LICs in both aqueous and organic systems: the aqueous Nb 16 W 5 O 55 //APDC device delivers 62.8 Wh kg −1 at 3.3 kW kg −1 , while the optimized organic Nb 16 W 5 O 55 ‐CNT//GO device operates over 0.01–3.7 V, achieving an ultrahigh energy density of 300.6 Wh kg −1 and a maximum power density of 33.3 kW kg −1 , with excellent rate capability and cycling stability. This work elucidates the structure–kinetics relationship governing fast lithium storage in niobium tungsten oxides and offers a strategy for next‐generation high‐energy, high‐power LICs.

papers.title: Interface-Engineered Proton-Gated Oxide Transistors with Multitimescale Synaptic Plasticity
papers.summary: Abstract Ion-gated transistors that mimic biological synapses are essential for energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware capable of adaptive learning and sensory processing. However, achieving both high-speed operation and stable memory in silicon-compatible platforms remains challenging due to the trade-off between ionic mobility and retention characteristics. In this work, we developed proton-gated synaptic transistors composed of an electron-beam (EB)-deposited SiO2 electrolyte and a sputtered WO3 channel. A low film density with the oxygen deficiency of EB-deposited SiO2 enables gate-controlled proton intercalation and deintercalation, producing versatile synaptic plasticity of continuously modulating the WO3 channel conductance. The devices exhibit a wide time response range (pulse widths from 100 ms to 50 μs) and a large dynamic range (>103) with a retention time of ∼18 s, successfully emulating short-term plasticity and nociceptor-like sensory behaviors such as threshold spiking, relaxation, and sensitization. They also achieve ∼90% image recognition accuracy and a low power consumption of ∼200 fJ for a single synaptic event. Furthermore, an introduction of a thin Al2O3 layer between the electrolyte and channel effectively suppresses proton back-diffusion, extending the retention time to ∼860 s. This also results in high recognition accuracy across a wide range of pulse widths, from subseconds to submilliseconds. By integrating two transistors with different retention times into a “one-transistor–one-synapse” architecture, we further demonstrated hardware-level temporal control of synaptic plasticity that enables event-driven learning, forgetting, and memory without altering input stimuli. These results indicate that all-oxide proton-gated transistors incorporating interface engineering provide a neuromorphic platform that enables highly flexible designs with excellent synaptic characteristics.

papers.title: Nickel‐Assisted Graphitization of Bimetallic ZIF‐Derived N‐Doped Carbon/Glucose Dual Coatings on TiO 2 Hollow Spheres for High‐Rate Lithium‐Ion Storage
papers.summary: Overcoming the slow reaction rate of TiO 2 anodes is crucial for achieving high‐rate lithium storage. In this study, we designed a hollow TiO 2 spherical anode with dual‐carbon coating and Ni doping to address the low electrical conductivity and slow Li + diffusion of TiO 2 . Ultrathin titanate nanosheets were assembled onto a polymer template, coated with a bimetallic Zn/Ni zeolitic imidazolate framework and glucose, and then pyrolyzed to obtain TiO 2 /ZnNi–NC/C hollow spheres. This structure features a grain boundary‐rich mixed‐phase TiO 2 framework, with an inner (N‐doped) and an outer (glucose‐derived) carbon layer. Ni incorporation is associated with increased carbon ordering, consistent with a proposed role in improving electronic connectivity within the carbon framework. The TiO 2 /ZnNi–NC/C‐HS material exhibits high reversible capacity and excellent rate performance, maintaining a higher capacity than TiO 2 ‐HS at 1 A g −1 and exhibiting a capacity retention of >99% over 1000 cycles. Control experiments confirmed that both nickel doping and the double carbon layer play important roles in the performance enhancement, and their synergistic effect enables fast and stable lithium storage within TiO 2 . Hence, this study highlights the potential of combining MOF‐derived architectures with metal‐catalyzed carbon matrices to develop next‐generation lithium‐ion battery anodes that simultaneously deliver high capacity and high‐power performance.

papers.title: “‐NH‐” Homologation Driven Self‐Exfoliated Bipolar Covalent Organic Nanosheet as Dual‐Ion Binding Anode for High‐Performance Aqueous Zinc‐Based Dual‐Ion Battery
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) offer safe, low‐cost, and sustainable alternatives to lithium‐ion systems. However, dendritic Zn growth downgrades Coulombic efficiency and cycling stability, limiting their practical deployment. Replacing Zn‐metal anodes with reversible organic anodes capable of efficient Zn 2+ storage with average discharge voltage below 0.6 V (vs Zn/Zn 2+ ) is superior yet challenging. Herein, we report a self‐exfoliated bipolar few‐layer polyimide‐based covalent organic nanosheet ( tht ‐NDA‐PI‐CON ) as anode, synthesized via solvent‐free organic flux route using “‐NH‐” homologation strategy, which promotes self‐exfoliation by introducing structural flexibility while simultaneously generating electron‐rich sp 3 ‐NH centres, acting as electronic buffer in between carbonyl and triazine units constructing a bipolar framework, enabling low‐energy barrier dual‐ion binding kinetics. The porous nanosheet, enriched with redox centres delivers 185 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 (84.6% contributes from single discharge plateau), high‐rate capability (78.6% retention/5 A g −1 ), and 81% capacity retention over 5000 cycles. Ex situ analyses and first‐principles calculations reveal Zn 2+ coordination with carbonyl and triazine sites during discharge, while SO 4 2− is stabilized by homologated ‐NH‐ unit upon charging. When paired with MnO 2 , full cell delivers record energy density of 82.73 Wh kg −1 with 84.8% capacity retention over 3000 cycles, demonstrating its potential for next‐generation Zn‐based dual‐ion battery technologies.

papers.title: Phase-change thermal energy storage: Materials, thermophysics and emerging applications
papers.summary: Abstract Phase change materials (PCMs) can reversibly store and release considerable thermal energy through nearly isothermal and isometric phase state transitions, thus have attracted broad attention in energy decarbonization, passive thermal management, and emerging fields such as medicine and intelligent robots. However, critical challenges at material, device, and system levels remain to be addressed. These include the development of pure or composite PCMs with superior thermophysical properties, the design of effective latent heat storage devices, and the optimization of system integration. This review provides a comprehensive overview of phase change thermal storage, beginning with the mechanisms underlying the regulation of PCMs’ thermophysical properties. We summarize recent advances in the physical and chemical modification of PCMs by molecular engineering, multi-component doping, and rational design of composite microstructure and morphology to improve thermodynamic and heat-transfer performance. We then highlight advanced latent heat storage device design using passive and active strategies for increasing both energy and power density, and outline PCM-integrated systems across multifunctional applications including energy harvesting and storage, thermal management, medical treatment, intelligent machine, and catalysis. Finally, we discuss future research directions towards next-generation PCMs, high-performance devices and intelligent system integration.

papers.title: Engineering the Interface between Sodium Metal and Inorganic Solid Electrolytes in Solid-State Batteries: From Interfacial Challenges to Functionalization Strategies
papers.summary: Abstract Solid-state sodium batteries (Na-SSBs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation energy storage systems owing to the natural abundance and low cost of sodium, as well as the potential to utilize high-capacity sodium metal anodes. However, the practical implementation of Na metal in combination with inorganic solid electrolytes remains limited by severe interfacial challenges, including chemical and electrochemical instability, as well as poor interfacial contact resulting in void evolution and dendrite growth during cycling. These phenomena lead to increased interfacial resistance, non-uniform sodium deposition, and rapid performance degradation. In this review, we discuss the fundamental interfacial processes occurring between sodium metal and the major classes of inorganic solid electrolytes, including β-alumina solid electrolytes (BASE), NASICON-type oxides, sulfides, complex hydrides, and halide-based electrolytes. Particular emphasis is placed on the origins of interfacial instability, including thermodynamic incompatibility, mixed conducting interphase formation, chemo-mechanical degradation, and wetting limitations. Furthermore, recent interface engineering and surface functionalization strategies are summarized, including metallic and ceramic coatings, artificial interphases, alloy interlayers, carbon-based modifications, polymeric interlayers, and composite sodium anodes. By correlating electrolyte chemistry, interfacial phenomena, and surface engineering strategies, this review provides perspectives for the rational design of stable sodium metal interfaces toward powerful Na-SSBs.

papers.title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries
papers.summary: The I-/I0/I+ redox chemistry is hindered by the inherent instability of the electrophilic I+, which undergoes hydrolysis in aqueous media or is rapidly consumed by comproportionation with triiodide ions. Here, we design a copper single-atom embedded nitrogen-doped carbon host that synergistically combines d-p orbital hybridization and local low-concentration chloride ions to stabilize the I+. The atomic Cu-Nx sites interact moderately with iodine species through Cu d- and I p-orbital hybridization, which enhances iodine species adsorption, accelerates redox kinetics, and increases the hydrolysis energy barrier of I+. Simultaneously, the Cu-Nx sites promote a localized I-Cl microenvironment through electrostatic interaction, enabling efficient I0/I+ conversion even in a low-concentration Cl- ion electrolyte. As a result, the assembled zinc | |iodine battery exhibits a distinct four-electron dual-voltage plateau, achieving a high capacity of ~408 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1. Even at a high specific current of 10 A g−1, the cell exhibits a high initial capacity of ~251 mAh g−1 and maintains a capacity retention of 70% with a low decay rate of 0.0062‰ per cycle over 50,000 cycles. This work provides a rational design method for coupling single-atom catalysis with localized ion confinement to realize high-voltage and long-life iodine conversion chemistry. Aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries suffer from irreversible iodine conversion and hydrolysis. Here, the authors design a copper single-atom porous carbon host that enables reversible four-electron I⁻/I⁰/I⁺ conversion for stable cycling.

papers.title: Recent progress of the exchange bias based on 2D van der Waals ferromagnet
papers.summary: Abstract Exchange bias (EB) is a central mechanism in spintronics, enabling unidirectional magnetic anisotropy, enhanced coercivity, and stable pinned magnetic states through interfacial exchange coupling. Two‐dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnets offer a new platform for engineering EB at the atomic scale, where sharp interfaces, reduced dimensionality, tunable interlayer coupling, and strong magnetic anisotropy give rise to unconventional interfacial spin phenomena. This review summarizes the recent progress in EB in 2D vdW magnetic heterostructures. We discuss the fundamental principles, key parameters, and theoretical models of EB followed by representative vdW systems based primarily on ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic materials. Particular attention is given to interfacial mechanisms including uncompensated spins, oxidation‐induced pinning, charge transfer, magnetic proximity effects, and spin–orbit coupling. We further examine external control strategies such as electric‐field tuning, thermal modulation, optical excitation, and strain engineering, as well as emerging applications in field‐free spin–orbit‐torque switching, magnetic tunnel junctions, spin‐filter devices, and nonvolatile memories. Finally, we outline the key challenges of thermal stability, interface reproducibility, and scalable fabrication. This review provides a compact framework for understanding and designing EB in 2D vdW heterostructures for future spintronic and quantum‐enabled technologies.

papers.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
papers.summary: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. It is not mentioned in well-known condensed-matter textbook. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.

papers.title: Chiroptical Valleytronic in SnSe
papers.summary: Quantum geometric properties of Bloch electrons play a central role in governing light-matter interactions and transport phenomena in solids. Here, we report quantum-geometric chiroptical selection rules that generate a helicity-dependent momentum-space population imbalance in the group-IV monochalcogenide SnSe. By combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with ab initio real-time simulations of photoexcited carrier dynamics, we identify valley-selective excitation at opposite crystal momenta arising from the breaking of time-reversal symmetry under circularly polarized illumination. We theoretically demonstrate that the magnitude of valley circular dichroism is strongly constrained by crystal symmetry through its influence on the quantum geometric tensor, the key quantity underlying valley optical selection rules. The resulting chiroptically induced valley polarization decays on sub-picosecond timescales through intervalley scattering mediated by electron-phonon coupling. Furthermore, we show theoretically that the population imbalance between valleys at opposite momenta gives rise to a helicity-reversible transient photocurrent. These findings provide microscopic insight into how quantum geometry governs valley-selective light-matter interactions, valley polarization, and photocurrent generation in van der Waals materials exhibiting hidden and transient symmetry breaking.

papers.title: Thermal expansion mechanisms, heat transport, and band-gap renormalization in strongly anharmonic Rb$_2$SO$_4$, Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$ from machine-learned interatomic potentials
papers.summary: Rb$_2$SO$_4$, Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$ are structurally complex materials whose thermal expansion has been interpreted, on the basis of high-temperature x-ray diffraction, in terms of specific polyhedral rearrangements. We study their lattice dynamics and its consequences for thermal and electronic properties using molecular dynamics with actively learned moment tensor potentials trained on density-functional theory data. The anharmonicity measure $σ^A$ (compares the anharmonic contribution to the interatomic forces with the total forces acting on atoms) reaches $\approx$0.3-0.5 for $β$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$, Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$ and $\approx$0.75 for orientationally disordered $α$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$, and the imaginary harmonic modes of Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ and $α$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$ are stabilized at finite temperature. The simulations reproduce the measured thermal expansion and support the mechanisms proposed from diffraction: expansion along $c$ in $β$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$ arises from both elongation and straightening of corrugated Rb chains, BO$_3$ reorientation accompanies the anisotropic expansion of Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$, and bending of polyhedral linkages limits expansion along the weakly expanding directions and in cubic Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$. Green-Kubo lattice thermal conductivities differ by more than an order of magnitude between compounds with comparable $σ^A$, showing that the anharmonicity measure alone does not determine heat transport. Phonon-induced band-gap renormalization, including lattice thermal expansion, reaches 2.7 and 1.7 eV at 1250 K in Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$ and 1.4 eV at 650 K in $β$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$, with zero-point renormalizations of 0.64, 0.70, and 0.31 eV for $β$-Rb$_2$SO$_4$, Rb$_2$Ca$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$, and Ba$_3$Lu(BO$_3$)$_3$, respectively.

papers.title: From stretchable materials and functional fibers to intelligent textile sensing systems
papers.summary: Abstract Wearable sensors that offer significant adaptability and comfort demonstrate substantial potential for discrete, seamless integration into garments, enabling diverse applications for remote monitoring. The transformation of rigid electronic devices into flexible and stretchable sensors, achieved by integrating conductive materials with compliant dielectrics, has enabled the development of robust sensors. However, several factors must be addressed to enable widespread adoption, including garment integration, wireless communication, data pipelines, signal processing, multimodal fusion, privacy and security concerns. Addressing these challenges is essential for establishing the technological and social infrastructure necessary for the widespread adoption of wearable technologies. This review highlights innovations in material and mechanical design strategies that have shaped the current landscape of wearables, and points out some remaining challenges.

papers.title: Decoding Composition-Structure-Performance Relations in Sodium Layered Oxide Positive Electrode Materials
papers.summary: Layered sodium transition-metal (TM) oxides, Na$_x$TMO$_2$, are among the most promising sodium-ion positive electrode materials, yet their Na/vacancy orderings, layer stacking sequences, and cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions are known only for a few single-TM compounds. We compile the Na/vacancy orderings reported in earlier studies into a single library of 41 unique orderings and apply this uniformly to five single-TM and all ten Na$_x$TM$_{0.5}$TM$'_{0.5}$O$_2$ oxides (TM = Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni), screening more than 120,000 structures with machine-learning interatomic potentials prior to 1,025 accurate first-principles calculations. The phase diagrams explain the observed O3/P3/O1 sequences and voltages, and the O3-to-P3 competition hinges on ordering energies of a few meV per atom that scalar descriptors, such as the cationic potential and the interlayer-slab distance, miss. Our extensive analysis reveals that the redox couples form a nearly partner-independent ladder, Ti$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Mn$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Co$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Ni$^{2+/3+}$ $<$ Fe$^{3+/4+}$, explaining pristine charge transfer and the oxidation sequence. Van Vleck analysis of every TMO$_6$ octahedron reveals that TM mixing suppresses the cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions of Mn$^{3+}$ and Ni$^{3+}$ through charge transfer to Jahn--Teller-inactive states or dilution of Jahn--Teller-active centers. We formulate an energy-density-versus-strain map that yields a design rule: a high-voltage couple without Jahn--Teller strain, which Mn$^{4+}$/Ni$^{2+}$ charge transfer realizes in Na$_x$Mn$_{0.5}$Ni$_{0.5}$O$_2$, the most practical composition. We release the ordering-resolved dataset as a training set for subsequent training of accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials.

papers.title: Nonlinear and Chaotic Dynamics of Two Dipolar-Coupled Anisotropic Spins under Periodic Excitation
papers.summary: We investigate the non-linear magnetization dynamics of two identical anisotropic macrospins coupled by dipolar interaction and subjected to periodic transverse excitation. The coupled Landau- Lifshitz-Gilbert equations are solved numerically using a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. By combining bifurcation diagrams, local-maxima analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and two-dimensional stability maps, we characterize how dipolar coupling, transverse driving amplitudes, and uniaxial anisotropy govern the long-time dynamics. The results reveal a non-monotonic reorganization of dynamical regimes, with alternating intervals of enhanced and suppressed instability. Analysis of symmetric and antisymmetric coordinates distinguishes the collective and relative spin responses, while Fourier spectra and three-dimensional trajectories provide complementary frequency-domain and geometrical characterizations. Simultaneous positivity of the two largest Lyapunov exponents identifies parameter regions consistent with hyperchaotic dynamics. Finally, analytical linearization and ferromagnetic-resonance calculations reveal the distinct coupling dependence of the collectivemode frequencies and clarify the limitations of the linearized description beyond the stability thresholds of the collinear reference state. These findings establish a unified framework for understanding the interplay of dipolar coupling, anisotropy, and periodic excitation in the non-linear dynamics of a minimal interacting-spin system.

papers.title: Vanadium Oxide–Modified Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries: A Review
papers.summary: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are gaining traction as a safe, low‑cost alternative to lithium‑based systems, not least because of their high ionic conductivity. Among the candidate cathode materials, vanadium oxides stand out for their layered/open frameworks, multiple valence states, and high theoretical capacities—V₂O₅ in particular offers a combination of facile synthesis and a two‑electron redox chemistry that gives a respectable 589 mAh·g⁻¹. In practice, though, its poor electronic conductivity, sluggish Zn²⁺ diffusion, structural degradation upon repeated cycling, and active‑material dissolution remain serious bottlenecks. This review summarizes the four main classes of AZIB cathodes and the three prevailing energy‑storage mechanisms, then focuses on recent modification strategies for V₂O₅—namely, preparation routes, Li⁺‑storage/deintercalation behavior, morphology engineering, and conductive composite design—and discusses how each strategy improves electrochemical performance. Despite these advances, long‑term structural stability and rate capability at high current densities still fall short of practical requirements. The aim here is to offer a reference for developing better vanadium‑based cathodes in the future.

papers.title: Higher-order Angular Momentum Transport of Alteraxial Phonons in 2D Magnets
papers.summary: The coupling between lattice vibrations and magnetic order in two-dimensional (2D) magnets gives rise to a variety of physical phenomena, among which magnetic effects of axial phonons carrying phonon angular momentum (PAM) have attracted considerable interest. However, a systematic classification of axial phonons in 2D magnets that covers their multipolar patterns and the resulting transport manifestations remains largely unexplored. Here, based on symmetry analysis, we classify all 2D magnetic point groups by their long-wavelength PAM wave patterns. Beyond the s-wave axial phonon, we identify alteraxial phonons with p-, d-, f-, g-, and i-wave multipolar textures, characterized by 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 zero-PAM nodal lines, respectively. We then develop a theory of nonlinear PAM transport driven by a temperature gradient and derive two selection rules: a parity selection rule that determines whether the response occurs at even or odd orders, and an angular-harmonic selection rule that fixes the lowest allowed order for each wave pattern. The multipolar PAM patterns and selection rules are exemplified by two effective lattice models realizing f-wave and d-wave PAM patterns, respectivley. The angular dependence of the nonlinear PAM current reflects the underlying multipolar PAM texture, offering a signature for experiments. Our results establish a symmetry-guided framework for detecting and utilizing higher-order PAM textures in 2D magnets.

papers.title: Nanobiosensors at the Frontier: A Comprehensive Review on the Design, Digital Integration, and Clinical Applications for Next‐Generation Precision Diagnostics
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Recent progress in nanotechnology and biosensing is driving the development of advanced diagnostic tools for precision medicine. This review provides a systematic summary and critical analysis of intelligent nanobiosensors, which integrate engineered nanomaterials with biological recognition components and advanced signal‐transduction mechanisms. Key design paradigms, classification frameworks, and the role of diverse nanomaterials (e.g., metallic, carbon‐based, magnetic, and hybrid structures) are discussed in detail. Furthermore, major transduction technologies, including electrochemical, optical, mechanical, thermal, and magnetic platforms, together with clinical translation pathways and integration with artificial intelligence (AI), edge computing, and mobile health technologies, are comprehensively reviewed. Particular emphasis is placed on clinical applications in infectious, oncological, cardiovascular, and neurological diseases, as well as therapeutic monitoring. Key challenges, including scalability, data security, and regulatory barriers, are also critically discussed. Finally, emerging trends such as federated learning, the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), and personalized digital diagnostics are highlighted, providing perspectives on future directions in intelligent biosensing and precision healthcare.

papers.title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
papers.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise. As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasingly important because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing. Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates---close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns---with intrinsic errors suppressed to the $2\times10^{-5}$ level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from $1/f$ flux noise. Using these models, we identify dephasing sweet spots that suppress sensitivity to dephasing noise. We further exploit transmon asymmetry as a design parameter to access distinct noise-resilient operating regimes. These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.

papers.title: Zero-group-velocity modes in textured steel plates: experiments and elastic modeling
papers.summary: Zero-group-velocity (ZGV) resonances are investigated as a non-contact ultrasonic probe of elastic anisotropy in textured steel plates. Directional laser-ultrasonic measurements were performed on 70% cold-rolled Ti-stabilized interstitial-free steel plates in the full-hard and recrystallized condition. Experimental results were compared with predictions based on effective elastic stiffness tensors derived from X-ray diffraction measurements. Classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill estimates and microstructure-resolved finite-element homogenization reproduce the measured angular dependence of the ZGV frequencies well for both states, with the finite-element KUBC/SUBC bounds considerably narrower than the classical Voigt-Reuss bounds. For the full-hard state, agreement with the texture-based model is obtained only after a recovery treatment. This indicates that dislocations present in the full-hard material contribute to its elastic response, an interpretation that is further supported by theoretical estimations. An identifiability analysis shows that the directional ZGV measurements provide access to at least three independently observable combinations of the stiffness tensor components, and concluding suggestions for application in recrystallization monitoring are provided.

papers.title: Microstructural evolution during isothermal tempering of a highly supersaturated metastable austenitic state of a PM high-speed steel
papers.summary: This study investigates the microstructural evolution of the powder metallurgical high-speed steel PM HS 3-3-4 during isothermal holding within the transformation gap between pearlite and bainite formation. The focus is on the mechanism of carbide spheroidization and the proposed formation of a chemically graded carbide rim. The heat treatments were carried out in a quenching dilatometer, enabling precise control of the thermal cycles and isothermal holding conditions. Spatially resolved analytic microscopy techniques, including scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), Auger electron spectroscopy (AES) and atom probe tomography (APT), image analysis and complementary thermodynamic simulations (MatCalc) were used to characterize the carbide evolution. Isothermal holding increased carbide circularity, carbide volume fraction, and hardness, while MatCalc calculations predict a strong thermodynamic driving force for additional carbide precipitation. The analytic techniques revealed a compositional gradient of approximately 15 nm at the carbide-matrix interface in the isothermally treated condition, compared with a sharp transition of only 2-3 nm in the directly quenched state. This nanometer-scale gradient provides strong evidence for epitaxial, interface-controlled carbide growth and the formation of a chemically graded carbide rim. The associated solute depletion of the surrounding austenite provides a plausible explanation for its reduced stability, reflected by an increase in the martensite start temperature. The combined results demonstrate that isothermal holding promotes interfacial chemical reorganization, offering new insights into carbide spheroidization and providing a basis for tailoring carbide morphology and the resulting mechanical properties through heat treatment.

papers.title: Characterizing universal topological phases beyond spatial embedding
papers.summary: Although Hamiltonians govern wave-matter interactions, conventional characterizations of topological phases of matter require more than the Hamiltonian alone, relying on global invariants defined on closed reciprocal-space manifolds or local commutation relations with position operators. This spatial dependence precludes a unique characterization of topological phases on an abstract platform, whose Hamiltonian can be defined independently of its spatial embedding. Here we establish a framework for characterizing universal topological phases, grounded in the invariance of topological features under arbitrary Hamiltonian-preserving deformations. We construct a Hamiltonian-based spatial embedding that groups a system's constituents according to their connectivity. This embedding, which reproduces the results of conventional topological diagnostics in established systems, enables a coherent extension of topological phases to complex networks using the Hamiltonian alone, further highlighting exceptional robustness in small-world networks. Our results reshape the conceptual foundations of topological physics by decoupling topological characterization from prescribed physical platforms.

papers.title: An Electronic‐Geometric Descriptor for Predicting High‐Voltage Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) are promising sodium‐ion battery cathodes owing to their open frameworks, compositional tunability, and high operating voltages. However, the rational design of high‐voltage PBAs is hindered by the lack of physically interpretable descriptors connecting atomic‐scale properties with voltage behavior. Here, we develop an electronic‐geometric coupled descriptor for correlating and predicting voltage plateaus in PBAs. The descriptor combines the p‐band center of the cyano‐ligand N atom, which characterizes the electronic contribution to Na‐N interactions, with a lattice‐response term that describes framework confinement during sodiation. Density functional theory calculations on ordered binary PBAs show that the coupled descriptor improves the correlations with both high‐ and low‐voltage plateaus relative to the electronic descriptor alone, and the predicted trends are consistent with available experimental reports for representative systems. We further apply this descriptor to screen 78 PBA compositions, including ordered binary, multielement‐doped Fe‐based, and high‐entropy PBAs. Eight compositions are predicted to exhibit both high‐ and low‐voltage plateaus above 3.8 V, among which Cu[Fe(CN) 6 ], Ni[Fe(CN) 6 ], and Zn 2 Cu 2 [Fe(CN) 6 ] 4 agree with reported experimental trends, while Zn[Zn(CN) 6 ], Zn[Fe(CN) 6 ], Cu[Mn(CN) 6 ], Cu[Zn(CN) 6 ], and Ni 3 Zn[Fe(CN) 6 ] 4 are proposed as candidates for further experimental validation. This study offers a descriptor‐guided strategy for the discovery of high‐voltage PBA cathodes.

papers.title: Nanocrystalline cubic boron arsenide growth on GaAs(100) by gas source molecular beam epitaxy
papers.summary: Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) is a promising ultrahigh thermal conductivity semiconductor, but its direct synthesis on lattice-mismatched substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of nanocrystalline c-BAs thin films on GaAs(100) substrates using gas source molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals an optimal growth temperature window of 250-400 C to maintain near stoichiometry and suppress severe arsenic loss. Surface and structural characterizations via atomic force microscopy, reflection high-energy electron diffraction, and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction demonstrate a Volmer-Weber 3D island growth mode and a preferential crystallographic alignment with the GaAs substrate. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms a chemically sharp interface without gallium interdiffusion into the c-BAs layer. These findings establish an initial step for the integration of c-BAs into advanced thermal and optoelectronic platforms.

papers.title: Heat-current-induced nonreciprocal phonon damping
papers.summary: Time-reversal symmetry enforces equal equilibrium linewidths for time-reversed phonon modes at opposite wave vectors. Here we show that a steady heat current can produce nonreciprocal anharmonic damping even in centrosymmetric nonmagnetic crystals. The effect arises from nonequilibrium occupations of scattering partners, which change the statistical weights of time-reversed three-phonon channels while their squared matrix elements remain equal. Within the single-mode relaxation-time approximation, we derive a linewidth correction that is linear in the temperature gradient and odd under wave-vector reversal. The response depends on scattering-partner velocities and equilibrium lifetimes and retains signed channel weights absent from the equilibrium linewidth. First-principles calculations for centrosymmetric MgO and diamond yield nonzero, mode-dependent linewidth corrections at selected finite wave vectors, demonstrating the mechanism in both ionic and covalent crystals. Reversing the heat current at fixed local temperature exchanges the broadening and narrowing of paired modes. This current-reversible linewidth contrast provides a spectral signature of occupation feedback, with potential implications for nonlinear phonon transport.

papers.title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
papers.summary: A first-principles-informed multiscale modeling approach is reported for oxide formation during corrosion of zirconium. The present simulations reproduce the columnar corrosion film microstructure and grain size distribution seen in micrographs of oxidized Zr surfaces. This structural feature emerges from a hexagonal ZrO layer adjacent to the $α$-Zr/ZrO$_{2-x}$ interface, which is dynamically stabilized by continuous heterogeneous grain nucleation and grain boundary mass diffusion. This ZrO layer is identified as a significant oxygen diffusion barrier and a potential contributor to sub-parabolic pretransition corrosion kinetics. The simulations also reproduce the undulatory nature of the metal/oxide interface, leading to regions with tensile stress components capable of nucleating cracks, despite the overall state of compressive hydrostatic stress within the oxide film. First principles density functional theory (DFT) computations of fundamental ZrO$_x$ properties were combined with molecular dynamics simulations using a machine-learned potential based on a DFT training set to provide extensive input to an advanced phase field model for oxide formation and its microstructure, as implemented in the new MedeA PhaseField module. The phase field simulations reported herein incorporated computed stoichiometry-dependent thermochemical data, anisotropic elastic properties, interface energies, bulk and grain boundary mass transport processes, multiphase heterogeneous grain nucleation, and strain energy-dependent phase stabilities.

papers.title: Steady-state cooperative emission of interlayer excitons in atomically thin light-emitting diodes
papers.summary: When an ensemble of emitters is confined within an optical wavelength, its radiation can become correlated, leading to cooperative emission. In two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) electron-hole bilayers, strong light-matter coupling enables the formation of interlayer excitons (IXs), long-lived dipolar excitations that provide an ideal setting for emergent collective phenomena. Here, we engineer an atomically thin light-emitting diode (LED) that generates electroluminescence (EL) from electrically injected IXs that are confined near the sample edges by an edge-enhanced fringing electric field. By measuring Hanbury-Brown-Twiss photon-photon correlations, we find pronounced signatures of collective decay in the form of large photon bunching followed by finite delay antibunching and bunching revivals. These emitter correlation signatures disappear when free charge carriers are doped to form a degenerate Fermi sea but are enhanced by the introduction of localized electrons. The results are consistent with a many-body quantum master equation that models the steady-state superradiant photon statistics of incoherently injected IXs. Our work establishes steady-state cooperative emission in a 2D TMD LED as a platform for studying strong light-matter interactions in electrically driven, non-equilibrium phases of Bose-Fermi mixtures.

papers.title: Dramatic pressure-induced slowdown and the soft glassy rheology of water at 2D material interface
papers.summary: The flow of molecularly confined water has attracted considerable interest in recent years. Yet despite their exquisite character, current nanofluidic devices cannot probe molecular water flow beyond the linear-response regime, while nanomechanical force- based approaches have produced markedly inconsistent results. Here, using tuning- fork-based atomic force microscopy, we tackle these limitations by measuring the full linear-to-nonlinear, shear-dependent viscoelastic rheology of molecularly confined water at various two-dimensional material interfaces -- demonstrating pronounced rate effects in water flow response. The observed rheological behaviors are remarkably analogous to that of macroscopic soft glassy yielding materials and fully captured by a non-linear model accounting for the shear-induced acceleration of the dynamics -- a hallmark of disordered supercooled and metastable systems. We further unveil a pronounced pressure-induced slowdown in nanoconfined water dynamics, with relaxation times extending into the microsecond range and marked material dependence. These results reveal non-linear, glassy rheology as a general feature of interfacial water and offer a route to tunable, non-linear nanofluidic elements.

papers.title: Density Saturation and Autocorrelation Characteristics of Interlayer Exciton Ensembles in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ Heterostructures
papers.summary: We investigate interlayer excitons in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterostructures using time-resolved photoluminescence and second-order autocorrelation measurements across a wide range of excitation powers and bath temperatures. By analyzing the photoluminescence amplitude and lifetime of the interlayer exciton state with the lowest emission energy, we extract a corresponding density-temperature diagram. The extracted exciton density exhibits a saturation at approximately $10^{13}$cm$^{-2}$, consistent with values predicted for a Mott transition of interlayer exciton ensembles in van der Waals heterostructures. Moreover, possible interpretations beyond the Mott transition are discussed. We further test whether the density limit is accompanied by a departure from classical photon statistics. The second-order autocorrelation measurements reveal that the photoluminescence maintains an emission characteristic of $g^{(2)}(0) \approx 1$ from low exciton densities up to the maximum reachable density in the investigated exciton ensembles consistent with the lowest-energy exciton ensemble obeying Poissonian statistics.

papers.title: Quantum Fluctuations and Wigner Dynamics of a Carbon Nanotube Oscillator Driven by an Atomic Force Microscope
papers.summary: Suspended carbon nanotubes provide a useful platform for studying controlled nanomechanical motion in regimes where environmental fluctuations, memory effects, and quantum coherence can all influence the dynamics. We model the fundamental flexural mode of a carbon nanotube driven by an atomic force microscope as a harmonic quantum Brownian oscillator subject to a prescribed classical force and coupled linearly to a thermal environment. Starting from the generalized Langevin equation, we formulate the reduced dynamics directly in phase space, where the Wigner function evolves through a Gaussian propagator determined by dissipative linear transport, a deterministic force-induced displacement, and bath-induced fluctuations. For a Drude memory kernel, the retarded response is expressed through the three roots of a characteristic cubic equation. In the classical-noise limit, the three independent entries of the finite-time covariance matrix reduce to explicit finite sums over these response poles, eliminating numerical double-time covariance integration. We extend the construction to the full quantum fluctuation spectrum, obtaining a thermal frequency series representation that retains zero-point and low-temperature fluctuations. For an initial two-packet superposition, we examine interference attenuation and the integrated negative part of the Wigner function, which provides a phase space measure of nonclassicality. These results provide an explicit analytical framework for finite-memory quantum Brownian motion of bound oscillators and a tractable phase space description of driven carbon nanotube dynamics relevant to future quantum state preparation and quantum tomography experiments.

papers.title: An efficient approach to electron-phonon coupling calculations of heterostructures within an all-electron framework
papers.summary: A major challenge in calculating electron-phonon coupling at interfaces from first principles is the prohibitive computational cost due to the large supercells involved. Here, we present an efficient approach, which builds the electron-phonon matrix of weakly bound heterostructures from the properties of the isolated layers. The two key ingredients, the dynamical matrices and the potential response, are constructed in two steps. In the expansion step, these quantities are folded from the unit cells onto the supercell through an exact Fourier mapping. In the addition step, the interatomic force constants and the potential responses of the heterostructure are assembled blockwise from the corresponding quantities of the isolated layers, neglecting the weak interlayer contribution. The method is implemented in the electron-phonon module of the all-electron full-potential code exciting, enabling efficient calculations of the electron-phonon self-energy. We demonstrate the approach for the phonon dispersion and spectral functions of bilayer WSe$_2$ and pyridine/MoS$_2$, in comparison with exact reference calculations.

papers.title: Stacking-Induced Tuning of a Flat-Band Surface State in NbIrTe4
papers.summary: Ternary layered transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) offer high tunability and access to correlated and topological states. However, like the broader family of layered TMDCs, their properties are sensitive to stacking order and interlayer coupling. Here, we investigate the electronic structure and surface states of NbIrTe$_4$, a candidate Weyl semimetal in bulk, and predicted to be a quantum spin Hall insulator in monolayer form. Using scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM), angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), and density-functional theory (DFT), we attribute the strong resonance in tunnelling spectroscopy located approximately 8 meV below the Fermi level to a surface-derived flat band which shows sensitivity to the local stacking order at the surface. In regions where the top layer is laterally shifted, tunnelling spectroscopy instead shows a gap-like feature with intensity near the Fermi level shifted in energy. Combining DFT and quasiparticle interference (QPI) measurements, we find this dramatic change in the spectroscopy in the vicinity of the quasi-1D flat-band surface state becomes dispersive due to a change in the spatial distribution of the density of states in the top two layers. These findings establish NbIrTe$_4$ as a platform where surface band dispersion can be effectively tuned through local structural manipulation.

papers.title: Zeeman Quantum Geometry of the Layer Pseudo-spin
papers.summary: Two-dimensional layers coupled by position-dependent interlayer tunnelling host a layer pseudo-spin whose polarization is a controllable internal degree of freedom. We introduce the quantum geometry of this layer pseudo-spin: a mixed tensor formed from the interband Berry connection and the layer matrix element, which governs the response to an oscillating in-plane electric field. Because the layer pseudo-spin is an Ising-type scalar invariant under threefold rotation, its selection rules differ from those of a pseudovector spin. In a minimal two-band model, the layer-pseudo-spin quantum metric and Zeeman--Berry curvature are nonzero, while their zone integrals vanish. An in-plane drive therefore leaves the spatially averaged polarization unchanged at linear order but imprints a moiré-periodic intracell pattern, directly imageable by layer-resolved tunnelling. For twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayer, we quantify the local dipole modulation and identify the rectified, helicity-odd, and third-harmonic channels through which a net response appears at higher order.

papers.title: A Chiral Superlattice Route to Spin-Split Topological Antiferromagnetism
papers.summary: The interplay between chirality and magnetism is a profound topic, spanning particle physics, condensed matter, chemistry and origin of life. In this paper, we study this interplay in the new antiferromagnet (AFM) UOTe, and we report a chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological phenomena from collinear antiferromagnetism. Pristine UOTe is a collinear AFM without Berry curvature or spin-split bands. However, we identify the spontaneous formation of a chiral superlattice in UOTe, which can be viewed as frozen chiral phonons at finite wave vector. When electrons move through the chiral superlattice, their orbital Bloch wavefunction and quantum geometry are modulated by the strong chiral superlattice potential, generating large Berry curvature in the chiral superlattice, which we detect by the nonlinear Hall effect. At 150 K, the chiral superlattice induced Berry curvature couples to the collinear AFM order, generating a giant anomalous Hall angle ~0.14 abruptly near $T_N$ that is among the largest in bulk magnets. Moreover, our spin Hanle precession measurement shows that the chiral superlattice also generates spin-polarized current from the collinear AFM, a long-standing goal in spintronics. We shed light on the supermodulation formation mechanism based on chemical ion size and physical interlayer-intralayer energy competitions, using which we propose a design principle to discover similar bond-mismatch superlattices, providing a chiral superlattice pathway through real space engineering of quantum geometry.

papers.title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
papers.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.

papers.title: Correcting topographic artifacts in three-dimensional ToF-SIMS: A practical guide from data-only reconstruction to correlative AFM
papers.summary: Three-dimensional time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (3D ToF-SIMS) builds chemical volumes by stacking images acquired between sputter cycles. Standard reconstruction assumes a flat starting surface and a single sputter rate, so samples with topography, or with layers that sputter at different rates, yield distorted interface positions and depth scales. This article is a practical guide to correcting these artifacts. We group the available corrections by the information they need: the SIMS data alone, atomic force microscopy (AFM) topography before and after the profile, or AFM topography also at intermediate stages. All three are applied to a model Pt/TaOx/Ta/Pt/Ti crossbar memristor device measured with in situ SIMS/AFM at ten stages, together with the data preparation they share. Each correction method is evaluated using the known device geometry and the measured surface evolution. The data-only correction requires no additional instrumentation and restores relative topography, but its depth scale depends on nominal layer thicknesses and remains unconstrained below the last calibrated interface. AFM before and after the profile fixes the start and end surfaces but assumes uniform sputtering in between, which fails next to the device, where the surroundings change material during the profile. Multi-stage AFM correction follows these changes and reproduces the structure of the device, at the cost of instrument time and repeated imaging of a partially sputtered surface. A decision flowchart and a checklist help readers choose, validate and report a correction.

papers.title: Atomic identification via the Prandtl-Tomlinson stick-slip mechanism
papers.summary: Distinguishing atomic species is an ongoing challenge in the field of scanning probe microscopy. Typically, atomic force microscopy makes use of electrostatic interactions to perform atomic identification. Here we perform lateral force microscopy (LFM) measurements with a CO terminated tip of a partially oxidized Cu(110) surface and show clear differences between the metal and oxygen sites over a large z-range. This allows for atomic identification on a typical metal oxide. Density functional theory based calculations show that the tip-sample interaction is dominated by short-ranged orbital interactions and that the electrostatic contribution is negligible. At small tip-sample distances, LFM can probe the Prandtl-Tomlinson stick-slip mechanism on the single-atom scale. It is visible as a striking asymmetry in the forward and backward scan directions, experimentally revealing this fundamental model for nanotribology on the single-atom scale.

papers.title: Collective Hall quantization in 3D Chern vector systems
papers.summary: Understanding the three-dimensional (3D) quantum Hall effect, characterized by a Chern vector rather than a single Chern number, has been a central pursuit in topological physics. While quantized Hall transport is established for the special case with one nonzero Chern component, recent realizations of more general Chern-vector states raise a fundamental question: how does such topology protect quantized transport? Here, we predict a distinct 3D quantized Hall effect protected by $\mathbf{C}=(0,m,n)$. For samples with dimensions $L_y$ and $L_z$, global topology enforces collective quantization of $mL_y+nL_z$, despite the fragility of individual edge modes to disorder. This reveals a novel transport regime in which robust quantization emerges as a holistic property of a unified chiral network,rather than of its constituent modes. Crucially, this collective response manifests as a quantized Hall conductance $G_{xy}=\pm(mL_y+nL_z)e^2/h$, with a distinctive dependence on both Chern-vector components and sample dimensions. We propose candidate materials to facilitate experimental observation.

papers.title: Steering of topological criticality in the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain via non-Hermitian substitutional impurities
papers.summary: We investigate the topological phase in a one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain in the presence of a finite concentration of non-Hermitian substitutional impurities. Our primary focus is the discovery of a deterministic mechanism to actively reconfigure the topological phase boundaries by introducing site-dependent, non-reciprocal intracell and intercell hopping amplitudes. Specifically, breaking the internal structural symmetry of the non-reciprocal impurity hoppings induces a targeted macroscopic displacement of the critical point. This mechanism allows for the controlled expansion or compression of the topological phase strictly via local defect asymmetry. We validate this boundary displacement through finite-size scaling analysis. The extracted correlation length critical exponents ($ν\approx 1.455$ and $ν\approx 1.397$ for symmetric and asymmetric configurations, respectively) confirm a disorder-induced departure from the pristine SSH universality class, with the exponent diverging at high defect densities. We also report an impurity-induced real-to-complex spectral transition geometrically characterized by the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect. Ultimately, our results establish how isolated non-Hermitian asymmetries cooperatively interact to deterministically shift macroscopic topological protection.

papers.title: Nanoscale chemical engineering of Ti3C2Tx MXene multilayers through in situ electron beam irradiation in a TEM
papers.summary: Defect engineering in low-dimensional materials is a powerful approach to tailor their structure and chemistry at the atomic scale, with high relevance for tuning physical properties. Here, we apply this strategy to MXenes, one of the largest families of two-dimensional (2D) materials, and demonstrate the use of a highly focused scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) beam for the structural and chemical nanoengineering of titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) multilayers. By adjusting the beam energy, electron dose, and scanning parameters, Ti3C2Tx multilayers were irradiated at 80 and 300 keV and characterized in situ using annular dark-field imaging and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS). The irradiation induces gradual structural and chemical modifications, largely driven by the selective sputtering of atomic species and MXene layers. We identify irradiation conditions that selectively remove Cl or F surface terminations while largely preserving the Ti3C2 framework, whereas other conditions promote preferential carbon removal, in agreement with theoretical predictions. Most notably, electron irradiation drives the migration and accumulation of initially dilute nitrogen impurities within the irradiated regions, leading to the formation of nitrogen-rich titanium carbonitride (Ti3CyNzTx) nanodomains embedded in the Ti3C2Tx multilayers. These laterally patterned carbide/carbonitride architectures constitute in-plane MXene heterostructures with nanometer-scale spatial control. These results demonstrate that electron irradiation can be used to locally tailor MXene composition and create nanoscale architectures beyond those accessible through conventional chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Frustration-Assisted Electrical Switching in $Co_xTaS_2$
papers.summary: Electrical switching in antiferromagnets is commonly described as the action of current-induced torques on a rigid order parameter. In frustrated magnets, however, competing states can create a history-dependent energy landscape in which slow collective dynamics actively participate in electrical reconfiguration. Here, we demonstrate frustration-assisted switching in near-stoichiometric $Co_xTaS_2$, a van der Waals antiferromagnet located at the composition-sensitive boundary between Hall-active and Hall-inactive multi-Q-related magnetic regimes. Although the crystals exhibit no resolved spontaneous Hall response, they retain van Hove singularities near the Fermi level and order antiferromagnetically below $T_N \simeq 31.5 K$. Current pulses write nonvolatile anisotropic resistance states in microstructured devices, with an activation current density nearly an order of magnitude below that reported for the Hall-active lower-intercalation phase. The switching response separates into two temperature-dependent dynamical regimes rather than following a single current threshold. Independent magnetization-aging and post-field-relaxation measurements reveal slow, history-dependent magnetic dynamics, and the relaxation strength closely follows the inverse switching amplitude. These results identify magnetic frustration and glassy dynamics as central ingredients in the electrical reconfiguration of $Co_xTaS_2$, establishing a route to functional switching through a dynamically soft antiferromagnetic landscape.

papers.title: Large exchange bias from coupled antiferromagnetic order and glassy magnetic freezing in $Co_{0.36}NbS_{2}$
papers.summary: Magnetization measurements on single-crystalline $Co_{0.36}NbS_{2}$ reveal antiferromagnetic order near $T_{N} \simeq 26 K$ and a lower-temperature history-dependent magnetic response consistent with glassy freezing of a subset of magnetic moments. After field cooling, $M(H)$ loops exhibit a sizable exchange-bias shift, reaching $|H_{EB}| \simeq 4.4 kOe$ at $1.8 K$ for a $70 kOe$ field-cooling sweep protocol. The training effect, field-sweep and cooling-field protocol dependence, and disappearance of the bias near a blocking temperature $T_{B} \simeq 12 K$, well below $T_{N}$, support an interpretation in which frozen uncompensated moments are exchange-coupled to an antiferromagnetic matrix. These results suggest that antiferromagnetic-glassy-moment coupling may provide a broader route to exchange bias in off-stoichiometric magnetic $NbS_{2}$ intercalates.

papers.title: Atomic-level study of dose-dependent lattice thermal conductivity degradation in irradiated tungsten
papers.summary: Plasma-facing components (PFCs) in future fusion reactors must withstand extreme environments, making tungsten (W) a prime candidate material due to its high thermal conductivity, high melting temperature, low sputtering yield, low tritium absorption. However, neutron irradiation introduces complex nanostructural defects that severely degrade these critical properties. In this work, we use Non-Equilibrium Molecular Dynamics (NEMD) simulations coupled with the Creation Relaxation Algorithm (CRA) to investigate the lattice thermal conductivity (kappa) of W across a wide range of irradiation doses. Systems treated with different doses up to 1.8 canonical displacements per atom (cdpa) were simulated to generate and study diverse defect structures, including vacancies and self-interstitial atom (SIA) clusters. By correlating spatially-resolved temperature gradients with local defect concentrations, we show that even small changes in defect type and distribution significantly affect thermal transport. We employ Machine Learning (ML) models to develop a quantitative relationship between the defect features and the resulting thermal conductivity degradation. The ML analysis identifies vacancy density as the dominant structural factor controlling thermal transport. We found a significant, nonlinear suppression of kappa with increasing defect density. Predictive multi-defect mapping built upon our ML model resolved a step-like degradation transition at a critical vacancy threshold of 0.05 at.%, beyond which phonon scattering completely saturated and capped the maximum relative lattice thermal conductivity degradation at approximately 30 at.%. This integrated simulation and ML approach provides a powerful, predictive framework for quantifying the complex relationship between structure and thermal conductivity in irradiated fusion materials.

papers.title: Phonon-dominated thermal conductivity of a superconducting amorphous MoSi thin film
papers.summary: We use the differential 3ω method to directly measure the temperature dependent thermal conductivity for about 90 nm Mo0.78Si0.22 thin films. The measurements are performed in a closed-cycle cryostat to access the temperature range between 50 K and 300 K. The MoSi thin films are capped with Al2O3 and probed with a Pt wire. The results show that the thermal conductivity does not satisfy the Wiedemann-Franz law. This implies that thermal transport in MoSi is not dominated by electrons but by phonon-like excitations, contrary to what is assumed in many electro-thermal models of superconducting devices. We argue that this property might be related to the weak localization visible in the resistivity as a function of temperature curves of the superconductor.

papers.title: NEP-kappa 2.0: A unified framework for phonon transport and nonequilibrium thermalization with machine-learning interatomic potentials
papers.summary: We present NEP-kappa 2.0, a unified framework that integrates density-functional theory, material-specific machine-learning interatomic potentials, and pretrained force models for advanced phonon calculations.
